# SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION (SRS)

## Drug Discovery Literature Mining System
**Version:** 1.0  
**Project Type:** Final-Year B.Tech IT Project  
**Category:** Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, NLP and Multi-Agent Systems

---

# 1. Project Overview

## 1.1 Project Description

The Drug Discovery Literature Mining System is a local-first, AI-powered multi-agent research platform designed to automate the discovery, extraction, analysis and interpretation of biomedical scientific literature.

The system will retrieve scientific research papers from public literature databases, process their contents using locally running NLP and language models, extract drug-target relationships, analyze supporting evidence, identify potential research gaps and generate structured scientific research reports.

The system must operate without cloud-based LLM inference services.

## 1.2 Problem Statement

Biomedical researchers must manually search, read and compare large numbers of scientific publications to discover drug-target interactions and identify unexplored research opportunities.

This process is time-consuming and makes it difficult to systematically compare findings across multiple publications.

The proposed system aims to automate this workflow through scientific literature mining, biomedical information extraction, evidence analysis and multi-agent coordination.

## 1.3 Project Objectives

1. Automate scientific literature discovery.
2. Download and organize accessible research papers.
3. Extract biomedical entities such as drugs, genes, proteins and diseases.
4. Identify drug-target relationships and their interaction types.
5. Extract supporting evidence from scientific publications.
6. Compare findings across multiple publications.
7. Identify potential research gaps and contradictory findings.
8. Construct interactive drug-target knowledge graphs.
9. Generate research reports with traceable citations.
10. Perform all AI inference and data processing locally.

---

# 2. System Operating Requirements

## 2.1 Development Environment

Development machine:

- Dell Inspiron 15 3511
- Intel Core i5-1135G7
- 16 GB RAM
- Arch Linux
- Hyprland
- OpenCode coding agent

## 2.2 Execution Environment

Target execution machine:

- ASUS TUF Gaming A17
- AMD Ryzen 5 4600
- NVIDIA GTX 1650, 4 GB VRAM
- 16 GB dual-channel RAM
- Windows 11

The application must be portable between both machines.

## 2.3 Internet Requirements

Internet is permitted exclusively for scientific literature acquisition and associated metadata retrieval.

Permitted:
- PubMed E-utilities.
- Europe PMC REST services.
- Optional additional public scientific literature sources.

Not permitted:
- OpenAI API.
- Gemini API.
- Claude API.
- OpenRouter inference API.
- Any cloud-hosted LLM inference.
- Cloud AI processing services.

All AI inference, NLP processing, agent orchestration, database operations and report generation must run locally.

---

# 3. Proposed Technology Stack

The following is the proposed stack. OpenCode must evaluate compatibility and recommend final versions before implementation.

| Frontend | React |
| UI styling | Tailwind CSS |
| Backend | Python + FastAPI |

The system must have CPU-compatible fallbacks.

Do not assume that every model can run on the GTX 1650. Benchmark model compatibility, VRAM consumption and CPU performance before selecting the final models.

---

# 4. User Requirements

## 4.1 User Input

The user should be able to provide:

- Research question.
- Disease or medical condition.
- Drug name (optional).
- Gene or protein name (optional).
- Publication date range.
- Maximum number of papers.
- Research publication types.
- Full-text preference.
- Research analysis preferences.

Example research question:

"Identify potential drug-target relationships associated with Alzheimer's disease and identify underexplored research areas."

The application should also support a simple mode where the user enters only a research question.

## 4.2 Expected Output

The system should generate:

1. Retrieved scientific paper collection.
2. Paper metadata and abstracts.
3. Extracted biomedical entities.
4. Drug-target relationship dataset.
5. Supporting evidence passages.
6. Contradictory evidence.
7. Drug-target knowledge graph.
8. Potential research gaps.
9. Research summaries.
10. Exportable scientific research report.

---

# 5. Functional Requirements

## FR-01: Literature Discovery

The system shall:

- Search PubMed and Europe PMC.
- Construct search queries from user input.
- Retrieve relevant paper metadata.
- Support publication date filtering.
- Support publication-type filtering.
- Remove duplicate papers.
- Store PMID, DOI, title, authors, abstract and publication date.
- Track source database and retrieval date.

## FR-02: Paper Acquisition

The system shall:

- Download available open-access full-text papers.
- Support PDF imports from the user.
- Support TXT and other useful document formats.
- Respect copyright, licensing and access restrictions.
- Identify unavailable or inaccessible full-text papers.
- Maintain original source references.

Paywalled papers must not be bypassed.

## FR-03: Scientific Document Processing

The system shall:

- Extract text from PDF documents.
- Preserve section information where possible.
- Identify abstract, introduction, methods, results and conclusion.
- Split documents into meaningful text chunks.
- Preserve page and section references.
- Handle extraction errors.

## FR-04: Biomedical Entity Recognition

The system shall identify:

- Drug names.
- Protein names.
- Gene names.
- Diseases.
- Biological pathways.
- Relevant biomedical concepts.

The system must normalize recognized entities where possible and preserve original text.

## FR-05: Relationship Extraction

The system shall identify relationships between biomedical entities.

Supported relationship types:

- Inhibits.
- Activates.
- Binds to.
- Regulates.
- Upregulates.
- Downregulates.
- Associated with.
- Other or unknown.

The system must not treat every association as a confirmed direct molecular interaction.

## FR-06: Evidence Extraction

Every extracted relationship must contain:

- Source paper identifier.
- DOI or PMID when available.
- Exact supporting text.
- Paper section.
- Relationship type.
- Extraction method.
- Confidence score.
- Processing timestamp.

The system must preserve contradictory evidence rather than silently selecting one conclusion.

## FR-07: Drug-Target Analysis

The system shall:

- Aggregate relationships across papers.
- Identify frequently reported relationships.
- Compare supporting and contradicting findings.
- Group relationships by disease, drug and protein.
- Distinguish preclinical and clinical evidence where identifiable.

## FR-08: Research Gap Identification

The system shall identify candidate research gaps through:

- Low literature coverage.
- Conflicting findings.
- Limited experimental evidence.
- Missing validation.
- Underexplored drug-target combinations.
- Changes in research trends over time.

Research gaps must be evidence-based.

A missing relationship in the collected papers must never be presented as proof that no research exists globally.

Each gap must include its supporting reasoning, literature coverage and limitations.

## FR-09: Knowledge Graph

The system shall create an interactive graph containing:

- Drug nodes.
- Protein nodes.
- Gene nodes.
- Disease nodes.
- Relationship edges.
- Evidence references.

Users should be able to inspect individual nodes and relationships.

## FR-10: Report Generation

The system shall generate research reports containing:

1. Research question.
2. Search methodology.
3. Literature collection statistics.
4. Identified drugs.
5. Identified proteins and genes.
6. Extracted relationships.
7. Supporting evidence.
8. Contradictory findings.
9. Potential research gaps.
10. Limitations.
11. References.

Supported export formats:

- PDF.
- CSV.
- JSON.

---

# 6. Multi-Agent Architecture

The system should use one research coordinator and five specialized agents.

## Agent 1: Literature Discovery Agent

Responsibilities:

- Interpret research queries.
- Generate search keywords.
- Search supported literature databases.
- Retrieve paper metadata.
- Remove duplicates.
- Organize retrieved papers.

Output: Structured literature collection.

## Agent 2: Biomedical Extraction Agent

Responsibilities:

- Process scientific papers.
- Extract biomedical entities.
- Normalize drug, gene and protein names.
- Identify candidate relationships.
- Preserve supporting text.

Output: Structured biomedical entities and candidate relationships.

## Agent 3: Evidence Analysis Agent

Responsibilities:

- Validate extracted evidence against source passages.
- Compare findings across publications.
- Identify contradictory findings.
- Categorize evidence types.
- Preserve uncertainty.

Output: Evidence matrix.

## Agent 4: Research Gap Agent

Responsibilities:

- Analyze literature coverage.
- Identify underexplored relationships.
- Detect conflicting results.
- Identify evidence limitations.
- Rank potential research gaps using transparent criteria.

Output: Candidate research gaps with explanations and references.

## Agent 5: Research Report Agent

Responsibilities:

- Consolidate findings.
- Generate structured summaries.
- Prepare research reports.
- Include citations.
- Include limitations and confidence information.

Output: Final research report.

## Research Coordinator

The coordinator shall:

- Manage agent execution.
- Pass structured data between agents.
- Track execution status.
- Handle failures.
- Prevent duplicate processing.
- Maintain investigation history.
- Support restarting interrupted workflows.

Agents should be modular. They may share one local LLM while using specialized prompts, tools and deterministic Python processing.

# 8. Non-Functional Requirements

## Performance

- Support batch paper processing.
- Avoid loading unnecessary documents into memory.
- Support CPU-only inference.
- Avoid loading multiple large language models simultaneously.
- Provide progress indicators.

## Reliability

- Handle failed downloads.
- Prevent duplicate records.
- Support interrupted task recovery.
- Log agent errors.
- Preserve source documents.

## Accuracy

- Preserve evidence provenance.
- Provide extraction confidence.
- Distinguish association from direct interaction.
- Preserve contradictory findings.
- Avoid unsupported scientific claims.

## Security

- Process local files securely.
- Do not execute downloaded document content.
- Do not expose the local database externally.
- Validate uploaded files.
- Treat paper contents as untrusted input to prevent prompt injection.

## Portability

- Support Arch Linux development.
- Support Windows 11 execution.
- Avoid machine-specific paths.
- Use configuration files and environment variables.
- Provide reproducible dependency installation.
- Document GPU and CPU execution modes.

# SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION (SRS)

## Drug Discovery Literature Mining System
**Version:** 1.0  
**Project Type:** Final-Year B.Tech IT Project  
**Category:** Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, NLP and Multi-Agent Systems

---

# 1. Project Overview

## 1.1 Project Description

The Drug Discovery Literature Mining System is a local-first, AI-powered multi-agent research platform designed to automate the discovery, extraction, analysis and interpretation of biomedical scientific literature.

The system will retrieve scientific research papers from public literature databases, process their contents using locally running NLP and language models, extract drug-target relationships, analyze supporting evidence, identify potential research gaps and generate structured scientific research reports.

The system must operate without cloud-based LLM inference services.

## 1.2 Problem Statement

Biomedical researchers must manually search, read and compare large numbers of scientific publications to discover drug-target interactions and identify unexplored research opportunities.

This process is time-consuming and makes it difficult to systematically compare findings across multiple publications.

The proposed system aims to automate this workflow through scientific literature mining, biomedical information extraction, evidence analysis and multi-agent coordination.

## 1.3 Project Objectives

1. Automate scientific literature discovery.
2. Download and organize accessible research papers.
3. Extract biomedical entities such as drugs, genes, proteins and diseases.
4. Identify drug-target relationships and their interaction types.
5. Extract supporting evidence from scientific publications.
6. Compare findings across multiple publications.
7. Identify potential research gaps and contradictory findings.
8. Construct interactive drug-target knowledge graphs.
9. Generate research reports with traceable citations.
10. Perform all AI inference and data processing locally.

---

Not permitted:

- Cloud AI processing services.

All AI inference, NLP processing, agent orchestration, database operations and report generation must run locally.

The user should be able to provide:

- Gene or protein name (optional).

- Maximum number of papers.

- Full-text preference.
- Research analysis preferences.

Example research question:

"Identify potential drug-target relationships associated with Alzheimer's disease and identify underexplored research areas."

The application should also support a simple mode where the user enters only a research question.

## 4.2 Expected Output

The system should generate:

1. Retrieved scientific paper collection.
2. Paper metadata and abstracts.
3. Extracted biomedical entities.
4. Drug-target relationship dataset.
5. Supporting evidence passages.
6. Contradictory evidence.
7. Drug-target knowledge graph.
8. Potential research gaps.
9. Research summaries.
10. Exportable scientific research report.

# 5. Functional Requirements

## FR-01: Literature Discovery

The system shall:

- Search PubMed and Europe PMC.
- Construct search queries from user input.
- Retrieve relevant paper metadata.
- Support publication date filtering.
- Support publication-type filtering.
- Remove duplicate papers.
- Store PMID, DOI, title, authors, abstract and publication date.
- Track source database and retrieval date.

## FR-02: Paper Acquisition

The system shall:

- Download available open-access full-text papers.
- Support PDF imports from the user.
- Support TXT and other useful document formats.
- Respect copyright, licensing and access restrictions.
- Identify unavailable or inaccessible full-text papers.
- Maintain original source references.

Paywalled papers must not be bypassed.

## FR-03: Scientific Document Processing

The system shall:

- Extract text from PDF documents.
- Preserve section information where possible.
- Identify abstract, introduction, methods, results and conclusion.
- Split documents into meaningful text chunks.
- Preserve page and section references.
- Handle extraction errors.

## FR-04: Biomedical Entity Recognition

The system shall identify:

- Drug names.
- Protein names.
- Gene names.
- Diseases.
- Biological pathways.
- Relevant biomedical concepts.

The system must normalize recognized entities where possible and preserve original text.

## FR-05: Relationship Extraction

The system shall identify relationships between biomedical entities.

Supported relationship types:

- Inhibits.
- Activates.
- Binds to.
- Regulates.
- Upregulates.
- Downregulates.
- Associated with.
- Other or unknown.

The system must not treat every association as a confirmed direct molecular interaction.

## FR-06: Evidence Extraction

Every extracted relationship must contain:

- Source paper identifier.
- DOI or PMID when available.
- Exact supporting text.
- Paper section.
- Relationship type.
- Extraction method.
- Confidence score.
- Processing timestamp.

The system must preserve contradictory evidence rather than silently selecting one conclusion.

## FR-07: Drug-Target Analysis

The system shall:

- Aggregate relationships across papers.
- Identify frequently reported relationships.
- Compare supporting and contradicting findings.
- Group relationships by disease, drug and protein.
- Distinguish preclinical and clinical evidence where identifiable.

## FR-08: Research Gap Identification

The system shall identify candidate research gaps through:

- Low literature coverage.
- Conflicting findings.
- Limited experimental evidence.
- Missing validation.
- Underexplored drug-target combinations.
- Changes in research trends over time.

Research gaps must be evidence-based.

A missing relationship in the collected papers must never be presented as proof that no research exists globally.

Each gap must include its supporting reasoning, literature coverage and limitations.

## FR-09: Knowledge Graph

The system shall create an interactive graph containing:

- Drug nodes.
- Protein nodes.
- Gene nodes.
- Disease nodes.
- Relationship edges.
- Evidence references.

Users should be able to inspect individual nodes and relationships.

## FR-10: Report Generation

The system shall generate research reports containing:

1. Research question.
2. Search methodology.
3. Literature collection statistics.
4. Identified drugs.
5. Identified proteins and genes.
6. Extracted relationships.
7. Supporting evidence.
8. Contradictory findings.
9. Potential research gaps.
10. Limitations.
11. References.

Supported export formats:

- PDF.
- CSV.
- JSON.

# 6. Multi-Agent Architecture

The system should use one research coordinator and five specialized agents.

## Agent 1: Literature Discovery Agent

Responsibilities:

- Interpret research queries.
- Generate search keywords.
- Search supported literature databases.
- Retrieve paper metadata.
- Remove duplicates.
- Organize retrieved papers.

Output: Structured literature collection.

## Agent 2: Biomedical Extraction Agent

Responsibilities:

- Process scientific papers.
- Extract biomedical entities.
- Normalize drug, gene and protein names.
- Identify candidate relationships.
- Preserve supporting text.

Output: Structured biomedical entities and candidate relationships.

## Agent 3: Evidence Analysis Agent

Responsibilities:

- Validate extracted evidence against source passages.
- Compare findings across publications.
- Identify contradictory findings.
- Categorize evidence types.
- Preserve uncertainty.

Output: Evidence matrix.

## Agent 4: Research Gap Agent

Responsibilities:

- Analyze literature coverage.
- Identify underexplored relationships.
- Detect conflicting results.
- Identify evidence limitations.
- Rank potential research gaps using transparent criteria.

Output: Candidate research gaps with explanations and references.

## Agent 5: Research Report Agent

Responsibilities:

- Consolidate findings.
- Generate structured summaries.
- Prepare research reports.
- Include citations.
- Include limitations and confidence information.

Output: Final research report.

## Research Coordinator

The coordinator shall:

- Manage agent execution.
- Pass structured data between agents.
- Track execution status.
- Handle failures.
- Prevent duplicate processing.
- Maintain investigation history.
- Support restarting interrupted workflows.

Agents should be modular. They may share one local LLM while using specialized prompts, tools and deterministic Python processing.

# SRS Analysis — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0  
**Project Type:** Final-Year B.Tech IT Project  
**Status:** Planning phase — analysis of the provided Software Requirements Specification

---

## 1. Source Document

This document analyses the SRS provided by the project owner (version 1.0). The full SRS text (Sections 1–14) is the authoritative source; this file summarises the requirements, flags missing/ambiguous items, and records recommended revisions before implementation begins.

---

## 2. Requirements Summary

### 2.1 Objectives (1.3)
Ten objectives, all local-first: literature discovery, paper download/organisation, biomedical entity extraction (drugs, genes, proteins, diseases), drug-target relationship extraction, evidence extraction, cross-publication comparison, research-gap and contradiction identification, interactive knowledge graphs, traceable research reports, and 100% local AI inference.

### 2.2 Operating Environments (2.1–2.2)
| Machine | OS | CPU | RAM | GPU/VRAM | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dell Inspiron 15 3511 | Arch Linux (Hyprland) | Intel i5-1135G7 | 16 GB | integrated | Development |
| ASUS TUF Gaming A17 | Windows 11 | AMD Ryzen 5 4600 | 16 GB dual-channel | NVIDIA GTX 1650, 4 GB | Target execution |

Portability between both is required.

### 2.3 Internet Use (2.3)
Permitted: PubMed E-utilities, Europe PMC REST, optional public scientific sources.  
Prohibited: OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, OpenRouter, any cloud-hosted LLM inference or cloud AI processing.

### 2.4 Functional Requirements (FR-01 to FR-10)
- FR-01 Literature Discovery: PubMed + Europe PMC search, query construction, date/type filtering, deduplication, PMID/DOI/title/authors/abstract/date storage, source + retrieval-date tracking.
- FR-02 Paper Acquisition: open-access full-text download, user PDF/TXT import, copyright/licence respect, paywalled-paper identification (must not bypass paywalls), source reference maintenance.
- FR-03 Document Processing: PDF text extraction, section preservation (abstract/intro/methods/results/conclusion), chunking with page/section references, error handling.
- FR-04 Entity Recognition: drugs, proteins, genes, diseases, pathways, concepts; normalisation where possible; preserve original text.
- FR-05 Relationship Extraction: inhibits, activates, binds to, regulates, upregulates, downregulates, associated with, other/unknown. Do not treat every association as a direct molecular interaction.
- FR-06 Evidence Extraction: per-relationship source paper ID, DOI/PMID, exact supporting text, section, relationship type, extraction method, confidence score, timestamp. Preserve contradictory evidence.
- FR-07 Drug-Target Analysis: aggregation across papers, frequency ranking, support/contradiction comparison, grouping by disease/drug/protein, preclinical vs clinical distinction where identifiable.
- FR-08 Research Gap Identification: low coverage, conflicting findings, limited evidence, missing validation, underexplored combinations, trend changes. Gaps must be evidence-based; absence in collected papers != proof of no global research; each gap needs reasoning, coverage, limitations.
- FR-09 Knowledge Graph: drug/protein/gene/disease nodes, relationship edges, evidence references; node/edge inspection.
- FR-10 Report Generation: 11 sections (research question through references). Exports: PDF, CSV, JSON.

### 2.5 Multi-Agent Architecture (Section 6)
One research coordinator + five specialised agents:
1. Literature Discovery Agent
2. Biomedical Extraction Agent
3. Evidence Analysis Agent
4. Research Gap Agent
5. Research Report Agent

Agents may share one local LLM via specialised prompts + deterministic Python processing. Coordinator manages execution, data flow, status tracking, failure handling, duplicate prevention, investigation history, and restart of interrupted workflows.

### 2.6 Database (Section 7)
SQLite. Proposed entities: Papers, Biomedical Entities, Relationships, Evidence, Research Investigations, Research Gaps, Processing History.

### 2.7 Non-Functional Requirements (Section 8)
Batch processing, bounded memory, CPU-only inference, single-model-at-a-time, progress indicators; failed-download handling, duplicate prevention, interrupted-task recovery, error logging, document preservation; provenance, confidence, association-vs-interaction distinction, contradiction preservation, no unsupported claims; secure local file handling, no execution of document content, no external DB exposure, upload validation, prompt-injection treatment of paper text; portability Arch ↔ Windows, config/env vars, reproducible deps, GPU/CPU modes documented.

### 2.8 UI Requirements (Section 9)
React dashboard, 12 views (home, new investigation, search results, paper library, paper detail/evidence viewer, entity explorer, relationship explorer, knowledge graph, gap analysis, report generation, history, settings). Dark theme, scientific dashboard style, responsive, interactive charts (Plotly), minimal animation.

### 2.9 Evaluation & Testing (Section 10)
NLP evaluation (NER/RE precision, recall, F1 on manually annotated dataset), evidence evaluation (source attribution, passage accuracy, citation correctness, contradiction accuracy), gap evaluation via human review (relevance, evidence quality, reasoning transparency, reproducibility, false-gap detection), system evaluation (download reliability, PDF processing, agent coordination, failure recovery, memory, CPU/GPU inference, cross-platform). No accuracy claims without measured results.

### 2.10 Milestones (Section 11)
M0 Requirements & Architecture → M1 Foundation → M2 Literature Acquisition → M3 Scientific NLP → M4 Evidence Analysis → M5 Multi-Agent System → M6 Research Analytics → M7 Frontend & Reporting → M8 Validation & Deployment.

### 2.11 Constraints (Section 12)
Nine constraints, including no cloud LLM, no paid AI APIs, internet only for literature, Ollama/local runtime, local DB/storage, ASUS hardware target, portability, provenance, no clinical-validity claims.

### 2.12 Definition of Completion (Section 13)
Ten completion criteria, ending with documented scientific evaluation results.

---

## 3. Missing, Ambiguous, or Technically Unrealistic Requirements

The following items should be revised or clarified before development:

| # | Area | Issue | Recommended Revision |
|---|------|-------|----------------------|
| A-1 | LLMs / hardware | SRS proposes Ollama + one shared LLM on a GTX 1650 (4 GB VRAM) but does not specify which model(s), context window, or quantisation. 4 GB VRAM is tight for most instruct models. | Add explicit model-selection criteria: candidate models must fit in ≤3 GB VRAM (leaving headroom) or run acceptably on CPU. Require a benchmarking step (M0) before final model lock-in. Do not claim any specific model will work until measured. |
| A-2 | Evidence validation | FR-03/FR-06 require "validate extracted evidence against source passages" but with a local LLM this is inherently probabilistic, not deterministic validation. | Reframe as "cross-check candidate evidence against source passages and flag low-confidence matches"; never present LLM output as ground truth. |
| A-3 | Research gaps | FR-08 says gaps must be "evidence-based" but also that absence in collected papers is not proof of no global research. The system can only identify gaps *relative to the collected corpus*. | State explicitly: gaps are candidate gaps within the retrieved literature, labelled with corpus coverage and limitations. |
| A-4 | Preclinical vs clinical | FR-07 requires distinguishing preclinical vs clinical evidence "where identifiable" but no method is specified. | Define a deterministic heuristic (e.g., section + keyword matching: animal/cell/in vitro vs clinical trial/patient) plus LLM-assisted classification with low confidence when uncertain. |
| A-5 | Full-text availability | FR-02 assumes open-access full-text download is broadly feasible. In practice most PubMed papers are paywalled or abstract-only. | Set expectations: the system processes whatever full text is obtainable (open-access + user imports) and clearly marks papers as metadata-only / abstract-only / full-text. |
| A-6 | Entity normalisation | FR-04 requires normalisation "where possible" with no authority specified. | Specify external identifiers as best-effort (e.g., NCBI Gene, UniProt, DrugBank only when openly accessible via permitted internet); otherwise store original text with normalised_name = NULL. |
| A-7 | LangGraph dependency | Section 6 proposes LangGraph agent orchestration. LangGraph is a Python library; verify it runs on the target hardware and version-pin it. | Add LangGraph to dependency list with CPU-compatible requirement; document fallback to a simple Python state machine if LangGraph proves problematic offline. |
| A-8 | PDF security | Security section says "do not execute downloaded document content" and "treat paper contents as untrusted input". PyMuPDF text extraction is generally safe, but malicious PDFs can trigger parser bugs. | Sandbox PDF extraction (single-process, timeout, size limits), validate file type/magic bytes, scan for embedded scripts/JS before parsing. |
| A-9 | Evaluation dataset | Section 10 requires a manually annotated evaluation dataset but no source or size is specified. | Define: minimum N annotated abstracts/full-texts with gold-standard entities and relationships; source (e.g., a small set of PubMed open-access papers annotated by the project owner). |
| A-10 | Report export | PDF export from a React + Python stack typically requires a library (e.g., ReportLab/WeasyPrint) or browser printing. | Specify the PDF generation approach explicitly (server-side ReportLab/WeasyPrint or client-side jsPDF) and pin the library. |

---

## 4. Requirements Requiring Project-Owner Decision

1. Final local LLM model choice after benchmarking (see MODEL_SELECTION.md).
2. Whether to use LangGraph or a lightweight custom state machine for agent orchestration.
3. Scope of the manually annotated evaluation dataset (size, source papers, who annotates).
4. PDF export library choice (ReportLab/WeasyPrint vs client-side).
5. Whether to integrate any additional literature source beyond PubMed + Europe PMC.
6. Maximum corpus size per investigation (e.g., max papers to download/process) to bound memory and time on the ASUS target.

# System Architecture — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written yet

---

## 1. Architectural Goals

- **Local-first:** all inference, NLP, orchestration, storage, and reporting run on the user's machine. No cloud LLM APIs.
- **Portable:** identical codebase runs on Arch Linux (development) and Windows 11 (target ASUS).
- **Modular:** agents, NLP stages, data sources, and exporters are independently replaceable.
- **Resource-bounded:** designed for 16 GB RAM and a 4 GB VRAM GPU; single model loaded at a time; CPU fallback everywhere.
- **Scientifically sound:** full provenance, confidence scores, contradiction preservation, no unsupported clinical claims.

---

## 2. High-Level Architecture

The system is a **three-tier local application**:

```
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                     TIER 3 — FRONTEND (React)                  |
|  Tailwind CSS dashboard, Plotly charts, file upload, exports   |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                         HTTP / JSON (REST)                     |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|              TIER 2 — BACKEND (Python + FastAPI)               |
|  API routers | Agent coordinator (LangGraph) | 5 agents       |
|  NLP services | DB access (SQLite) | File/storage services     |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                         Local file system                      |
|  SQLite DB | PDFs/TXTs | reports | models (Ollama GGUF)       |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|              TIER 1 — LOCAL RUNTIMES                           |
|  Ollama (local LLM) | Python venv | Node.js (frontend build)  |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Tier responsibilities

- **Frontend (React + Tailwind + Plotly):** user interface, investigation creation, result browsing, knowledge-graph visualisation, report download. Communicates only with the FastAPI backend over HTTP.
- **Backend (FastAPI):** REST API, request validation, job queue, agent orchestration via the research coordinator, NLP service wrappers, database access, file storage, report assembly.
- **Local runtimes:** Ollama serves the local LLM over `http://localhost:11434` (default). The backend calls Ollama's REST API — never a cloud endpoint. Python environment hosts FastAPI, LangGraph (or fallback state machine), SciSpaCy, Transformers, Sentence-Transformers, FAISS, PyMuPDF, NetworkX.

---

## 3. Component Diagram (logical)

```
User input
   |
   v
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
| FastAPI  |---->| Coordinator     |---->| Agent 1: Lit.       |
| API      |     | (LangGraph)     |     | Discovery           |
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
      |                |                      |
      v                v                      v
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
| SQLite   |     | Agent 2: Bio    |---->| Agent 3: Evidence   |
| DB       |     | Extraction      |     | Analysis            |
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
      |                |                      |
      v                v                      v
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
| Ollama   |     | Agent 4: Gap    |---->| Agent 5: Report     |
| (LLM)    |     | Analysis        |     | Generation          |
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
      |
+----------+
| File sys |
| (PDFs,   |
| reports) |
+----------+
```

Agents read from and write to SQLite; the coordinator owns the state machine. LLM calls go through Ollama; deterministic NLP (SciSPaCy, PyMuPDF, NetworkX, FAISS) runs in-process.

---

## 4. Layered Backend Design

| Layer | Responsibility | Key technologies |
|---|---|---|
| API layer | REST endpoints, request/response validation, progress streaming | FastAPI, Pydantic |
| Orchestration layer | Investigation lifecycle, agent sequencing, retries, checkpoints | LangGraph (or custom state machine), SQLite |
| Agent layer | Five specialised agents with prompts + deterministic tools | Ollama client, SciSpaCy, Transformers |
| NLP services | PDF extraction, chunking, NER, relationship extraction, embeddings, vector search | PyMuPDF, SciSpaCy, Sentence-Transformers, FAISS |
| Analytics layer | Knowledge graph, gap ranking, contradiction detection | NetworkX, Plotly (data prep), deterministic Python |
| Data layer | SQLite access, migrations, file storage paths | sqlite3, SQLAlchemy (optional), alembic-like migrations |
| Report layer | PDF/CSV/JSON assembly with citations | ReportLab or WeasyPrint (server-side), Python csv/json |

### Single-model constraint
Only one LLM is loaded/served by Ollama at a time. The backend reuses the same Ollama model for all agents via different prompts. Embedding and NER models are separate, smaller processes; they must not be loaded simultaneously with a large LLM if memory is constrained.

---

## 5. Data Flow (end-to-end, logical)

1. User creates an investigation (research question + parameters) via frontend → API.
2. Coordinator creates investigation record (status: `queued`) and enqueues Agent 1.
3. Agent 1 builds queries, calls PubMed/Europe PMC, deduplicates, stores paper metadata.
4. Coordinator enqueues download/processing for each paper (FR-02, FR-03).
5. Agent 2 processes full text: extract text → chunk → NER → normalise → candidate relationships.
6. Agent 3 validates evidence, compares across papers, flags contradictions, builds evidence matrix.
7. Agent 4 analyses coverage, ranks candidate research gaps with reasoning + limitations.
8. Agent 5 consolidates findings and generates the report (JSON/CSV/PDF).
9. Frontend polls progress; user browses results and exports.

Each stage writes to SQLite and emits progress events. Failed stages can be retried or resumed from the last checkpoint (FR: interrupted task recovery).

---

## 6. Cross-Cutting Design Decisions

### 6.1 No cloud inference
Ollama runs locally. All model files (GGUF) live on the local disk. The backend's Ollama client points at `127.0.0.1:11434` (configurable via env var). No API keys for OpenAI/Gemini/Claude/OpenRouter are accepted or stored.

### 6.2 Database as the integration point
Agents do not call each other directly; they communicate through the shared SQLite state and the coordinator's LangGraph state. This makes each agent independently testable and restartable.

### 6.3 Untrusted document handling
Downloaded PDFs/TXTs are stored outside the web root, validated by magic bytes + size limit before parsing, and treated as untrusted input in prompts (prompt-injection mitigations: system-message isolation, no raw user/paper text reflected back to the user without sanitisation).

### 6.4 Memory management
- Documents are streamed/chunked; full text is not loaded into memory all at once.
- Vector index (FAISS) is built per-investigation and can be discarded after the investigation completes.
- Progress indicators are emitted per paper so the UI remains responsive.

### 6.5 Portability
No machine-specific absolute paths. Storage root is configurable via environment variable (`DDS_DATA_DIR`, default `./data` relative to the executable). SQLite is file-based and portable. Python dependencies pinned in `requirements.txt`; frontend in `package.json`. GPU vs CPU is a configuration flag, not hard-coded.

---

## 7. Architectural Requirements Revisions

- If LangGraph cannot be installed/used offline on Windows 11, replace with a lightweight deterministic Python state machine (same interfaces, no external orchestration dependency).
- PDF export library must be chosen and pinned (see SRS.md item A-10).
- FAISS is optional: if memory is too tight on the ASUS, replace with SQLite full-text search + cosine similarity over NumPy arrays in batches.

# Database Design — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written yet

---

## 1. Design Principles

- **SQLite** as the single local relational database (file-based, portable, no server).
- **Fully normalised** to at least 3NF; junction tables for many-to-many relationships.
- **Provenance-first:** every extracted fact links back to a paper, section, page, and extraction method with a timestamp and confidence score.
- **Contradiction-safe:** relationships and evidence are never soft-deleted or overwritten to "pick a winner"; contradictory rows coexist.
- **Cross-platform:** relative, configurable storage paths; no machine-specific absolute paths.
- **Migratable:** versioned SQL migration files applied at startup.

---

## 2. Entity-Relationship Summary

investigation 1:N processing_history

**processing_history**
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| task_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |

| agent_name | TEXT | NOT NULL | |

| started_at | TEXT | | |
| completed_at | TEXT | | |
| execution_time_seconds | REAL | | |
| error_details | TEXT | | JSON error info |
| retry_count | INTEGER | NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 | |

### 3.2 Indexes

```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_investigation ON papers(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_pmid ON papers(pmid) WHERE pmid IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_doi ON papers(doi) WHERE doi IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_access_status ON papers(access_status);
CREATE INDEX idx_mentions_paper ON paper_entity_mentions(paper_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_mentions_entity ON paper_entity_mentions(entity_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_entities_type ON entities(entity_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_investigation ON relationships(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_entities ON relationships(source_entity_id, target_entity_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_type ON relationships(relationship_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_evidence_relationship ON evidence(relationship_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_evidence_paper ON evidence(paper_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_gaps_investigation ON research_gaps(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_history_investigation ON processing_history(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_history_agent ON processing_history(agent_name);
```

### 3.3 Foreign keys

SQLite `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;` must be enabled on every connection. All FK columns reference the corresponding PK with `ON DELETE CASCADE` only where semantically safe (e.g., `paper_entity_mentions` → `papers`); `evidence` → `relationships` uses `ON DELETE CASCADE`; investigations → gaps uses `ON DELETE CASCADE`.

---

## 4. Migration Strategy

- Migrations are versioned SQL files in `db/migrations/` named `V001__initial_schema.sql`, `V002__...`, etc.
- A `schema_version` table tracks the applied version:
  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL);
  ```
- On startup, the backend applies pending migrations in order within a single transaction.
- Rollbacks are not automated; destructive migrations require a backup copy of the SQLite file first.
- No ORM-migration magic (e.g., Alembic) is required; raw SQL keeps the dependency surface small and auditable.

---

## 5. Data Retention & Portability

- The SQLite file and the `data/` storage root are relocatable; paths are relative to a configurable `DDS_DATA_DIR`.
- Backups = copy the SQLite file + data folder (file-level copy is safe when the app is stopped).
- No cloud sync of the database; it never leaves the local machine.

---

## 6. Schema Gaps to Confirm

- Whether `authors` should be normalised into a separate `authors` table (many-to-many with papers) — deferred; JSON array is acceptable for v1.
- Whether `external_identifier` lookups are required at all, given the "permitted internet" restriction and possible rate limits — marked nullable/best-effort.

# SRS Analysis — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Project Type:** Final-Year B.Tech IT Project  
**Status:** Planning phase — analysis of the provided Software Requirements Specification

---

## 1. Source Document

This document analyses the SRS provided by the project owner (version 1.0). The full SRS text (Sections 1–14) is the authoritative source; this file summarises the requirements, flags missing/ambiguous items, and records recommended revisions before implementation begins.

---

## 2. Requirements Summary

### 2.1 Objectives (Section 1.3)
Ten objectives, all local-first: literature discovery; paper download/organisation; biomedical entity extraction (drugs, genes, proteins, diseases); drug-target relationship extraction; evidence extraction; cross-publication comparison; research-gap and contradiction identification; interactive knowledge graphs; traceable research reports; 100% local AI inference.

### 2.2 Operating Environments (Sections 2.1–2.2)

| Machine | OS | CPU | RAM | GPU/VRAM | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dell Inspiron 15 3511 | Arch Linux (Hyprland) | Intel i5-1135G7 | 16 GB | integrated | Development |
| ASUS TUF Gaming A17 | Windows 11 | AMD Ryzen 5 4600 | 16 GB dual-channel | NVIDIA GTX 1650, 4 GB | Target execution |

Portability between both is required.

### 2.3 Internet Use (Section 2.3)
Permitted: PubMed E-utilities, Europe PMC REST, optional public scientific sources.  
Prohibited: OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, OpenRouter, any cloud-hosted LLM inference or cloud AI processing.

### 2.4 Functional Requirements (FR-01 to FR-10)
- **FR-01 Literature Discovery:** PubMed + Europe PMC search, query construction, date/type filtering, deduplication, PMID/DOI/title/authors/abstract/date storage, source + retrieval-date tracking.
- **FR-02 Paper Acquisition:** open-access full-text download, user PDF/TXT import, copyright/licence respect, paywalled-paper identification (must not bypass paywalls), source reference maintenance.
- **FR-03 Document Processing:** PDF text extraction, section preservation (abstract/introduction/methods/results/conclusion), chunking with page/section references, error handling.
- **FR-04 Entity Recognition:** drugs, proteins, genes, diseases, pathways, concepts; normalisation where possible; preserve original text.
- **FR-05 Relationship Extraction:** inhibits, activates, binds to, regulates, upregulates, downregulates, associated with, other/unknown. Do not treat every association as a direct molecular interaction.
- **FR-06 Evidence Extraction:** per-relationship source paper ID, DOI/PMID, exact supporting text, section, relationship type, extraction method, confidence score, timestamp. Preserve contradictory evidence.
- **FR-07 Drug-Target Analysis:** aggregation across papers, frequency ranking, support/contradiction comparison, grouping by disease/drug/protein, preclinical vs clinical distinction where identifiable.
- **FR-08 Research Gap Identification:** low coverage, conflicting findings, limited evidence, missing validation, underexplored combinations, trend changes. Gaps must be evidence-based; absence in collected papers != proof of no global research; each gap needs reasoning, coverage, limitations.
- **FR-09 Knowledge Graph:** drug/protein/gene/disease nodes, relationship edges, evidence references; node/edge inspection.
- **FR-10 Report Generation:** 11 sections (research question through references). Exports: PDF, CSV, JSON.

### 2.5 Multi-Agent Architecture (Section 6)
One research coordinator + five specialised agents:
1. Literature Discovery Agent
2. Biomedical Extraction Agent
3. Evidence Analysis Agent
4. Research Gap Agent
5. Research Report Agent

Agents may share one local LLM via specialised prompts + deterministic Python processing. Coordinator manages execution, data flow, status tracking, failure handling, duplicate prevention, investigation history, and restart of interrupted workflows.

### 2.6 Database (Section 7)
SQLite. Proposed entities: Papers, Biomedical Entities, Relationships, Evidence, Research Investigations, Research Gaps, Processing History.

### 2.7 Non-Functional Requirements (Section 8)
Batch processing, bounded memory, CPU-only inference, single-model-at-a-time, progress indicators; failed-download handling, duplicate prevention, interrupted-task recovery, error logging, document preservation; provenance, confidence, association-vs-interaction distinction, contradiction preservation, no unsupported claims; secure local file handling, no execution of document content, no external DB exposure, upload validation, prompt-injection treatment of paper text; portability Arch ↔ Windows, config/env vars, reproducible deps, GPU/CPU modes documented.

### 2.8 UI Requirements (Section 9)
React dashboard, 12 views (home, new investigation, search results, paper library, paper detail/evidence viewer, entity explorer, relationship explorer, knowledge graph, gap analysis, report generation, history, settings). Dark theme, scientific dashboard style, responsive, interactive charts (Plotly), minimal animation.

### 2.9 Evaluation & Testing (Section 10)
NLP evaluation (NER/RE precision, recall, F1 on manually annotated dataset), evidence evaluation (source attribution, passage accuracy, citation correctness, contradiction accuracy), gap evaluation via human review (relevance, evidence quality, reasoning transparency, reproducibility, false-gap detection), system evaluation (download reliability, PDF processing, agent coordination, failure recovery, memory, CPU/GPU inference, cross-platform). No accuracy claims without measured results.

### 2.10 Milestones (Section 11)
M0 Requirements & Architecture → M1 Foundation → M2 Literature Acquisition → M3 Scientific NLP → M4 Evidence Analysis → M5 Multi-Agent System → M6 Research Analytics → M7 Frontend & Reporting → M8 Validation & Deployment.

### 2.11 Constraints (Section 12)
Nine constraints: no cloud LLM, no paid AI APIs, internet only for literature, Ollama/local runtime, local DB/storage, ASUS hardware target, portability, provenance, no clinical-validity claims.

### 2.12 Definition of Completion (Section 13)
Ten completion criteria, ending with documented scientific evaluation results.

---

## 3. Missing, Ambiguous, or Technically Unrealistic Requirements

| # | Area | Issue | Recommended Revision |
|---|------|-------|----------------------|
| A-1 | LLMs / hardware | SRS proposes Ollama + one shared LLM on a GTX 1650 (4 GB VRAM) but names no model, context window, or quantisation. 4 GB VRAM is tight for most instruct models. | Add explicit model-selection criteria: candidate models must fit in ≤3 GB VRAM (headroom for OS/display) or run acceptably on CPU. Require a benchmarking step (M0) before final model lock-in. Do not claim any specific model will work until measured. |
| A-2 | Evidence validation | FR-03/FR-06 require "validate extracted evidence against source passages", but with a local LLM this is probabilistic, not deterministic validation. | Reframe as "cross-check candidate evidence against source passages and flag low-confidence matches"; never present LLM output as ground truth. |
| A-3 | Research gaps | FR-08 says gaps must be "evidence-based" but absence in collected papers is not proof of no global research. | State explicitly: gaps are candidate gaps *within the retrieved corpus*, labelled with corpus coverage and limitations. |
| A-4 | Preclinical vs clinical | FR-07 requires distinguishing preclinical vs clinical evidence "where identifiable" with no method specified. | Define a deterministic heuristic (section + keyword matching: animal/cell/in vitro vs clinical trial/patient) plus LLM-assisted classification with low confidence when uncertain. |
| A-5 | Full-text availability | FR-02 assumes open-access full-text download is broadly feasible; most PubMed papers are paywalled or abstract-only. | Set expectations: the system processes whatever full text is obtainable (open-access + user imports) and clearly marks papers as metadata-only / abstract-only / full-text. |
| A-6 | Entity normalisation | FR-04 requires normalisation "where possible" with no authority specified. | Specify external identifiers as best-effort (NCBI Gene, UniProt, DrugBank only when openly accessible via permitted internet); otherwise store original text with normalized_name = NULL. |
| A-7 | LangGraph dependency | Section 6 proposes LangGraph agent orchestration. Verify it runs on target hardware and version-pin it. | Add LangGraph to dependency list with CPU-compatible requirement; document fallback to a simple Python state machine if LangGraph proves problematic offline. |
| A-8 | PDF security | Security section: "do not execute downloaded document content", "treat paper contents as untrusted input". PyMuPDF extraction is generally safe, but malicious PDFs can trigger parser bugs. | Sandbox PDF extraction (single-process, timeout, size limits), validate file type/magic bytes, scan for embedded scripts/JS before parsing. |
| A-9 | Evaluation dataset | Section 10 requires a manually annotated evaluation dataset but no source or size specified. | Define: minimum N annotated abstracts/full-texts with gold-standard entities and relationships; source (small set of PubMed open-access papers annotated by project owner). |
| A-10 | Report export | PDF export from React + Python typically needs a library (ReportLab/WeasyPrint) or browser printing. | Specify the PDF generation approach explicitly (server-side ReportLab/WeasyPrint or client-side jsPDF) and pin the library. |

---

## 4. Requirements Requiring Project-Owner Decision

1. Final local LLM model choice after benchmarking (see MODEL_SELECTION.md).
2. LangGraph vs lightweight custom state machine for agent orchestration.
3. Scope of the manually annotated evaluation dataset (size, source papers, annotator).
4. PDF export library choice (ReportLab/WeasyPrint vs client-side jsPDF).
5. Whether to integrate any literature source beyond PubMed + Europe PMC.
6. Maximum corpus size per investigation (max papers to download/process) to bound memory and time on the ASUS target.

# System Architecture — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written yet

---

## 1. Architectural Goals

- **Local-first:** all inference, NLP, orchestration, storage, and reporting run on the user's machine. No cloud LLM APIs.
- **Portable:** identical codebase runs on Arch Linux (development) and Windows 11 (target ASUS).
- **Modular:** agents, NLP stages, data sources, and exporters are independently replaceable.
- **Resource-bounded:** designed for 16 GB RAM and a 4 GB VRAM GPU; single model loaded at a time; CPU fallback everywhere.
- **Scientifically sound:** full provenance, confidence scores, contradiction preservation, no unsupported clinical claims.

---

## 2. High-Level Architecture

The system is a **three-tier local application**:

```
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|             TIER 3 — FRONTEND (React + Tailwind + Plotly)      |
|  Dashboard, investigation creation, result browsing, graph     |
|  visualisation, file upload, report download                  |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                     HTTP / JSON (REST API)                     |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|             TIER 2 — BACKEND (Python + FastAPI)                |
|  API routers | Agent coordinator (LangGraph) | 5 agents       |
|  NLP service wrappers | DB access (SQLite) | file/storage     |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    Local file system                            |
|  SQLite DB | PDFs/TXTs | reports | models (Ollama GGUF)       |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|              TIER 1 — LOCAL RUNTIMES                            |
|  Ollama (local LLM) | Python venv | Node.js (frontend build)   |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Tier responsibilities

- **Frontend (React + Tailwind + Plotly):** user interface, investigation creation, result browsing, knowledge-graph visualisation, report download. Communicates only with the FastAPI backend over HTTP.
- **Backend (FastAPI):** REST API, request validation, job queue, agent orchestration via the research coordinator, NLP service wrappers, database access, file storage, report assembly.
- **Local runtimes:** Ollama serves the local LLM over `http://localhost:11434` (default). The backend calls Ollama's REST API — never a cloud endpoint. Python environment hosts FastAPI, LangGraph (or fallback state machine), SciSpaCy, Transformers, Sentence-Transformers, FAISS, PyMuPDF, NetworkX.

---

## 3. Component Diagram (logical)

```
User input
   |
   v
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
| FastAPI  |---->| Coordinator     |---->| Agent 1: Lit.       |
| API      |     | (LangGraph)     |     | Discovery           |
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
      |                |                      |
      v                v                      v
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
| SQLite   |     | Agent 2: Bio    |---->| Agent 3: Evidence   |
| DB       |     | Extraction      |     | Analysis            |
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
      |                |                      |
      v                v                      v
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
| Ollama   |     | Agent 4: Gap    |---->| Agent 5: Report     |
| (LLM)    |     | Analysis        |     | Generation          |
+----------+     +-----------------+     +---------------------+
      |
+----------+
| File sys |
| (PDFs,   |
| reports) |
+----------+
```

Agents read from and write to SQLite; the coordinator owns the state machine. LLM calls go through Ollama; deterministic NLP (SciSpaCy, PyMuPDF, NetworkX, FAISS) runs in-process.

---

## 4. Layered Backend Design

| Layer | Responsibility | Key technologies |
|---|---|---|
| API layer | REST endpoints, request/response validation, progress streaming | FastAPI, Pydantic |
| Orchestration layer | Investigation lifecycle, agent sequencing, retries, checkpoints | LangGraph (or custom state machine), SQLite |
| Agent layer | Five specialised agents with prompts + deterministic tools | Ollama client, SciSpaCy, Transformers |
| NLP services | PDF extraction, chunking, NER, relationship extraction, embeddings, vector search | PyMuPDF, SciSpaCy, Sentence-Transformers, FAISS |
| Analytics layer | Knowledge graph, gap ranking, contradiction detection | NetworkX, Plotly (data prep), deterministic Python |
| Data layer | SQLite access, migrations, file storage paths | sqlite3 (stdlib), file storage |
| Report layer | PDF/CSV/JSON assembly with citations | ReportLab or WeasyPrint (server-side), Python csv/json |

### Single-model constraint
Only one LLM is loaded/served by Ollama at a time. The backend reuses the same Ollama model for all agents via different prompts. Embedding and NER models are separate, smaller processes; they must not be loaded simultaneously with a large LLM if memory is constrained.

---

## 5. Data Flow (end-to-end, logical)

1. User creates an investigation (research question + parameters) via frontend → API.
2. Coordinator creates investigation record (status: `queued`) and enqueues Agent 1.
3. Agent 1 builds queries, calls PubMed/Europe PMC, deduplicates, stores paper metadata.
4. Coordinator enqueues download/processing for each paper (FR-02, FR-03).
5. Agent 2 processes full text: extract text → chunk → NER → normalise → candidate relationships.
6. Agent 3 validates evidence, compares across papers, flags contradictions, builds evidence matrix.
7. Agent 4 analyses coverage, ranks candidate research gaps with reasoning + limitations.
8. Agent 5 consolidates findings and generates the report (JSON/CSV/PDF).
9. Frontend polls progress; user browses results and exports.

Each stage writes to SQLite and emits progress events. Failed stages can be retried or resumed from the last checkpoint (interrupted task recovery).

---

## 6. Cross-Cutting Design Decisions

### 6.1 No cloud inference
Ollama runs locally. All model files (GGUF) live on the local disk. The backend's Ollama client points at `127.0.0.1:11434` (configurable via env var). No API keys for OpenAI/Gemini/Claude/OpenRouter are accepted or stored.

### 6.2 Database as the integration point
Agents do not call each other directly; they communicate through the shared SQLite state and the coordinator's LangGraph state. This makes each agent independently testable and restartable.

### 6.3 Untrusted document handling
Downloaded PDFs/TXTs are stored outside the web root, validated by magic bytes + size limit before parsing, and treated as untrusted input in prompts (prompt-injection mitigations: system-message isolation, no raw user/paper text reflected back to the user without sanitisation).

### 6.4 Memory management
- Documents are streamed/chunked; full text is not loaded into memory all at once.
- Vector index (FAISS) is built per-investigation and can be discarded after the investigation completes.
- Progress indicators are emitted per paper so the UI remains responsive.

### 6.5 Portability
No machine-specific absolute paths. Storage root is configurable via environment variable (`DDS_DATA_DIR`, default `./data` relative to the executable). SQLite is file-based and portable. Python dependencies pinned in `requirements.txt`; frontend in `package.json`. GPU vs CPU is a configuration flag, not hard-coded.

---

## 7. Architectural Requirements Revisions

- If LangGraph cannot be installed/used offline on Windows 11, replace with a lightweight deterministic Python state machine (same interfaces, no external orchestration dependency).
- PDF export library must be chosen and pinned (see SRS.md item A-10).
- FAISS is optional: if memory is too tight on the ASUS, replace with SQLite full-text search + cosine similarity over NumPy arrays in batches.

# Database Design — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written yet

---

## 1. Design Principles

- **SQLite** as the single local relational database (file-based, portable, no server).
- **Fully normalised** to at least 3NF; junction tables for many-to-many relationships.
- **Provenance-first:** every extracted fact links back to a paper, section, page, and extraction method with a timestamp and confidence score.
- **Contradiction-safe:** relationships and evidence are never soft-deleted or overwritten to "pick a winner"; contradictory rows coexist.
- **Cross-platform:** relative, configurable storage paths; no machine-specific absolute paths.
- **Migratable:** versioned SQL migration files applied at startup.

---

## 2. Entity-Relationship Summary

```
investigation 1:N paper
investigation 1:N research_gap
investigation 1:N processing_history
paper 1:N paper_section
paper 1:N paper_entity_mention
paper_entity_mention N:1 entity
paper_entity_mention N:1 paper_section
entity 1:N relationship (as source)
entity 1:N relationship (as target)
relationship 1:N evidence
evidence N:1 paper
evidence N:1 relationship
evidence N:1 paper_section
research_gap 1:N gap_supporting_evidence (junction)
```

---

## 3. Schema Specification

### 3.1 Core tables

**investigations**
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| investigation_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| research_question | TEXT | NOT NULL | |
| search_parameters | TEXT | NOT NULL | JSON: disease, drug, gene, date range, max papers, types, full-text pref |
| status | TEXT | NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued' | queued/running/completed/failed/partial |
| created_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |
| updated_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |

**papers**
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| paper_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | FK → investigations | |
| pmid | TEXT | unique (nullable) | PubMed ID |
| doi | TEXT | unique (nullable) | |
| title | TEXT | NOT NULL | |
| authors | TEXT | | JSON array of author strings |
| abstract | TEXT | | |
| publication_date | TEXT | | ISO-8601 or year |
| source | TEXT | NOT NULL | 'pubmed' / 'europepmc' / 'user_import' |
| full_text_path | TEXT | | relative path under storage root |
| access_status | TEXT | NOT NULL | 'open_access' / 'abstract_only' / 'paywalled' / 'user_import' / 'unavailable' |
| retrieved_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |
| source_database | TEXT | NOT NULL | which DB provided metadata |

**paper_sections**
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| section_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| paper_id | INTEGER | FK → papers | |

### 3.2 Indexes

```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_investigation ON papers(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_pmid ON papers(pmid) WHERE pmid IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_doi ON papers(doi) WHERE doi IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_access_status ON papers(access_status);

CREATE INDEX idx_mentions_entity ON paper_entity_mentions(entity_id);

CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_type ON relationships(relationship_type);

CREATE INDEX idx_history_investigation ON processing_history(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_history_agent ON processing_history(agent_name);
```

### 3.3 Foreign keys

SQLite `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;` must be enabled on every connection. All FK columns reference the corresponding PK with `ON DELETE CASCADE` only where semantically safe (e.g., `paper_entity_mentions` → `papers`); `evidence` → `relationships` uses `ON DELETE CASCADE`; investigations → gaps uses `ON DELETE CASCADE`.

---

## 4. Migration Strategy

- Migrations are versioned SQL files in `db/migrations/` named `V001__initial_schema.sql`, `V002__...`, etc.
- A `schema_version` table tracks the applied version:
  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL);
  ```
- On startup, the backend applies pending migrations in order within a single transaction.
- Rollbacks are not automated; destructive migrations require a backup copy of the SQLite file first.
- No ORM-migration magic (e.g., Alembic) is required; raw SQL keeps the dependency surface small and auditable.

---

## 5. Data Retention & Portability

- The SQLite file and the `data/` storage root are relocatable; paths are relative to a configurable `DDS_DATA_DIR`.
- Backups = copy the SQLite file + data folder (file-level copy is safe when the app is stopped).
- No cloud sync of the database; it never leaves the local machine.

---

## 6. Schema Gaps to Confirm

- Whether `authors` should be normalised into a separate `authors` table (many-to-many with papers) — deferred; JSON array is acceptable for v1.
- Whether `external_identifier` lookups are required at all, given the "permitted internet" restriction and possible rate limits — marked nullable/best-effort.

input.content:
# SRS Analysis — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Project Type:** Final-Year B.Tech IT Project  
**Status:** Planning phase — analysis of the provided Software Requirements Specification

---

## 1. Source Document

This document analyses the SRS provided by the project owner (version 1.0). The full SRS text (Sections 1–14) is the authoritative source; this file summarises the requirements, flags missing/ambiguous items, and records recommended revisions before implementation begins.

---

## 2. Requirements Summary

### 2.1 Objectives (Section 1.3)
Ten objectives, all local-first: literature discovery; paper download/organisation; biomedical entity extraction (drugs, genes, proteins, diseases); drug-target relationship extraction; evidence extraction; cross-publication comparison; research-gap and contradiction identification; interactive knowledge graphs; traceable research reports; 100% local AI inference.

### 2.2 Operating Environments (Sections 2.1–2.2)

| Machine | OS | CPU | RAM | GPU/VRAM | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dell Inspiron 15 3511 | Arch Linux (Hyprland) | Intel i5-1135G7 | 16 GB | integrated | Development |
| ASUS TUF Gaming A17 | Windows 11 | AMD Ryzen 5 4600 | 16 GB dual-channel | NVIDIA GTX 1650, 4 GB | Target execution |

Portability between both is required.

### 2.3 Internet Use (Section 2.3)
Permitted: PubMed E-utilities, Europe PMC REST, optional public scientific sources.  
Prohibited: OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, OpenRouter, any cloud-hosted LLM inference or cloud AI processing.

### 2.4 Functional Requirements (FR-01 to FR-10)
- **FR-01 Literature Discovery:** PubMed + Europe PMC search, query construction, date/type filtering, deduplication, PMID/DOI/title/authors/abstract/date storage, source + retrieval-date tracking.
- **FR-02 Paper Acquisition:** open-access full-text download, user PDF/TXT import, copyright/licence respect, paywalled-paper identification (must not bypass paywalls), source reference maintenance.
- **FR-03 Document Processing:** PDF text extraction, section preservation (abstract/introduction/methods/results/conclusion), chunking with page/section references, error handling.
- **FR-04 Entity Recognition:** drugs, proteins, genes, diseases, pathways, concepts; normalisation where possible; preserve original text.
- **FR-05 Relationship Extraction:** inhibits, activates, binds to, regulates, upregulates, downregulates, associated with, other/unknown. Do not treat every association as a direct molecular interaction.
- **FR-06 Evidence Extraction:** per-relationship source paper ID, DOI/PMID, exact supporting text, section, relationship type, extraction method, confidence score, timestamp. Preserve contradictory evidence.
- **FR-07 Drug-Target Analysis:** aggregation across papers, frequency ranking, support/contradiction comparison, grouping by disease/drug/protein, preclinical vs clinical distinction where identifiable.
- **FR-08 Research Gap Identification:** low coverage, conflicting findings, limited evidence, missing validation, underexplored combinations, trend changes. Gaps must be evidence-based; absence in collected papers != proof of no global research; each gap needs reasoning, coverage, limitations.
- **FR-09 Knowledge Graph:** drug/protein/gene/disease nodes, relationship edges, evidence references; node/edge inspection.
- **FR-10 Report Generation:** 11 sections (research question through references). Exports: PDF, CSV, JSON.

### 2.5 Multi-Agent Architecture (Section 6)
One research coordinator + five specialised agents:
1. Literature Discovery Agent
2. Biomedical Extraction Agent
3. Evidence Analysis Agent
4. Research Gap Agent
5. Research Report Agent

Agents may share one local LLM via specialised prompts + deterministic Python processing. Coordinator manages execution, data flow, status tracking, failure handling, duplicate prevention, investigation history, and restart of interrupted workflows.

### 2.6 Database (Section 7)
SQLite. Proposed entities: Papers, Biomedical Entities, Relationships, Evidence, Research Investigations, Research Gaps, Processing History.

### 2.7 Non-Functional Requirements (Section 8)
Batch processing, bounded memory, CPU-only inference, single-model-at-a-time, progress indicators; failed-download handling, duplicate prevention, interrupted-task recovery, error logging, document preservation; provenance, confidence, association-vs-interaction distinction, contradiction preservation, no unsupported claims; secure local file handling, no execution of document content, no external DB exposure, upload validation, prompt-injection treatment of paper text; portability Arch ↔ Windows, config/env vars, reproducible deps, GPU/CPU modes documented.

### 2.8 UI Requirements (Section 9)
React dashboard, 12 views (home, new investigation, search results, paper library, paper detail/evidence viewer, entity explorer, relationship explorer, knowledge graph, gap analysis, report generation, history, settings). Dark theme, scientific dashboard style, responsive, interactive charts (Plotly), minimal animation.

### 2.9 Evaluation & Testing (Section 10)
NLP evaluation (NER/RE precision, recall, F1 on manually annotated dataset), evidence evaluation (source attribution, passage accuracy, citation correctness, contradiction accuracy), gap evaluation via human review (relevance, evidence quality, reasoning transparency, reproducibility, false-gap detection), system evaluation (download reliability, PDF processing, agent coordination, failure recovery, memory, CPU/GPU inference, cross-platform). No accuracy claims without measured results.

### 2.10 Milestones (Section 11)
M0 Requirements & Architecture → M1 Foundation → M2 Literature Acquisition → M3 Scientific NLP → M4 Evidence Analysis → M5 Multi-Agent System → M6 Research Analytics → M7 Frontend & Reporting → M8 Validation & Deployment.

### 2.11 Constraints (Section 12)
Nine constraints: no cloud LLM, no paid AI APIs, internet only for literature, Ollama/local runtime, local DB/storage, ASUS hardware target, portability, provenance, no clinical-validity claims.

### 2.12 Definition of Completion (Section 13)
Ten completion criteria, ending with documented scientific evaluation results.

---

## 3. Missing, Ambiguous, or Technically Unrealistic Requirements

| # | Area | Issue | Recommended Revision |
|---|------|-------|----------------------|
| A-1 | LLMs / hardware | SRS proposes Ollama + one shared LLM on a GTX 1650 (4 GB VRAM) but names no model, context window, or quantisation. 4 GB VRAM is tight for most instruct models. | Add explicit model-selection criteria: candidate models must fit in ≤3 GB VRAM (headroom for OS/display) or run acceptably on CPU. Require a benchmarking step (M0) before final model lock-in. Do not claim any specific model will work until measured. |
| A-2 | Evidence validation | FR-03/FR-06 require "validate extracted evidence against source passages", but with a local LLM this is probabilistic, not deterministic validation. | Reframe as "cross-check candidate evidence against source passages and flag low-confidence matches"; never present LLM output as ground truth. |
| A-3 | Research gaps | FR-08 says gaps must be "evidence-based" but absence in collected papers is not proof of no global research. | State explicitly: gaps are candidate gaps *within the retrieved corpus*, labelled with corpus coverage and limitations. |
| A-4 | Preclinical vs clinical | FR-07 requires distinguishing preclinical vs clinical evidence "where identifiable" with no method specified. | Define a deterministic heuristic (section + keyword matching: animal/cell/in vitro vs clinical trial/patient) plus LLM-assisted classification with low confidence when uncertain. |
| A-5 | Full-text availability | FR-02 assumes open-access full-text download is broadly feasible; most PubMed papers are paywalled or abstract-only. | Set expectations: the system processes whatever full text is obtainable (open-access + user imports) and clearly marks papers as metadata-only / abstract-only / full-text. |
| A-6 | Entity normalisation | FR-04 requires normalisation "where possible" with no authority specified. | Specify external identifiers as best-effort (NCBI Gene, UniProt, DrugBank only when openly accessible via permitted internet); otherwise store original text with normalized_name = NULL. |
| A-7 | LangGraph dependency | Section 6 proposes LangGraph agent orchestration. Verify it runs on target hardware and version-pin it. | Add LangGraph to dependency list with CPU-compatible requirement; document fallback to a simple Python state machine if LangGraph proves problematic offline. |
| A-8 | PDF security | Security section: "do not execute downloaded document content", "treat paper contents as untrusted input". PyMuPDF extraction is generally safe, but malicious PDFs can trigger parser bugs. | Sandbox PDF extraction (single-process, timeout, size limits), validate file type/magic bytes, scan for embedded scripts/JS before parsing. |
| A-9 | Evaluation dataset | Section 10 requires a manually annotated evaluation dataset but no source or size specified. | Define: minimum N annotated abstracts/full-texts with gold-standard entities and relationships; source (small set of PubMed open-access papers annotated by project owner). |
| A-10 | Report export | PDF export from React + Python typically needs a library (ReportLab/WeasyPrint) or browser printing. | Specify the PDF generation approach explicitly (server-side ReportLab/WeasyPrint or client-side jsPDF) and pin the library. |

---

## 4. Requirements Requiring Project-Owner Decision

1. Final local LLM model choice after benchmarking (see MODEL_SELECTION.md).
2. LangGraph vs lightweight custom state machine for agent orchestration.
3. Scope of the manually annotated evaluation dataset (size, source papers, annotator).
4. PDF export library choice (ReportLab/WeasyPrint vs client-side jsPDF).
5. Whether to integrate any literature source beyond PubMed + Europe PMC.
6. Maximum corpus size per investigation (max papers to download/process) to bound memory and time on the ASUS target.
