# SRS Analysis — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — analysis of the provided Software Requirements Specification

## Source Document
This file analyses the SRS provided by the project owner (version 1.0). The full SRS text (Sections 1–14) is authoritative; this file summarises requirements, flags missing/ambiguous items, and records recommended revisions before implementation.

## Requirements Summary

**Objectives (1.3):** Ten local-first objectives — literature discovery; paper download/organisation; biomedical entity extraction (drugs, genes, proteins, diseases); drug-target relationship extraction; evidence extraction; cross-publication comparison; research-gap and contradiction identification; interactive knowledge graphs; traceable research reports; 100% local AI inference.

**Operating environments (2.1–2.2):**
| Machine | OS | CPU | RAM | GPU/VRAM | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dell Inspiron 15 3511 | Arch Linux (Hyprland) | Intel i5-1135G7 | 16 GB | integrated | Development |
| ASUS TUF Gaming A17 | Windows 11 | AMD Ryzen 5 4600 | 16 GB dual-channel | NVIDIA GTX 1650, 4 GB | Target execution |

**Internet (2.3):** Permitted — PubMed E-utilities, Europe PMC REST, optional public scientific sources. Prohibited — OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, OpenRouter, any cloud-hosted LLM inference or cloud AI processing.

**FR-01 to FR-10:** Literature discovery (PubMed + Europe PMC, filtering, deduplication); paper acquisition (open-access download, PDF/TXT import, no paywall bypass); document processing (PDF extraction, section preservation, chunking, page refs); entity recognition (drugs/proteins/genes/diseases/pathways, normalise, preserve original text); relationship extraction (inhibits/activates/binds_to/regulates/upregulates/downregulates/associated_with/other; association ≠ direct interaction); evidence extraction (source ID, DOI/PMID, exact text, section, type, method, confidence, timestamp; preserve contradictions); drug-target analysis (aggregate, rank, compare support/contradiction, group by disease/drug/protein, preclinical vs clinical); research gaps (low coverage, conflicts, limited evidence, missing validation, underexplored combos, trend changes; evidence-based; absence ≠ proof; reasoning + coverage + limitations per gap); knowledge graph (drug/protein/gene/disease nodes, edges, evidence refs; node/edge inspection); report generation (11 sections; PDF/CSV/JSON exports).

**Multi-agent (6):** Coordinator + 5 agents (Literature Discovery, Biomedical Extraction, Evidence Analysis, Research Gap, Research Report). Agents share one local LLM via specialised prompts + deterministic Python. Coordinator manages execution, data flow, status, failures, duplicate prevention, history, restart.

**Database (7):** SQLite. Entities: Papers, Biomedical Entities, Relationships, Evidence, Research Investigations, Research Gaps, Processing History.

**Non-functional (8):** Batch processing, bounded memory, CPU-only inference, single model at a time, progress indicators; failed-download handling, duplicate prevention, interrupted-task recovery, error logging, document preservation; provenance, confidence, association-vs-interaction, contradiction preservation, no unsupported claims; secure local file handling, no execution of document content, no external DB exposure, upload validation, prompt-injection treatment of paper text; portability Arch ↔ Windows, config/env vars, reproducible deps, GPU/CPU modes documented.

**UI (9):** React dashboard, 12 views; dark theme; responsive; Plotly charts; minimal animation.

**Evaluation (10):** NER/RE precision/recall/F1 on manually annotated dataset; evidence evaluation (attribution, passage accuracy, citation correctness, contradiction accuracy); gap human review (relevance, evidence quality, reasoning transparency, reproducibility, false-gap detection); system evaluation (download reliability, PDF processing, agent coordination, failure recovery, memory, CPU/GPU, cross-platform). No accuracy claims without measured results.

**Milestones (11):** M0 → M1 → M2 → M3 → M4 → M5 → M6 → M7 → M8.

**Constraints (12):** Nine constraints incl. no cloud LLM, no paid AI APIs, internet only for literature, Ollama/local runtime, local DB/storage, ASUS target, portability, provenance, no clinical-validity claims.

**Completion (13):** Ten criteria ending with documented scientific evaluation results.

## Missing, Ambiguous, or Technically Unrealistic Requirements

| # | Area | Issue | Recommended Revision |
|---|------|-------|----------------------|
| A-1 | LLMs / hardware | No model, context window, or quantisation specified for Ollama on GTX 1650 (4 GB VRAM). | Model must fit ≤3 GB VRAM or run on CPU. Benchmarking step in M0 before model lock-in. No claims until measured. |

## 2. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

# System Architecture — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written

## Architectural Goals
- **Local-first:** all inference, NLP, orchestration, storage, reporting run on the user's machine. No cloud LLM APIs.
- **Portable:** identical codebase on Arch Linux (dev) and Windows 11 (target ASUS).
- **Modular:** agents, NLP stages, data sources, exporters independently replaceable.
- **Resource-bounded:** 16 GB RAM, 4 GB VRAM GPU; single model loaded at a time; CPU fallback everywhere.
- **Scientifically sound:** full provenance, confidence scores, contradiction preservation, no unsupported clinical claims.

## High-Level Architecture (three-tier local)

```
TIER 3 — FRONTEND (React + Tailwind + Plotly)
   Dashboard, investigation creation, result browsing, graph viz, upload, exports
          HTTP / JSON (REST API)
TIER 2 — BACKEND (Python + FastAPI)
   API routers | Coordinator (LangGraph) | 5 agents | NLP wrappers | SQLite | file storage
          Local file system
   SQLite DB | PDFs/TXTs | reports | Ollama GGUF models
TIER 1 — LOCAL RUNTIMES
   Ollama (local LLM) | Python venv | Node.js (frontend build)
```

**Tier responsibilities:**
- **Frontend:** UI only; talks to FastAPI backend over HTTP.
- **Backend:** REST API, validation, job queue, agent orchestration via coordinator, NLP service wrappers, DB access, file storage, report assembly.
- **Local runtimes:** Ollama serves the LLM on `http://localhost:11434` (configurable). Backend calls Ollama REST — never cloud. Python hosts FastAPI, LangGraph (or fallback state machine), SciSpaCy, Transformers, Sentence-Transformers, FAISS, PyMuPDF, NetworkX.

## Component Diagram (logical)

```
User input -> FastAPI API -> Coordinator (LangGraph)
   |                 |                 |
   v                 v                 v
 SQLite DB    Agent 2: Bio Extraction   Agent 1: Lit Discovery
                                |                 |
                                v                 v
                          Agent 3: Evidence   Agent 4: Gap Analysis
                          Agent 5: Report   Ollama (LLM)
                                |
                          File system (PDFs, reports)
```

Agents read/write SQLite; coordinator owns the state machine. LLM calls via Ollama; deterministic NLP (SciSpaCy, PyMuPDF, NetworkX, FAISS) in-process.

## Layered Backend Design

| Layer | Responsibility | Technologies |
|---|---|---|
| API layer | REST endpoints, validation, progress streaming | FastAPI, Pydantic |
| Orchestration | Investigation lifecycle, sequencing, retries, checkpoints | LangGraph (or custom state machine), SQLite |
| Agent layer | Five agents with prompts + deterministic tools | Ollama client, SciSpaCy, Transformers |
| NLP services | PDF extraction, chunking, NER, RE, embeddings, vector search | PyMuPDF, SciSpaCy, Sentence-Transformers, FAISS |
| Analytics | Knowledge graph, gap ranking, contradiction detection | NetworkX, Plotly data prep, deterministic Python |
| Data layer | SQLite access, migrations, storage paths | sqlite3 (stdlib), file storage |
| Report layer | PDF/CSV/JSON assembly with citations | ReportLab or WeasyPrint (server-side), csv/json |

**Single-model constraint:** one LLM served by Ollama at a time; reused across agents via different prompts. Embedding/NER models are smaller; not loaded simultaneously with a large LLM if memory constrained.

## End-to-End Data Flow (logical)
1. User creates investigation (question + params) → API.
2. Coordinator creates investigation record (`queued`), enqueues Agent 1.
3. Agent 1 builds queries, calls PubMed/Europe PMC, deduplicates, stores metadata.
4. Coordinator enqueues download/processing per paper (FR-02, FR-03).
5. Agent 2: extract text → chunk → NER → normalise → candidate relationships.
6. Agent 3: validate evidence, compare across papers, flag contradictions, evidence matrix.
7. Agent 4: coverage analysis, rank candidate gaps with reasoning + limitations.
8. Agent 5: consolidate findings, generate report (JSON/CSV/PDF).
9. Frontend polls progress; user browses and exports.
Each stage writes SQLite and emits progress events; failed stages retry/resume from checkpoint.

## Cross-Cutting Design Decisions
- **No cloud inference:** Ollama local; model files (GGUF) on local disk; Ollama client at `127.0.0.1:11434` (env-configurable). No OpenAI/Gemini/Claude/OpenRouter keys accepted or stored.
- **Database as integration point:** agents communicate via shared SQLite state + coordinator LangGraph state — independently testable and restartable.
- **Untrusted document handling:** PDFs/TXTs stored outside web root, validated by magic bytes + size limit before parsing, treated as untrusted input in prompts (system-message isolation, no raw paper text reflected unsanitised).
- **Memory management:** documents streamed/chunked; full text not loaded at once; FAISS index per-investigation, discardable after completion; per-paper progress events keep UI responsive.
- **Portability:** no machine-specific absolute paths; storage root configurable via `DDS_DATA_DIR` (default `./data`); SQLite file-based and portable; deps pinned in `requirements.txt` / `package.json`; GPU vs CPU is a config flag.

## Architectural Revisions
- If LangGraph can't run offline on Windows 11 → lightweight deterministic Python state machine (same interfaces).
- PDF export library must be chosen and pinned (SRS item A-10).
- FAISS optional: if ASUS memory too tight, replace with SQLite FTS + batched NumPy cosine similarity.

# Database Design — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written

## Design Principles
- **SQLite** — single local relational DB, file-based, portable, no server.
- **Normalised** to ≥3NF; junction tables for many-to-many.
- **Provenance-first:** every extracted fact links to paper, section, page, extraction method, timestamp, confidence.
- **Contradiction-safe:** relationships/evidence never soft-deleted or overwritten to "pick a winner"; contradictory rows coexist.
- **Cross-platform:** relative, configurable paths; no machine-specific absolute paths.
- **Migratable:** versioned SQL migrations applied at startup.

## Entity-Relationship Summary
```
investigation 1:N paper
investigation 1:N research_gap
investigation 1:N processing_history
paper 1:N paper_section
paper 1:N paper_entity_mention
paper_entity_mention N:1 entity
paper_entity_mention N:1 paper_section
entity 1:N relationship (as source), 1:N relationship (as target)
relationship 1:N evidence
evidence N:1 paper, N:1 relationship, N:1 paper_section
research_gap 1:N gap_supporting_evidence (junction)
```

## Schema Specification

**investigations**
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| investigation_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| research_question | TEXT | NOT NULL | |
| search_parameters | TEXT | NOT NULL | JSON: disease, drug, gene, date range, max papers, types, full-text pref |
| status | TEXT | NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued' | queued/running/completed/failed/partial |
| created_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |
| updated_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |

**papers**
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| paper_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | FK → investigations | |
| pmid | TEXT | unique (nullable) | PubMed ID |
| doi | TEXT | unique (nullable) | |
| title | TEXT | NOT NULL | |
| authors | TEXT | | JSON array |
| abstract | TEXT | | |
| publication_date | TEXT | | ISO-8601 or year |
| source | TEXT | NOT NULL | pubmed/europepmc/user_import |
| full_text_path | TEXT | | relative path under storage root |
| access_status | TEXT | NOT NULL | open_access/abstract_only/paywalled/user_import/unavailable |
| retrieved_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |
| source_database | TEXT | NOT NULL | |

**paper_sections** — section_id PK, paper_id FK, section_name (abstract/introduction/methods/results/conclusion/other), section_order, page_start, page_end.

**entities** — entity_id PK, normalized_name unique (nullable), entity_type (drug/protein/gene/disease/pathway/concept/other), external_identifier (nullable, best-effort), external_source.

**paper_entity_mentions** — mention_id PK, paper_id FK, section_id FK, entity_id FK, entity_name_original (exact text), page_number, chunk_id.

**relationships** — relationship_id PK, investigation_id FK, source_entity_id FK, target_entity_id FK, relationship_type (inhibits/activates/binds_to/regulates/upregulates/downregulates/associated_with/other), confidence_score (0–1), extraction_method (llm/rule/hybrid), is_direct_interaction (0=association, 1=direct), created_at.

**evidence** — evidence_id PK, relationship_id FK, paper_id FK, section_id FK, supporting_text (exact passage), page_number, evidence_type (experimental/computational/review/clinical/other), extraction_method, confidence_score (0–1), extracted_at.

**research_gaps** — gap_id PK, investigation_id FK, gap_description, gap_category (low_coverage/conflicting_findings/limited_evidence/missing_validation/underexplored_combination/trend_change), ranking_score (0–1), literature_coverage, limitations, supporting_reasoning, created_at.

**gap_supporting_evidence** — gap_id FK, evidence_id FK, PK(gap_id, evidence_id).

**processing_history** — task_id PK, investigation_id FK, agent_name, status (queued/running/completed/failed/skipped), started_at, completed_at, execution_time_seconds, error_details (JSON), retry_count DEFAULT 0.

## Indexes
```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_investigation ON papers(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_pmid ON papers(pmid) WHERE pmid IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_doi ON papers(doi) WHERE doi IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_access_status ON papers(access_status);
CREATE INDEX idx_mentions_paper ON paper_entity_mentions(paper_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_mentions_entity ON paper_entity_mentions(entity_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_entities_type ON entities(entity_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_investigation ON relationships(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_entities ON relationships(source_entity_id, target_entity_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_type ON relationships(relationship_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_evidence_relationship ON evidence(relationship_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_evidence_paper ON evidence(paper_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_gaps_investigation ON research_gaps(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_history_investigation ON processing_history(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_history_agent ON processing_history(agent_name);
```

## Foreign Keys
`PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;` on every connection. `ON DELETE CASCADE` only where safe (paper_entity_mentions → papers; evidence → relationships; investigations → gaps).

## Migration Strategy
- Versioned SQL in `db/migrations/`: `V001__initial_schema.sql`, `V002__...`, etc.
- `schema_version` table: `CREATE TABLE schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL);`
- Startup applies pending migrations in order in a single transaction.
- No automated rollbacks; destructive migrations require a SQLite backup first.
- Raw SQL (no Alembic) — small, auditable dependency surface.

## Data Retention & Portability
- SQLite file + `data/` storage root relocatable; paths relative to configurable `DDS_DATA_DIR`.
- Backups = copy SQLite file + data folder (safe when app stopped).
- No cloud sync; DB never leaves local machine.

## Schema Gaps to Confirm
- Authors normalised into separate table? Deferred — JSON array acceptable for v1.
- external_identifier lookups required given permitted-internet limits? Marked nullable/best-effort.

## 4. docs/AGENT_SPECIFICATION.md

# Agent Specification — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written

## Orchestration Model
- **Research Coordinator** (LangGraph or fallback state machine): owns investigation lifecycle, agent sequencing, state, retries, checkpoints, duplicate prevention, history, restart.
- **Agents communicate via shared SQLite state**, not direct calls. Each agent reads inputs from DB, writes outputs to DB, records `processing_history`.
- **One shared local LLM** (Ollama) across agents, specialised prompts per agent; deterministic Python post-processing where possible.
- **State schema (LangGraph):** investigation_id, status, current_agent, papers[], entities[], relationships[], evidence[], gaps[], errors[], retry_counts, checkpoints.

## Agent 1 — Literature Discovery
**Inputs:** investigation research question + search parameters (disease, drug, gene, date range, max papers, publication types, full-text preference).
**Responsibilities:** interpret query; generate search keywords (Boolean, MeSH-aware); call PubMed E-utilities + Europe PMC REST; retrieve metadata (PMID, DOI, title, authors, abstract, date); deduplicate by PMID/DOI/title; store source DB + retrieval date; mark access_status (open_access/abstract_only/paywalled/unavailable).
**Outputs:** structured literature collection (paper metadata rows).
**Deterministic parts:** query construction, deduplication, metadata normalisation. **LLM parts:** keyword generation from research question.
**Failure handling:** API rate limits → backoff/retry; one DB down → use the other; empty result → flag to user.

## Agent 2 — Biomedical Extraction
**Inputs:** paper list from Agent 1; full-text paths (open-access downloads + user imports).
**Responsibilities:** extract PDF/TXT text (PyMuPDF); preserve sections (abstract/intro/methods/results/conclusion); chunk text with page/section refs; NER (SciSpaCy) for drugs, proteins, genes, diseases, pathways; normalise names (best-effort external IDs); identify candidate relationships; preserve supporting text.
**Outputs:** entities, entity mentions, candidate relationships.
**Deterministic parts:** PDF extraction, chunking, section detection, SciSpaCy NER, normalisation lookup. **LLM parts:** relationship classification (type + direct-vs-association), normalisation disambiguation.
**Security:** paper text treated as untrusted; prompt-injection mitigations; size/time limits on extraction.
**Failure handling:** corrupted PDF → mark paper extraction_failed, continue with others; abstract-only papers → entity extraction from abstract only, flagged.

## Agent 3 — Evidence Analysis
**Inputs:** candidate relationships + source passages from Agent 2.
**Responsibilities:** cross-check candidate evidence against source passages; compare findings across publications; identify contradictory findings (same drug-target, opposite relationship types); categorise evidence types (experimental/computational/review/clinical); preserve uncertainty (low confidence, conflicting).
**Outputs:** evidence matrix (evidence rows with provenance, confidence, type).
**Deterministic parts:** passage matching, contradiction detection (opposite types for same entity pair), evidence categorisation heuristics. **LLM parts:** passage-relationship validation, confidence scoring.
**Contradiction handling:** both supporting and contradicting rows stored; no silent selection of one conclusion.

## Agent 4 — Research Gap
**Inputs:** aggregated relationships + evidence matrix from Agent 3.
**Responsibilities:** analyse literature coverage per drug-target-disease; identify underexplored relationships; detect conflicting results; identify evidence limitations; rank candidate gaps using transparent criteria.
**Outputs:** candidate research gaps with explanations + references.
**Deterministic parts:** coverage counts, frequency ranking, conflict detection, trend-over-time (publication_date bucketing). **LLM parts:** gap description generation, reasoning text, limitation drafting.
**Transparency:** ranking_score formula documented (e.g., weighted combination of coverage, conflict, evidence strength); each gap includes supporting_reasoning, literature_coverage, limitations; absence ≠ proof of no global research.

## Agent 5 — Research Report
**Inputs:** all prior agent outputs for an investigation.
**Responsibilities:** consolidate findings; generate structured summaries; prepare report with citations; include limitations + confidence info.
**Outputs:** final report (JSON/CSV/PDF).
**Contents:** research question, search methodology, literature stats, identified drugs, proteins/genes, relationships, supporting evidence, contradictory findings, gaps, limitations, references.
**Deterministic parts:** stats computation, citation formatting, section assembly. **LLM parts:** narrative summaries, gap narratives.
**Export:** JSON (full data), CSV (relationships/evidence flat), PDF (server-side ReportLab/WeasyPrint).

## Research Coordinator
- Manage agent execution order (1→2→3→4→5, with per-paper parallelism inside Agent 2).
- Pass structured data between agents via SQLite.
- Track execution status per task (processing_history).
- Handle failures: retry (configurable), mark failed, continue other papers, allow restart from checkpoint.
- Prevent duplicate processing (unique constraints, idempotent tasks).
- Maintain investigation history.
- Support restarting interrupted workflows (resume from last completed stage).
- Expose progress events to frontend (polling/WebSocket).

## Communication Contracts (summary)
| From → To | Via | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| Coordinator → Agent 1 | SQLite task queue | investigation_id, search params |
| Agent 1 → Coordinator | SQLite | paper rows, access_status |
| Coordinator → Agent 2 | SQLite task queue | paper_id, full_text_path |
| Agent 2 → Coordinator | SQLite | entities, mentions, candidate relationships |
| Agent 2 → Agent 3 | SQLite | relationships + source passages |
| Agent 3 → Agent 4 | SQLite | evidence matrix |
| Agent 4 → Agent 5 | SQLite | research gaps |
| Agent 5 → Coordinator | SQLite | report artifacts |
| All → Coordinator | processing_history | status, timestamps, errors |

## 5. docs/DATA_PIPELINE.md

# Data Pipeline — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written

## Pipeline Stages (end-to-end)

```
[1] Ingestion & Query
    User creates investigation → coordinator → Agent 1
[2] Literature Discovery
    Agent 1: keywords → PubMed + Europe PMC → metadata → deduplicate → store (Papers table)
[3] Paper Acquisition
    Download open-access full text (PDF); user PDF/TXT import;
    validate magic bytes + size; mark access_status; store files under data/papers/
[4] Document Processing
    Agent 2: PyMuPDF text extraction → section detection (abstract/intro/methods/results/conclusion)
    → chunk with page/section refs → handle errors (corrupt PDF → flag, continue)
[5] Biomedical NLP
    SciSpaCy NER → entities (drug/protein/gene/disease/pathway/concept)
    → normalise (best-effort external IDs) → preserve original text
    → store Entities + Paper Entity Mentions
[6] Relationship Extraction
    LLM + rules → candidate relationships (type, direct-vs-association, confidence)
    → store Relationships + Evidence (supporting text, section, page, method, timestamp)
[7] Evidence Analysis
    Agent 3: cross-check vs passages → compare across papers → contradictions → evidence matrix
[8] Research Analytics
    Agent 4: coverage → gaps → ranking → store Research Gaps
    NetworkX knowledge graph (drug/protein/gene/disease nodes, edges, evidence refs)
[9] Reporting
    Agent 5: consolidate → JSON/CSV/PDF report with citations + limitations
[10] Export & UI
    Frontend browses; downloads JSON/CSV/PDF; Plotly graph visualisation
```

## Stage Details

### Stage 1–2: Ingestion & Discovery
- Query builder: disease + drug + gene + date range + publication types → Boolean/MeSH queries for PubMed E-utilities + Europe PMC.
- Rate-limit respect (PubMed: 3 req/sec without key; Europe PMC limits).
- Deduplication key: PMID > DOI > normalized title.
- Store: PMID, DOI, title, authors, abstract, publication_date, source, retrieved_at, access_status.

### Stage 3: Acquisition
- Open-access full-text via Europe PMC `fullTextUrl` / PubMed Central OA; respect `access_status`.
- User imports: validate file (PDF magic `%PDF`, TXT), size cap, scan for embedded JS/scripts; store outside web root.
- Paywalled: mark `paywalled`, do NOT bypass; user may upload manually.

### Stage 4: Processing
- PyMuPDF extract text per page; detect sections via headings; preserve page numbers.
- Chunk size target ~512–1024 tokens with overlap; each chunk carries paper_id, section_id, page range.
- Errors logged per paper; pipeline continues.

### Stage 5–6: NLP & Relationships
- SciSpaCy models (`en_ner_bc5cdr_md` for chemicals/diseases, `en_ner_bionlp13cg_md` for genes/proteins — see MODEL_SELECTION.md).
- Normalise: best-effort mapping to NCBI Gene/UniProt/DrugBank; store original + normalized.
- Relationship extraction: LLM prompt returns type + direct/interaction flag + confidence + supporting span; deterministic post-validation (span exists in source text).

### Stage 7: Evidence Analysis
- For each relationship, verify supporting span verbatim in source passage.
- Contradiction: same source→target entity pair with opposite types (e.g., inhibits vs activates) across papers → both kept, flagged.
- Evidence type heuristic: section keywords (methods/results → experimental; discussion → review; clinical trial terms → clinical).

### Stage 8: Analytics
- NetworkX graph: nodes = entities (typed), edges = relationships (typed, weighted by confidence/frequency).
- Gap ranking_score: documented transparent formula (coverage, conflict, evidence strength, recency).
- Trend: relationship counts bucketed by publication year.

### Stage 9–10: Reporting & Export
- JSON: nested, full provenance.
- CSV: flat relationships + evidence.
- PDF: server-side (ReportLab/WeasyPrint), citations, limitations.

## Memory & Performance Bounds
- Stream PDFs; never load full corpus into RAM.
- Per-paper processing; FAISS index per investigation (optional, discardable).
- Progress per paper → UI responsive.
- Single LLM at a time via Ollama.

## Failure & Recovery
- Failed download → retry (exponential backoff), then mark failed, continue.
- Corrupt PDF → extraction_failed flag, continue.
- Interrupted workflow → coordinator resumes from last completed stage (processing_history checkpoints).
- Duplicate prevention → unique constraints + idempotent tasks.

## Outputs per Investigation
- Papers collection + metadata
- Entities + mentions
- Relationships + evidence (with contradictions)
- Knowledge graph (NetworkX → Plotly for frontend)
- Research gaps (ranked, with reasoning/coverage/limitations)
- Report (JSON/CSV/PDF)

# Model Selection — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no benchmarks performed yet; no model lock-in

## Hardware Constraint
Target execution: ASUS TUF Gaming A17, AMD Ryzen 5 4600, 16 GB RAM, **NVIDIA GTX 1650 4 GB VRAM**, Windows 11.  
Development: Dell i5-1135G7, 16 GB RAM, integrated GPU, Arch Linux.

**4 GB VRAM is the binding constraint.** After OS/display overhead, roughly ≤3 GB is safely available for a model. Most 7B+ instruct models (even 4-bit quantised, ~4–5 GB) will not fit with headroom. CPU inference is required as fallback on both machines (dev has no dGPU).

**Rule:** No model is recommended as final until benchmarked on the target hardware for VRAM, load time, and tokens/sec. The SRS explicitly forbids inventing benchmarks; this section lists candidates and selection criteria only.

## Candidate Models by Role

### 6.1 Local LLM (extraction, relationship classification, report narratives, gap reasoning)
Ollama GGUF format, 4-bit quantised (Q4_K_M) preferred for VRAM fit.

| Candidate | Approx. size (Q4) | VRAM fit (4 GB) | Role fit | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct | ~1.3 GB | Yes | Primary candidate | Smallest instruct; leaves VRAM headroom; CPU OK |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | ~1.9 GB | Yes | Primary candidate | Strong instruction following; CPU OK |
| Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct | ~2.6 GB | Tight | Possible | May fit with careful context; test |
| Phi-3.5-mini-3.8B-Instruct | ~3.5 GB | Tight/Risky | Possible | Benchmark required |
| Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen-7B+ | ~4.7–5+ GB | No | Excluded for GPU | CPU-only possible but slow |

**Recommendation:** start with **Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct** or **Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct** (GGUF Q4_K_M) as primary, benchmark load time + tokens/sec + VRAM on the ASUS; fall back to CPU if GPU too slow. Context window ≤4096 to bound memory. Only one model loaded at a time (Ollama default).

### 6.2 Biomedical NER (SciSpaCy)
| Candidate | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| en_ner_bc5cdr_md | Chemicals + diseases | Drugs, diseases |
| en_ner_bionlp13cg_md | Genes, proteins, etc. | Broader biomedical |
| en_core_web_sm (fallback) | General entities | Lower precision |

Run on CPU (SciSpaCy models are small, ~100s MB). CPU-only acceptable; no GPU required.

### 6.3 Embeddings (Sentence Transformers)
| Candidate | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| all-MiniLM-L6-v2 | ~80 MB | Default; CPU fast |
| all-MiniLM-L12-v2 | ~120 MB | Better quality if needed |

CPU-only; small memory footprint.

### 6.4 Vector Search
FAISS (CPU index) preferred; fallback to SQLite FTS + batched NumPy cosine similarity if memory tight.

## Selection Criteria (to be applied in M0 benchmarking)
1. VRAM ≤ 3 GB on GTX 1650 (load + runtime overhead).
2. Load time < ~30 s on target.
3. Acceptable tokens/sec for batch extraction on CPU/GPU.
4. Accuracy sufficient for relationship classification (validated on annotated dataset, Section 10).
5. Ollama compatibility (GGUF).
6. CPU fallback performance acceptable on Ryzen 5 4600 / i5-1135G7.

## Outputs of M0
- Benchmark report (VRAM, load time, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU) — measured, not invented.
- Final model lock-in + quantisation + context window.
- Documented GPU and CPU execution modes.

- **FR-03 Document Processing:** PDF text extraction, section preservation (abstract/introduction/methods/results/conclusion), chunking with page/section references, error handling.
- **FR-04 Entity Recognition:** drugs, proteins, genes, diseases, pathways, concepts; stable identifiers + synonym normalisation; preserve original text.
- **FR-05 Relationship Extraction:** inhibits, activates, binds to, regulates, upregulates, downregulates, associated with, other/unknown. Detect negation, uncertainty, speculation and experimental context. Do not treat every association as a direct molecular interaction.
- **FR-06 Evidence Extraction:** every relationship carries an exact, verifiable source passage + source paper ID, DOI/PMID, section, relationship type, extraction method, confidence score, timestamp. Preserve contradictory evidence.
- **FR-07 Drug-Target Analysis:** aggregation across papers, frequency ranking, support/contradiction comparison, grouping by disease/drug/protein, preclinical vs clinical distinction where identifiable.
- **FR-08 Research Gap Identification:** low coverage, conflicting findings, limited evidence, missing validation, underexplored combinations, trend changes. Gaps evidence-based; corpus-relative (absence ≠ proof of no global research); deterministic, explainable ranking; each gap has reasoning, coverage, limitations.
- **FR-09 Knowledge Graph:** drug/protein/gene/disease nodes, relationship edges, evidence references; node/edge inspection.
- **FR-10 Report Generation:** 11 sections (research question through references). Exports: PDF (ReportLab), CSV, JSON.

### 2.5 Multi-Agent Architecture (Section 6)
Coordinator + 5 agents (Literature Discovery, Biomedical Extraction, Evidence Analysis, Research Gap, Research Report). LangGraph with lightweight state-machine fallback. Agents share one local LLM via specialised prompts; deterministic Python processing preferred where sufficient. Coordinator manages execution, data flow, status, failures, duplicate prevention, history, restart. Investigation-level data isolation.

SQLite, ≥3NF, investigation-level isolation, reliable transaction handling, provenance-first, contradiction-safe. Entities: Papers, Biomedical Entities, Relationships, Evidence, Research Investigations, Research Gaps, Processing History.

### 2.7 Non-Functional Requirements (Section 8)
Batch processing, bounded memory, CPU-only inference, single model at a time, progress indicators; failed-download handling, duplicate prevention, interrupted-task recovery, error logging, document preservation; provenance, confidence, association-vs-interaction, contradiction preservation, no unsupported claims; secure local file handling, no execution of document content, no external DB exposure, upload validation, prompt-injection treatment of paper text; portability Arch ↔ Windows, config/env vars, reproducible deps, GPU/CPU modes documented.

### 2.8 UI Requirements (Section 9)
React dashboard, 12 views; dark theme; responsive; Plotly charts; minimal animation.

### 2.9 Evaluation & Testing (Section 10)
NER/RE precision/recall/F1 on 50–100 manually annotated papers; evidence evaluation (attribution, passage accuracy, citation correctness, contradiction accuracy); gap human review (relevance, evidence quality, reasoning transparency, reproducibility, false-gap detection); system evaluation (download reliability, PDF processing, agent coordination, failure recovery, memory, CPU/GPU, cross-platform). No accuracy claims without measured results.

### 2.10 Milestones (Section 11)
M0 → M1 → M2 → M3 → M4 → M5 → M6 → M7 → M8.

### 2.11 Constraints (Section 12)
Nine constraints: no cloud LLM, no paid AI APIs, internet only for literature, Ollama/local runtime, local DB/storage, ASUS target, portability, provenance, no clinical-validity claims.

### 2.12 Definition of Completion (Section 13)
Ten criteria ending with documented scientific evaluation results.

---

## 3. Missing, Ambiguous, or Technically Unrealistic Requirements

| # | Area | Issue | Recommended Revision |
|---|------|-------|----------------------|
| A-1 | LLMs / hardware | No model, context window, or quantisation specified for Ollama on GTX 1650 (4 GB VRAM). | Benchmark Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama-3.2-1B (GGUF Q4_K_M). Model must fit ≤3 GB VRAM or run on CPU. Benchmarking step in M0 before lock-in. No claims until measured. |
| A-2 | Evidence validation | "Validate evidence against source passages" is probabilistic with a local LLM. | Reframe as "cross-check candidate evidence against source passages; every relationship must carry an exact, verifiable source passage; flag low-confidence matches". Never present LLM output as ground truth. |
| A-3 | Research gaps | Absence in collected papers is not proof of no global research. | Gaps are candidate gaps within the retrieved corpus, labelled corpus-relative with coverage and limitations. Ranking is deterministic and explainable; LLM writes descriptions only, never invents scores. |
| A-4 | Preclinical vs clinical | No method specified. | Deterministic heuristic (section + keyword: animal/cell/in vitro vs clinical trial/patient) + LLM classification with low confidence when uncertain. |
| A-5 | Full-text availability | Most PubMed papers paywalled/abstract-only. | Process whatever full text is obtainable; mark papers metadata-only / abstract-only / full-text. |
| A-6 | Entity normalisation | No authority specified. | Stable biomedical entity identifiers + synonym normalisation; best-effort external IDs (NCBI Gene/UniProt/DrugBank via permitted internet); otherwise normalized_name/synonyms nullable. |
| A-7 | LangGraph | Offline/Windows compatibility unknown; version-pin. | LangGraph with lightweight Python state-machine fallback. |
| A-8 | PDF security | Malicious PDFs can trigger parser bugs. | Magic-byte validation, size caps, single-process extraction with timeout, scan for embedded JS; treat paper text as untrusted (prompt injection). |
| A-9 | Evaluation dataset | No source or size specified. | 50–100 manually annotated papers (gold-standard entities/relationships), annotated by project owner. |
| A-10 | Report export | PDF export needs a library. | ReportLab (server-side); pin the library. |

---

1. Final local LLM model after M0 benchmarking (Qwen2.5-1.5B vs Llama-3.2-1B).
2. LangGraph vs custom state machine (primary/fallback).
3. Annotated evaluation dataset scope (50–100 papers, source, annotator).
4. PDF export library (ReportLab selected; confirm).
5. Any literature source beyond PubMed + Europe PMC.
6. Maximum corpus size per investigation (initial configurable max: 100 papers).

---

## 5. Adopted Design Decisions (from project owner)

- Benchmark **Qwen2.5-1.5B** and **Llama-3.2-1B** (GGUF Q4_K_M).
- **LangGraph** with lightweight **state-machine fallback**.

# System Architecture — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written  
**Planned location:** `/home/user/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`

---

## 1. Architectural Goals

- **Local-first:** all inference, NLP, orchestration, storage, reporting run on the user's machine. No cloud LLM APIs.
- **Portable:** identical codebase on Arch Linux (dev) and Windows 11 (target ASUS).
- **Modular:** agents, NLP stages, data sources, exporters independently replaceable.
- **Resource-bounded:** 16 GB RAM, 4 GB VRAM GPU; single model loaded at a time; CPU fallback everywhere.
- **Scientifically sound:** full provenance, confidence scores, contradiction preservation, no unsupported clinical claims.
- **Investigation-isolated:** all data scoped to an investigation_id; no cross-investigation leakage.
- **Deterministic-first:** prefer deterministic Python over LLM calls where sufficient; avoid unnecessary LLM invocations.

---

## 2. High-Level Architecture (three-tier local)

```
TIER 3 — FRONTEND (React + Tailwind + Plotly)
   Dashboard, investigation creation, result browsing, graph viz, upload, exports
          HTTP / JSON (REST API)
TIER 2 — BACKEND (Python + FastAPI)
   API routers | Coordinator (LangGraph, state-machine fallback) | 5 agents
   NLP service wrappers | SQLite (investigation-isolated, transactions) | file/storage
          Local file system
   SQLite DB | PDFs/TXTs | reports | Ollama GGUF models
TIER 1 — LOCAL RUNTIMES
   Ollama (local LLM) | Python venv | Node.js (frontend build)
```

### Tier responsibilities
- **Frontend:** UI only; talks to FastAPI backend over HTTP.
- **Backend:** REST API, validation, job queue, agent orchestration via coordinator, NLP wrappers, DB access, file storage, report assembly.
- **Local runtimes:** Ollama serves the LLM on `http://localhost:11434` (configurable). Backend calls Ollama REST — never cloud. Python hosts FastAPI, LangGraph (or fallback state machine), SciSpaCy, Transformers, Sentence-Transformers, FAISS, PyMuPDF, NetworkX.

---

## 3. Component Diagram (logical)

```
User input -> FastAPI API -> Coordinator (LangGraph / state-machine fallback)
   |                 |                         |
   v                 v                         v
 SQLite DB    Agent 2: Bio Extraction      Agent 1: Lit Discovery
                     |                         |
                     v                         v
               Agent 3: Evidence          Agent 4: Gap Analysis
               Agent 5: Report            Agent 1..5 share 1 Ollama LLM
                     |
               File system (PDFs, reports)
```

- Agents read/write SQLite; coordinator owns the state machine.
- LLM calls via Ollama; deterministic NLP (SciSpaCy, PyMuPDF, NetworkX, FAISS) in-process.
- One LLM loaded at a time; reused across agents via different prompts.

---

## 4. Layered Backend Design

| Layer | Responsibility | Technologies |
|---|---|---|
| API layer | REST endpoints, validation, progress streaming | FastAPI, Pydantic |
| Orchestration | Investigation lifecycle, sequencing, retries, checkpoints, transactions | LangGraph (or state-machine fallback), SQLite |
| Agent layer | Five agents with prompts + deterministic tools | Ollama client, SciSpaCy, Transformers |
| NLP services | PDF extraction, chunking, NER, RE, embeddings, vector search | PyMuPDF, SciSpaCy, Sentence-Transformers, FAISS |
| Analytics | Knowledge graph, gap ranking, contradiction detection | NetworkX, Plotly data prep, deterministic Python |
| Data layer | SQLite access, migrations, storage paths, investigation isolation | sqlite3 (stdlib), file storage |
| Report layer | PDF/CSV/JSON assembly with citations | ReportLab (server-side), csv/json |

### Single-model constraint
Only one LLM served by Ollama at a time; reused across agents via different prompts. Embedding/NER models are smaller; not loaded simultaneously with a large LLM if memory constrained.

### Deterministic-first principle
Relationship-type hints, negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental-context flags, section detection, deduplication, coverage counts and gap ranking scores are computed deterministically in Python where possible. The LLM is used only for disambiguation, narrative descriptions, and confidence-scoring assistance — never to invent ranking scores.

---

## 5. End-to-End Data Flow (logical)

1. User creates investigation (question + params) → API → coordinator creates investigation record (`queued`, investigation_id).
2. Coordinator enqueues Agent 1.
3. Agent 1 builds queries, calls PubMed/Europe PMC, deduplicates, stores paper metadata scoped to investigation_id.
4. Coordinator enqueues download/processing per paper (FR-02, FR-03).
5. Agent 2: extract text → chunk → NER → stable identifiers + synonym normalisation → candidate relationships (with negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental context) → every relationship gets an exact, verifiable source passage.
6. Agent 3: cross-check evidence vs passages → compare across papers → contradictions → evidence matrix (deterministic conflict detection).
7. Agent 4: coverage → deterministic, explainable gap ranking (score computed in Python; LLM writes description only) → research gaps.
8. Agent 5: consolidate → report (JSON/CSV/PDF via ReportLab).
9. Frontend polls progress; user browses and exports.

Each stage writes SQLite within a transaction scoped to investigation_id and emits progress events. Failed stages retry/resume from checkpoint (processing_history).

---

## 6. Cross-Cutting Design Decisions

### 6.1 No cloud inference
Ollama local; GGUF model files on local disk; Ollama client at `127.0.0.1:11434` (env-configurable). No OpenAI/Gemini/Claude/OpenRouter keys accepted or stored.

### 6.2 Database as integration point + investigation isolation
Agents communicate via shared SQLite state, not direct calls. Every core table carries `investigation_id`; queries are scoped to the active investigation. Transactions wrap multi-statement writes for atomicity.

### 6.3 Untrusted document handling
PDFs/TXTs stored outside web root, validated by magic bytes + size limit before parsing, treated as untrusted input in prompts (system-message isolation; no raw paper text reflected unsanitised to the user).

### 6.4 Memory management
Documents streamed/chunked; full text never loaded at once; FAISS index per-investigation, discardable after completion; per-paper progress events keep UI responsive; single model at a time.

### 6.5 Portability
No machine-specific absolute paths; storage root configurable via `DDS_DATA_DIR` (default `./data`); SQLite file-based and portable; deps pinned in `requirements.txt` / `package.json`; GPU vs CPU is a config flag.

---

## 7. Architectural Revisions

- If LangGraph cannot run offline on Windows 11 → lightweight deterministic Python state machine (same interfaces).
- PDF export library = ReportLab (server-side), pinned.
- FAISS optional; fallback to SQLite FTS + batched NumPy cosine similarity if ASUS memory too tight.

# Database Design — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written  
**Planned location:** `/home/user/docs/DATABASE_DESIGN.md`

---

## 1. Design Principles

- **SQLite** — single local relational DB, file-based, portable, no server.
- **Investigation-level isolation:** every core entity carries `investigation_id`; queries scoped to the active investigation; no cross-investigation leakage.
- **Reliable transaction handling:** multi-statement writes wrapped in explicit transactions; `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` on every connection; WAL journal mode for concurrent read safety.
- **Fully normalised** to ≥3NF; junction tables for many-to-many.
- **Provenance-first:** every extracted fact links to paper, section, page, extraction method, timestamp, confidence.
- **Contradiction-safe:** relationships/evidence never soft-deleted or overwritten to "pick a winner"; contradictory rows coexist.
- **Cross-platform:** relative, configurable paths; no machine-specific absolute paths.
- **Migratable:** versioned SQL migrations applied at startup within a transaction.

---

## 2. Entity-Relationship Summary

```
investigation 1:N paper
investigation 1:N research_gap
investigation 1:N processing_history
investigation 1:N relationship
investigation 1:N entity (ownership/origin)
paper 1:N paper_section
paper 1:N paper_entity_mention
paper_entity_mention N:1 entity
paper_entity_mention N:1 paper_section
entity 1:N entity_synonym
entity 1:N relationship (as source), 1:N relationship (as target)
relationship 1:N evidence
evidence N:1 paper, N:1 relationship, N:1 paper_section
research_gap 1:N gap_supporting_evidence (junction)
```

---

## 3. Schema Specification

### 3.1 Core tables

**investigations**
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| investigation_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | isolation root |
| research_question | TEXT | NOT NULL | |
| search_parameters | TEXT | NOT NULL | JSON: disease, drug, gene, date range, max_papers (default 100), types, full-text pref |
| status | TEXT | NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued' | queued/running/completed/failed/partial |
| created_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |
| updated_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |

**papers** (all rows scoped by investigation_id)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| paper_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL, FK → investigations | isolation |
| pmid | TEXT | unique nullable | PubMed ID |
| doi | TEXT | unique nullable | |
| title | TEXT | NOT NULL | |
| authors | TEXT | | JSON array |
| abstract | TEXT | | |
| publication_date | TEXT | | ISO-8601 or year |
| source | TEXT | NOT NULL | pubmed/europepmc/user_import |
| full_text_path | TEXT | | relative path under storage root |
| access_status | TEXT | NOT NULL | open_access/abstract_only/paywalled/user_import/unavailable |
| retrieved_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |
| source_database | TEXT | NOT NULL | |

**paper_sections** — section_id PK, paper_id FK, section_name (abstract/introduction/methods/results/conclusion/other), section_order, page_start, page_end.

**entities** (stable identifiers)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| entity_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL, FK → investigations | isolation |
| normalized_name | TEXT | nullable | canonical normalised name |
| entity_type | TEXT | NOT NULL | drug/protein/gene/disease/pathway/concept/other |
| stable_identifier | TEXT | nullable | stable biomedical ID (e.g. UniProt, NCBI Gene, DrugBank) |
| stable_identifier_source | TEXT | nullable | authority of stable_identifier |

**entity_synonyms** (synonym normalisation)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| synonym_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| entity_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL, FK → entities | |
| synonym | TEXT | NOT NULL | observed synonym / original mention |
| source | TEXT | nullable | where synonym observed |

**paper_entity_mentions** — mention_id PK, paper_id FK, section_id FK, entity_id FK, entity_name_original (exact text), page_number, chunk_id.

**relationships** — relationship_id PK, investigation_id FK (isolation), source_entity_id FK, target_entity_id FK, relationship_type (inhibits/activates/binds_to/regulates/upregulates/downregulates/associated_with/other), confidence_score (0–1), extraction_method (llm/rule/hybrid), is_direct_interaction (0=association, 1=direct), negation (0/1), uncertainty (0/1), speculation (0/1), experimental_context (0/1), source_passage (exact verifiable text NOT NULL), source_passage_hash TEXT (verifiable checksum), created_at.

**evidence** — evidence_id PK, relationship_id FK, paper_id FK, section_id FK, supporting_text (exact passage NOT NULL), page_number, evidence_type (experimental/computational/review/clinical/other), extraction_method, confidence_score (0–1), extracted_at.

**research_gaps** — gap_id PK, investigation_id FK, gap_description TEXT NOT NULL (LLM-generated), gap_category (low_coverage/conflicting_findings/limited_evidence/missing_validation/underexplored_combination/trend_change), ranking_score REAL NOT NULL (0–1, deterministic, computed in Python — LLM never invents), ranking_criteria TEXT NOT NULL (JSON explaining the deterministic inputs/weights), literature_coverage TEXT, limitations TEXT NOT NULL, supporting_reasoning TEXT NOT NULL, created_at.

**gap_supporting_evidence** — gap_id FK, evidence_id FK, PK(gap_id, evidence_id).

**processing_history** — task_id PK, investigation_id FK, agent_name, status, started_at, completed_at, execution_time_seconds, error_details (JSON), retry_count DEFAULT 0.

### 3.2 Indexes

```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_investigation ON papers(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_pmid ON papers(pmid) WHERE pmid IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_doi ON papers(doi) WHERE doi IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_entities_investigation ON entities(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_entities_type ON entities(entity_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_mentions_paper ON paper_entity_mentions(paper_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_mentions_entity ON paper_entity_mentions(entity_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_investigation ON relationships(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_entities ON relationships(source_entity_id, target_entity_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_type ON relationships(relationship_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_evidence_relationship ON evidence(relationship_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_evidence_paper ON evidence(paper_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_gaps_investigation ON research_gaps(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_history_investigation ON processing_history(investigation_id);
```

### 3.3 Foreign Keys & Transactions
`PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;` on every connection. `ON DELETE CASCADE` only where safe (paper_entity_mentions → papers; evidence → relationships; investigations → gaps/papers/history). Multi-table writes (e.g., relationship + its evidence) executed in a single `BEGIN...COMMIT` transaction.

---

## 4. Migration Strategy
- Versioned SQL in `db/migrations/`: `V001__initial_schema.sql`, `V002__...`, etc.
- `schema_version` table: `CREATE TABLE schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL);`
- Startup applies pending migrations in order within a single transaction.
- No automated rollbacks; destructive migrations require a SQLite backup first.
- Raw SQL (no Alembic) — small, auditable surface.

---

## 5. Data Retention & Portability
- SQLite file + `data/` storage root relocatable; paths relative to configurable `DDS_DATA_DIR`.
- Backups = copy SQLite file + data folder (safe when app stopped).
- No cloud sync; DB never leaves local machine.

---

## 6. Schema Gaps to Confirm
- Authors normalised into separate table? Deferred — JSON array acceptable for v1.
- stable_identifier lookups best-effort given permitted-internet limits; nullable.

# Agent Specification — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written  
**Planned location:** `/home/user/docs/AGENT_SPECIFICATION.md`

---

## 1. Orchestration Model

- **Research Coordinator** (LangGraph primary, lightweight Python state-machine fallback): owns investigation lifecycle, agent sequencing, state, retries, checkpoints, duplicate prevention, history, restart. All state and outputs scoped to `investigation_id` (investigation-level isolation).
- **Agents communicate via shared SQLite**, not direct calls. Each agent reads inputs from DB, writes outputs to DB within a transaction, records `processing_history`.
- **One shared local LLM** (Ollama) across agents, specialised prompts per agent; deterministic Python post-processing where possible.
- **Deterministic-first:** section detection, deduplication, negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental-context flags, coverage counts, conflict detection and gap ranking scores computed in Python where sufficient; LLM used only for disambiguation and narrative descriptions. Avoid unnecessary LLM calls/agents.

---

## 2. State Schema (coordinator)

`{ investigation_id, status, current_agent, papers[], entities[], relationships[], evidence[], gaps[], errors[], retry_counts, checkpoints, max_papers }` — all keyed by `investigation_id`.

---

## 3. Agent 1 — Literature Discovery

**Inputs:** investigation research question + search parameters (disease, drug, gene, date range, max_papers ≤ 100 configurable, publication types, full-text preference).
**Responsibilities:** interpret query; generate search keywords (Boolean, MeSH-aware); call PubMed E-utilities + Europe PMC REST; retrieve metadata (PMID, DOI, title, authors, abstract, date); deduplicate by PMID/DOI/normalized title; store source DB + retrieval date; mark access_status (open_access/abstract_only/paywalled/unavailable).
**Outputs:** paper metadata rows scoped to investigation_id.
**Deterministic:** query construction, deduplication, metadata normalisation. **LLM:** keyword generation from research question (optional; can be rule-based).
**Failure:** API rate limits → backoff/retry; one DB down → use the other; empty result → flag to user.

---

## 4. Agent 2 — Biomedical Extraction

**Inputs:** paper list from Agent 1; full-text paths (open-access downloads + user imports).
**Responsibilities:** extract PDF/TXT text (PyMuPDF); preserve sections (abstract/intro/methods/results/conclusion); chunk text with page/section references; NER (SciSpaCy) for drugs, proteins, genes, diseases, pathways; stable biomedical identifiers + synonym normalisation; identify candidate relationships.
**Relationship extraction (required detection):**
- relationship type: inhibits/activates/binds_to/regulates/upregulates/downregulates/associated_with/other
- negation (e.g., "does not inhibit")
- uncertainty (e.g., "may", "suggests", "could")
- speculation (e.g., "potential", "hypothesized")
- experimental context (in vitro / in vivo / animal / cell line / clinical)
**Every relationship must carry an exact, verifiable source passage** (verbatim span from source text) + source_passage_hash for verification. Association ≠ direct interaction (is_direct_interaction flag).
**Outputs:** entities, entity_synonyms, entity mentions, candidate relationships scoped to investigation_id.
**Deterministic:** PDF extraction, chunking, section detection, SciSpaCy NER, normalisation lookup, context flag heuristics. **LLM:** relationship-type disambiguation, direct-vs-association, confidence-scoring assistance.
**Security:** paper text treated as untrusted; prompt-injection mitigations; size/time limits on extraction.
**Failure:** corrupted PDF → extraction_failed flag, continue; abstract-only papers → NER from abstract only, flagged.

---

## 5. Agent 3 — Evidence Analysis

**Inputs:** candidate relationships + source passages from Agent 2.
**Responsibilities:** cross-check candidate evidence against source passages (verbatim span verification); compare findings across publications; identify contradictory findings (same source→target pair, opposite relationship types); categorise evidence types (experimental/computational/review/clinical); preserve uncertainty (low confidence, conflicting).
**Outputs:** evidence matrix scoped to investigation_id (provenance, confidence, type).
**Deterministic:** passage-span verification, contradiction detection (opposite types for same entity pair), evidence categorisation heuristics. **LLM:** passage-relationship validation, confidence scoring.
**Contradiction handling:** both supporting and contradicting rows stored; no silent selection of one conclusion.

---

## 6. Agent 4 — Research Gap

**Inputs:** aggregated relationships + evidence matrix from Agent 3.
**Responsibilities:** analyse literature coverage per drug-target-disease; identify underexplored relationships; detect conflicting results; identify evidence limitations; rank candidate gaps using transparent, deterministic criteria.
**Deterministic ranking_score (computed in Python):** documented formula — weighted combination of literature coverage (fewer papers = higher gap score), conflict presence, evidence strength, recency/trend. LLM writes gap_description and supporting_reasoning only; LLM never invents or adjusts ranking_score.
**Outputs:** research gaps scoped to investigation_id, each with gap_category, ranking_score, ranking_criteria (JSON of deterministic inputs), literature_coverage, limitations, supporting_reasoning, gap_supporting_evidence references.
**Corpus-relative:** gaps labelled as candidate gaps within retrieved corpus; absence ≠ proof of no global research; limitations field required.

---

## 7. Agent 5 — Research Report

**Inputs:** all prior agent outputs for an investigation.
**Responsibilities:** consolidate findings; generate structured summaries; prepare report with citations; include limitations + confidence info.
**Outputs:** final report (JSON/CSV/PDF via ReportLab).
**Contents:** research question, search methodology, literature stats, identified drugs, proteins/genes, relationships, supporting evidence, contradictory findings, gaps, limitations, references.
**Deterministic:** stats computation, citation formatting, section assembly. **LLM:** narrative summaries, gap narratives.

---

## 8. Research Coordinator

- Manage agent execution order (1→2→3→4→5; per-paper parallelism inside Agent 2).
- Pass structured data between agents via SQLite (investigation-isolated).
- Track execution status per task (processing_history) within transactions.
- Handle failures: retry (configurable), mark failed, continue other papers, allow restart from checkpoint.
- Prevent duplicate processing (unique constraints, idempotent tasks).
- Maintain investigation history.
- Support restarting interrupted workflows (resume from last completed stage).
- Expose progress events to frontend (polling).

---

## 9. Communication Contracts (summary)

| From → To | Via | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| Coordinator → Agent 1 | SQLite task queue | investigation_id, search params, max_papers |
| Agent 1 → Coordinator | SQLite (txn) | paper rows, access_status |
| Coordinator → Agent 2 | SQLite task queue | paper_id, full_text_path |
| Agent 2 → Coordinator | SQLite (txn) | entities, synonyms, mentions, candidate relationships (with source passages) |
| Agent 2 → Agent 3 | SQLite | relationships + source passages |
| Agent 3 → Agent 4 | SQLite | evidence matrix |
| Agent 4 → Agent 5 | SQLite | research gaps |
| Agent 5 → Coordinator | SQLite (txn) | report artifacts |
| All → Coordinator | processing_history (txn) | status, timestamps, errors |

**Version:** 1.0 (planning)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written

---

## 1. Pipeline Stages (end-to-end)

```
[1] Ingestion & Query
    User creates investigation → coordinator → Agent 1
[2] Literature Discovery
    Agent 1: keywords → PubMed + Europe PMC → metadata → deduplicate → store (Papers, investigation-scoped)
[3] Paper Acquisition
    Download open-access full text (PDF); user PDF/TXT import;
    validate magic bytes + size; mark access_status; store under data/papers/
[4] Document Processing
    Agent 2: PyMuPDF text extraction → section detection (abstract/intro/methods/results/conclusion)
    → chunk with page/section refs → handle errors (corrupt PDF → flag, continue)
[5] Biomedical NER & Normalisation
    SciSpaCy NER → entities (drug/protein/gene/disease/pathway/concept)
    → stable identifiers + synonym normalisation → preserve original text
    → store Entities + Entity Synonyms + Paper Entity Mentions
[6] Relationship Extraction
    Deterministic context flags + LLM → candidate relationships (type, direct-vs-association,
    negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental context, confidence)
    → EVERY relationship carries an exact, verifiable source passage + source_passage_hash
    → store Relationships + Evidence
[7] Evidence Analysis
    Agent 3: verbatim passage verification → compare across papers → contradictions → evidence matrix
[8] Research Analytics
    Agent 4: coverage → deterministic, explainable gap ranking (Python; LLM writes description only)
    → store Research Gaps; NetworkX knowledge graph (nodes/edges/evidence refs)
[9] Reporting
    Agent 5: consolidate → JSON/CSV/PDF (ReportLab) report with citations + limitations
[10] Export & UI
    Frontend browses investigation-scoped data; downloads JSON/CSV/PDF; Plotly graph visualisation
```

---

## 2. Stage Details

### Stage 1–2: Ingestion & Discovery
- Query builder: disease + drug + gene + date range + publication types → Boolean/MeSH queries for PubMed E-utilities + Europe PMC.
- Rate-limit respect (PubMed: 3 req/sec without key; Europe PMC limits).
- Deduplication key: PMID > DOI > normalized title.
- Store: PMID, DOI, title, authors, abstract, publication_date, source, retrieved_at, access_status. Max 100 papers per investigation (configurable).

### Stage 3: Acquisition
- Open-access full-text via Europe PMC `fullTextUrl` / PubMed Central OA; respect `access_status`.
- User imports: validate file (PDF magic `%PDF`, TXT), size cap, scan for embedded JS/scripts; store outside web root.
- Paywalled: mark `paywalled`, do NOT bypass; user may upload manually.

### Stage 4: Processing
- PyMuPDF extract text per page; detect sections via headings; preserve page numbers.
- Chunk size target ~512–1024 tokens with overlap; each chunk carries paper_id, section_id, page range.
- Errors logged per paper; pipeline continues.

### Stage 5–6: NLP & Relationships
- SciSpaCy models (`en_ner_bc5cdr_md` chemicals/diseases, `en_ner_bionlp13cg_md` genes/proteins — see MODEL_SELECTION.md).
- Stable identifiers + synonym normalisation (best-effort NCBI Gene/UniProt/DrugBank); store original + normalized.
- Relationship extraction: deterministic detection of negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental context; LLM classifies type + direct/interaction flag + confidence + supporting span; deterministic post-validation (span exists verbatim in source text).
- **Verifiable source passage:** every relationship stores `source_passage` (exact text) and `source_passage_hash` so a reviewer can locate and confirm the passage.

### Stage 7: Evidence Analysis
- For each relationship, verify supporting span verbatim in source passage.
- Contradiction: same source→target entity pair with opposite types across papers → both kept, flagged (contradiction-safe).
- Evidence type heuristic: section keywords (methods/results → experimental; discussion → review; clinical trial terms → clinical).

### Stage 8: Analytics
- NetworkX graph: nodes = entities (typed), edges = relationships (typed, weighted by confidence/frequency).
- Gap ranking_score: deterministic formula documented in `ranking_criteria` (JSON of inputs/weights); LLM writes description only, never invents score.
- Trend: relationship counts bucketed by publication year.

### Stage 9–10: Reporting & Export
- JSON: nested, full provenance.
- CSV: flat relationships + evidence.
- PDF: server-side ReportLab, citations, limitations.

---

## 3. Memory & Performance Bounds
- Stream PDFs; never load full corpus into RAM.
- Per-paper processing; FAISS index per-investigation (optional, discardable).
- Progress per paper → UI responsive.
- Single LLM at a time via Ollama.

---

## 4. Failure & Recovery
- Failed download → retry (exponential backoff), then mark failed, continue.
- Corrupt PDF → extraction_failed flag, continue.
- Interrupted workflow → coordinator resumes from last completed stage (processing_history checkpoints).
- Duplicate prevention → unique constraints + idempotent tasks.
- All multi-stage writes scoped to investigation_id within SQLite transactions.

---

## 5. Outputs per Investigation (investigation-scoped)
- Papers collection + metadata
- Entities + synonyms + mentions
- Relationships + evidence (with contradictions; verifiable source passages)
- Knowledge graph (NetworkX → Plotly for frontend)
- Research gaps (ranked, deterministic score, reasoning/coverage/limitations)
- Report (JSON/CSV/PDF)

### DATABASE_DESIGN.md — Investigation isolation with composite FKs

Key design:
- `investigations` table is the root. `investigation_id` PK.
- Every child table has `investigation_id` NOT NULL FK → investigations.
- Composite FKs: e.g., `paper_entity_mentions` references `(paper_id, investigation_id)` where papers has a composite unique key `(paper_id, investigation_id)`. Similarly evidence references `(relationship_id, investigation_id)`, mentions reference `(entity_id, investigation_id)`, etc.
- This enforces at DB level that relationships/mentions/evidence can't cross investigations.
- PMID/DOI unique only within an investigation: unique constraint on `(pmid, investigation_id)` and `(doi, investigation_id)`, not global unique. So same PMID can appear in different investigations.
- New `paper_chunks` table: chunk_id PK, paper_id FK, investigation_id FK, section_id FK (nullable), chunk_text, chunk_order, page_start, page_end, token_count. This is persistent chunk storage.
- `paper_entity_mentions` references `paper_chunks(chunk_id)` via chunk_id, plus investigation_id composite.

This gives us durable task storage with idempotency keys (task_key), inputs/outputs, checkpoint_state, retries.

### Composite FKs needed
For composite FKs to work in SQLite, the parent columns must have a UNIQUE constraint. So:
- `papers` needs UNIQUE(paper_id, investigation_id) — but paper_id is already PK, so (paper_id, investigation_id) is automatically unique. Actually since paper_id is PK, (paper_id, investigation_id) is unique. Good.
- `paper_sections` needs UNIQUE(section_id, paper_id, investigation_id) — section_id is PK so automatically unique combo.
- `entities` needs UNIQUE(entity_id, investigation_id) — entity_id PK, auto unique.
- `relationships` needs UNIQUE(relationship_id, investigation_id) — relationship_id PK, auto unique.
- `evidence` needs UNIQUE(evidence_id, investigation_id) — evidence_id PK, auto unique.
- `research_gaps` needs UNIQUE(gap_id, investigation_id) — gap_id PK, auto unique.
- `paper_chunks` needs UNIQUE(chunk_id, paper_id, investigation_id) — chunk_id PK, auto unique.

So composite FKs work because the PK makes the (id, investigation_id) combination unique. Good. SQLite supports composite foreign keys.

### WAL mode, transactions
Mention PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, foreign_keys=ON.

### Durable workflow recovery (correction 2)
- Use custom SQLite task/checkpoint schema (processing_history table above) rather than relying solely on LangGraph checkpointing, because we need explicit investigation isolation and idempotency. LangGraph SQLite checkpointing can be an option but the custom schema is the source of truth for recovery.
- task_key = idempotency key (e.g., "agent2:paper:{paper_id}" or "agent1:discover:{investigation_id}").
- On resume: query processing_history for tasks with status='completed' for the investigation; skip those; retry 'failed' up to max_retries; run 'queued'/'running' (treat stale 'running' as interrupted → reset to queued).
- Checkpoint state stored as JSON in checkpoint_state column.

### Model benchmark (correction 3)

# SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION (SRS)

## Drug Discovery Literature Mining System
**Version:** 1.0  
**Project Type:** Final-Year B.Tech IT Project  
**Category:** Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, NLP and Multi-Agent Systems

---

# 1. Project Overview

## 1.1 Project Description

The Drug Discovery Literature Mining System is a local-first, AI-powered multi-agent research platform designed to automate the discovery, extraction, analysis and interpretation of biomedical scientific literature.

The system will retrieve scientific research papers from public literature databases, process their contents using locally running NLP and language models, extract drug-target relationships, analyze supporting evidence, identify potential research gaps and generate structured scientific research reports.

The system must operate without cloud-based LLM inference services.

## 1.2 Problem Statement

Biomedical researchers must manually search, read and compare large numbers of scientific publications to discover drug-target interactions and identify unexplored research opportunities.

This process is time-consuming and makes it difficult to systematically compare findings across multiple publications.

The proposed system aims to automate this workflow through scientific literature mining, biomedical information extraction, evidence analysis and multi-agent coordination.

## 1.3 Project Objectives

1. Automate scientific literature discovery.
2. Download and organize accessible research papers.
3. Extract biomedical entities such as drugs, genes, proteins and diseases.
4. Identify drug-target relationships and their interaction types.
5. Extract supporting evidence from scientific publications.
6. Compare findings across multiple publications.
7. Identify potential research gaps and contradictory findings.
8. Construct interactive drug-target knowledge graphs.
9. Generate research reports with traceable citations.
10. Perform all AI inference and data processing locally.

---

# 2. System Operating Requirements

## 2.1 Development Environment

Development machine:

- Dell Inspiron 15 3511
- Intel Core i5-1135G7
- 16 GB RAM
- Arch Linux
- Hyprland
- OpenCode coding agent

## 2.2 Execution Environment

Target execution machine:

- ASUS TUF Gaming A17
- AMD Ryzen 5 4600
- NVIDIA GTX 1650, 4 GB VRAM
- 16 GB dual-channel RAM
- Windows 11

The application must be portable between both machines.

## 2.3 Internet Requirements

Internet is permitted exclusively for scientific literature acquisition and associated metadata retrieval.

Permitted:
- PubMed E-utilities.
- Europe PMC REST services.
- Optional additional public scientific literature sources.

Not permitted:
- OpenAI API.
- Gemini API.
- Claude API.
- OpenRouter inference API.
- Any cloud-hosted LLM inference.
- Cloud AI processing services.

All AI inference, NLP processing, agent orchestration, database operations and report generation must run locally.

---

# 3. Proposed Technology Stack

The following is the proposed stack. OpenCode must evaluate compatibility and recommend final versions before implementation.

| Component | Proposed technology |
|---|---|
| Frontend | React |
| UI styling | Tailwind CSS |
| Backend | Python + FastAPI |
| Agent orchestration | LangGraph |
| Local LLM runtime | Ollama |
| Scientific NLP | SciSpaCy |
| General NLP | Transformers |
| Embeddings | Sentence Transformers |
| Vector search | FAISS |
| Database | SQLite |
| PDF processing | PyMuPDF |
| Knowledge graphs | NetworkX |
| Visualization | Plotly |
| Testing | Pytest + frontend testing tools |
| Version control | Git |

The system must have CPU-compatible fallbacks.

Do not assume that every model can run on the GTX 1650. Benchmark model compatibility, VRAM consumption and CPU performance before selecting the final models.

---

# 4. User Requirements

## 4.1 User Input

The user should be able to provide:

- Research question.
- Disease or medical condition.
- Drug name (optional).
- Gene or protein name (optional).
- Publication date range.
- Maximum number of papers.
- Research publication types.
- Full-text preference.
- Research analysis preferences.

Example research question:

"Identify potential drug-target relationships associated with Alzheimer's disease and identify underexplored research areas."

The application should also support a simple mode where the user enters only a research question.

## 4.2 Expected Output

The system should generate:

1. Retrieved scientific paper collection.
2. Paper metadata and abstracts.
3. Extracted biomedical entities.
4. Drug-target relationship dataset.
5. Supporting evidence passages.
6. Contradictory evidence.
7. Drug-target knowledge graph.
8. Potential research gaps.
9. Research summaries.
10. Exportable scientific research report.

---

# 5. Functional Requirements

## FR-01: Literature Discovery

The system shall:

- Search PubMed and Europe PMC.
- Construct search queries from user input.
- Retrieve relevant paper metadata.
- Support publication date filtering.
- Support publication-type filtering.
- Remove duplicate papers.
- Store PMID, DOI, title, authors, abstract and publication date.
- Track source database and retrieval date.

## FR-02: Paper Acquisition

The system shall:

- Download available open-access full-text papers.
- Support PDF imports from the user.
- Support TXT and other useful document formats.
- Respect copyright, licensing and access restrictions.
- Identify unavailable or inaccessible full-text papers.
- Maintain original source references.

Paywalled papers must not be bypassed.

## FR-03: Scientific Document Processing

The system shall:

- Extract text from PDF documents.
- Preserve section information where possible.
- Identify abstract, introduction, methods, results and conclusion.
- Split documents into meaningful text chunks.
- Preserve page and section references.
- Handle extraction errors.

## FR-04: Biomedical Entity Recognition

The system shall identify:

- Drug names.
- Protein names.
- Gene names.
- Diseases.
- Biological pathways.
- Relevant biomedical concepts.

The system must normalize recognized entities where possible and preserve original text.

## FR-05: Relationship Extraction

The system shall identify relationships between biomedical entities.

Supported relationship types:

- Inhibits.
- Activates.
- Binds to.
- Regulates.
- Upregulates.
- Downregulates.
- Associated with.
- Other or unknown.

The system must not treat every association as a confirmed direct molecular interaction.

## FR-06: Evidence Extraction

Every extracted relationship must contain:

- Source paper identifier.
- DOI or PMID when available.
- Exact supporting text.
- Paper section.
- Relationship type.
- Extraction method.
- Confidence score.
- Processing timestamp.

The system must preserve contradictory evidence rather than silently selecting one conclusion.

## FR-07: Drug-Target Analysis

The system shall:

- Aggregate relationships across papers.
- Identify frequently reported relationships.
- Compare supporting and contradicting findings.
- Group relationships by disease, drug and protein.
- Distinguish preclinical and clinical evidence where identifiable.

## FR-08: Research Gap Identification

The system shall identify candidate research gaps through:

- Low literature coverage.
- Conflicting findings.
- Limited experimental evidence.
- Missing validation.
- Underexplored drug-target combinations.
- Changes in research trends over time.

Research gaps must be evidence-based.

A missing relationship in the collected papers must never be presented as proof that no research exists globally.

Each gap must include its supporting reasoning, literature coverage and limitations.

## FR-09: Knowledge Graph

The system shall create an interactive graph containing:

- Drug nodes.
- Protein nodes.
- Gene nodes.
- Disease nodes.
- Relationship edges.
- Evidence references.

Users should be able to inspect individual nodes and relationships.

## FR-10: Report Generation

The system shall generate research reports containing:

1. Research question.
2. Search methodology.
3. Literature collection statistics.
4. Identified drugs.
5. Identified proteins and genes.
6. Extracted relationships.
7. Supporting evidence.
8. Contradictory findings.
9. Potential research gaps.
10. Limitations.
11. References.

Supported export formats:

- PDF.
- CSV.
- JSON.

---

# 6. Multi-Agent Architecture

The system should use one research coordinator and five specialized agents.

## Agent 1: Literature Discovery Agent

Responsibilities:

- Interpret research queries.
- Generate search keywords.
- Search supported literature databases.
- Retrieve paper metadata.
- Remove duplicates.
- Organize retrieved papers.

Output: Structured literature collection.

## Agent 2: Biomedical Extraction Agent

Responsibilities:

- Process scientific papers.
- Extract biomedical entities.
- Normalize drug, gene and protein names.
- Identify candidate relationships.
- Preserve supporting text.

Output: Structured biomedical entities and candidate relationships.

## Agent 3: Evidence Analysis Agent

Responsibilities:

- Validate extracted evidence against source passages.
- Compare findings across publications.
- Identify contradictory findings.
- Categorize evidence types.
- Preserve uncertainty.

Output: Evidence matrix.

## Agent 4: Research Gap Agent

Responsibilities:

- Analyze literature coverage.
- Identify underexplored relationships.
- Detect conflicting results.
- Identify evidence limitations.
- Rank potential research gaps using transparent criteria.

Output: Candidate research gaps with explanations and references.

## Agent 5: Research Report Agent

Responsibilities:

- Consolidate findings.
- Generate structured summaries.
- Prepare research reports.
- Include citations.
- Include limitations and confidence information.

Output: Final research report.

## Research Coordinator

The coordinator shall:

- Manage agent execution.
- Pass structured data between agents.
- Track execution status.
- Handle failures.
- Prevent duplicate processing.
- Maintain investigation history.
- Support restarting interrupted workflows.

Agents should be modular. They may share one local LLM while using specialized prompts, tools and deterministic Python processing.

### 2.1 Objectives (SRS 1.3)
Ten objectives, all local-first: literature discovery; paper download/organisation; biomedical entity extraction (drugs, genes, proteins, diseases); drug-target relationship extraction; evidence extraction; cross-publication comparison; research-gap and contradiction identification; interactive knowledge graphs; traceable research reports; 100% local AI inference.

Permitted: PubMed E-utilities, Europe PMC REST, optional public scientific sources.
