- **FR-02 Paper Acquisition:** open-access full-text download, user PDF/TXT import, copyright/licence respect, paywalled-paper identification (must not bypass paywalls), source reference maintenance.
- **FR-03 Document Processing:** PDF text extraction, section preservation (abstract/introduction/methods/results/conclusion), chunking with page/section references, error handling.
- **FR-04 Entity Recognition:** drugs, proteins, genes, diseases, pathways, concepts; normalisation where possible; preserve original text.
- **FR-05 Relationship Extraction:** inhibits/activates/binds_to/regulates/upregulates/downregulates/associated_with/other; association ≠ direct interaction. Detect negation, uncertainty, speculation and experimental context.

- **FR-08 Research Gap Identification:** low coverage, conflicting findings, limited evidence, missing validation, underexplored combinations, trend changes. Gaps evidence-based; corpus-relative (absence ≠ proof of no global research); deterministic, explainable ranking; reasoning + coverage + limitations per gap.
- **FR-09 Knowledge Graph:** drug/protein/gene/disease nodes, relationship edges, evidence references; node/edge inspection.

Coordinator + 5 agents (Literature Discovery, Biomedical Extraction, Evidence Analysis, Research Gap, Research Report). LangGraph with lightweight state-machine fallback. SQLite, ≥3NF, investigation-level isolation enforced at the schema level (composite foreign keys), reliable transaction handling, provenance-first, contradiction-safe. ---

## 3. Missing, Ambiguous, or Technically Unrealistic Requirements

| # | Area | Issue | Recommended Revision |
|---|------|-------|----------------------|
| A-1 | LLMs / hardware | SRS names no model, context window, or quantisation for Ollama on GTX 1650 (4 GB VRAM). | Benchmark Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama-3.2-1B (GGUF Q4_K_M) at a defined milestone before model lock-in. Model must fit ≤3 GB VRAM or run on CPU. No benchmark results invented; no accuracy claims until measured. |
| A-2 | Evidence validation | "Validate evidence against source passages" is probabilistic with a local LLM. | Reframe as "cross-check candidate evidence against source passages; every relationship must carry an exact, verifiable source passage; flag low-confidence matches". Never present LLM output as ground truth. |
| A-3 | Research gaps | Absence in collected papers is not proof of no global research. | Gaps are candidate gaps within the retrieved corpus, labelled corpus-relative with coverage and limitations. Ranking is deterministic and explainable; LLM writes descriptions only, never invents scores. |
| A-4 | Preclinical vs clinical | No method specified for distinguishing evidence types. | Deterministic heuristic (section + keyword: animal/cell/in vitro vs clinical trial/patient) + LLM-assisted classification with low confidence when uncertain. |
| A-5 | Full-text availability | Most PubMed papers paywalled/abstract-only. | Process whatever full text is obtainable; mark papers metadata-only / abstract-only / full-text. |
| A-6 | Entity normalisation | No authority specified. | Stable biomedical entity identifiers + synonym normalisation; best-effort external IDs (NCBI Gene/UniProt/DrugBank via permitted internet); otherwise normalized_name/stable_identifier nullable. |
| A-7 | LangGraph | Offline/Windows compatibility unknown; version-pin. | LangGraph with lightweight Python state-machine fallback. |
| A-8 | PDF security | Malicious PDFs can trigger parser bugs. | Isolated subprocess parsing with timeout, resource limits, magic-byte validation, size cap, embedded-JS scan; treat paper text as untrusted (prompt injection). |
| A-9 | Evaluation dataset | No source or size specified. | Manually annotated dataset (size determined by project owner; initially 50–100 papers) with gold-standard entities/relationships. |
| A-10 | Report export | PDF export needs a library. | ReportLab (server-side); pin the library. |

---

## 4. Requirements Requiring Project-Owner Decision

1. Final local LLM model after benchmarking (Qwen2.5-1.5B vs Llama-3.2-1B; see MODEL_SELECTION.md).
2. LangGraph vs custom state machine (primary/fallback).
3. Annotated evaluation dataset scope (size, source, annotator).
4. PDF export library (ReportLab selected; confirm).
5. Any literature source beyond PubMed + Europe PMC.
6. Maximum corpus size per investigation (initial configurable max: 100 papers).
7. Whether software dependencies and model weights may be downloaded as one-time setup or must be transferred offline (see DEPLOYMENT_PLAN.md §4).

---

## 5. Adopted Design Decisions (from project owner / review corrections)

- Benchmark **Qwen2.5-1.5B** and **Llama-3.2-1B** (GGUF Q4_K_M); actual benchmarking is a defined milestone gate, not part of M0.
- **LangGraph** with lightweight **state-machine fallback**.
- **ReportLab** for PDF generation.
- **PubMed + Europe PMC** as initial literature sources.
- Initial configurable maximum **100 papers per investigation**.
- Negation, uncertainty, speculation and experimental-context detection in relationship extraction.
- Every relationship carries an exact, verifiable source passage + hash.
- Stable biomedical entity identifiers + synonym normalisation.
- Deterministic, explainable research-gap ranking (LLM writes descriptions, never invents scores).
- Investigation-level data isolation enforced at the SQLite schema level (composite foreign keys).
- Durable task/checkpoint storage with idempotency keys; resume without duplicating completed work.
- Prefer deterministic Python processing; avoid unnecessary LLM calls/agents.
- Software dependencies and model weights: one-time setup download permitted; offline transfer required for air-gapped production (DEPLOYMENT_PLAN.md §4).

# Database Design — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.1 (planning, revised)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written  
**Planned location:** `/home/user/docs/DATABASE_DESIGN.md`  
**Consistent with:** SRS.md §7, SRS_ANALYSIS.md §2.6, ARCHITECTURE.md, AGENT_SPECIFICATION.md, DATA_PIPELINE.md

---

## 1. Design Principles

- **SQLite** — single local relational DB, file-based, portable, no server.
- **Investigation-level isolation enforced at the schema level:** every core entity carries `investigation_id` NOT NULL; composite foreign keys guarantee relationships, mentions, evidence and gap references can never cross investigations. Isolation is a database constraint, not merely an application-query assumption.
- **Same PMID/DOI allowed in different investigations:** uniqueness of PMID/DOI is scoped per investigation (`UNIQUE(pmid, investigation_id)`, `UNIQUE(doi, investigation_id)`), not global. A paper may be retrieved under multiple investigations.
- **Reliable transaction handling:** multi-statement writes wrapped in explicit transactions; `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` and `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` on every connection.
- **Fully normalised** to ≥3NF; junction tables for many-to-many.
- **Provenance-first:** every extracted fact links to paper, section, page/chunk, extraction method, timestamp, confidence.
- **Contradiction-safe:** relationships and evidence are never soft-deleted or overwritten to "pick a winner"; contradictory rows coexist.
- **Cross-platform:** relative, configurable paths; no machine-specific absolute paths.
- **Migratable:** versioned SQL migration files applied at startup within a transaction.

---

## 2. Entity-Relationship Summary

```
investigation 1:N paper
investigation 1:N paper_section (via paper)
investigation 1:N paper_chunk (via paper)
investigation 1:N entity
investigation 1:N entity_synonym (via entity)
investigation 1:N paper_entity_mention (via paper and entity)
investigation 1:N relationship (via source and target entities)
investigation 1:N evidence (via relationship and paper)
investigation 1:N research_gap
investigation 1:N gap_supporting_evidence (via gap and evidence)
investigation 1:N processing_history
```

Composite foreign key rule: every child table references its parent through `(parent_id, investigation_id)`. Because each parent's primary key makes `(id, investigation_id)` unique, SQLite composite foreign keys are valid and enforce isolation at storage time.

---

## 3. Schema Specification

### 3.1 Core tables

**investigations** (isolation root)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| investigation_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| research_question | TEXT | NOT NULL | |
| search_parameters | TEXT | NOT NULL | JSON: disease, drug, gene, date range, max_papers (default 100), publication types, full-text pref |
| status | TEXT | NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued' | queued/running/completed/failed/partial |
| created_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |
| updated_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |

**papers** (scoped per investigation; PMID/DOI unique within an investigation only)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| paper_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL, FK → investigations | isolation |
| pmid | TEXT | nullable | PubMed ID |
| doi | TEXT | nullable | |
| title | TEXT | NOT NULL | |
| authors | TEXT | | JSON array |
| abstract | TEXT | | |
| publication_date | TEXT | | ISO-8601 or year |
| source | TEXT | NOT NULL | pubmed/europepmc/user_import |
| full_text_path | TEXT | | relative path under storage root |
| access_status | TEXT | NOT NULL | open_access/abstract_only/paywalled/user_import/unavailable |
| retrieved_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |
| source_database | TEXT | NOT NULL | |
| UNIQUE (pmid, investigation_id) | | WHERE pmid IS NOT NULL | same PMID allowed across investigations |
| UNIQUE (doi, investigation_id) | | WHERE doi IS NOT NULL | same DOI allowed across investigations |
| FK (investigation_id) | | REFERENCES investigations | |

**paper_sections** (section boundaries within a paper)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| section_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| paper_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | isolation |
| section_name | TEXT | NOT NULL | abstract/introduction/methods/results/conclusion/other |
| section_order | INTEGER | | position in paper |
| page_start | INTEGER | | |
| page_end | INTEGER | | |
| FK (paper_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES papers | composite |

**paper_chunks** (persistent chunk storage; clarification 6)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| chunk_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| paper_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | isolation |
| section_id | INTEGER | nullable | FK to paper_sections |
| chunk_text | TEXT | NOT NULL | extracted chunk text |
| chunk_order | INTEGER | NOT NULL | order within paper |
| page_start | INTEGER | | |
| page_end | INTEGER | | |
| token_count | INTEGER | | approximate token count |
| FK (paper_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES papers | composite |
| FK (section_id, paper_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES paper_sections | composite, nullable section |

Relationship to `paper_sections` and `paper_entity_mentions`: a chunk belongs to one paper and (optionally) one section. `paper_entity_mentions.chunk_id` references `paper_chunks.chunk_id`, so every entity mention is anchored to a persistent chunk with page/section provenance.

**entities** (stable identifiers; clarification 6 normalisation)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| entity_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL, FK → investigations | isolation |
| normalized_name | TEXT | nullable | canonical normalised name |
| entity_type | TEXT | NOT NULL | drug/protein/gene/disease/pathway/concept/other |
| stable_identifier | TEXT | nullable | stable biomedical ID (UniProt, NCBI Gene, DrugBank) |
| stable_identifier_source | TEXT | nullable | authority of stable_identifier |
| UNIQUE (normalized_name, investigation_id) | | WHERE normalized_name IS NOT NULL | same normalised name allowed across investigations |
| FK (investigation_id) | | REFERENCES investigations | |

**entity_synonyms** (synonym normalisation)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| synonym_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| entity_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | isolation |
| synonym | TEXT | NOT NULL | observed synonym / original mention |
| source | TEXT | nullable | where synonym observed |
| FK (entity_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES entities | composite |

**paper_entity_mentions** (where an entity appears in a paper)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| mention_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| paper_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | isolation |
| section_id | INTEGER | nullable | |
| entity_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | |
| chunk_id | INTEGER | nullable | FK to paper_chunks |
| entity_name_original | TEXT | NOT NULL | exact text as it appears |
| page_number | INTEGER | | |
| FK (paper_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES papers | composite |
| FK (entity_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES entities | composite |
| FK (chunk_id) | | REFERENCES paper_chunks | |
| FK (section_id, paper_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES paper_sections | composite, nullable |

**relationships** (every row carries an exact, verifiable source passage; FR-05/FR-06)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| relationship_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL, FK → investigations | isolation |
| source_entity_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | |
| target_entity_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | |
| relationship_type | TEXT | NOT NULL | inhibits/activates/binds_to/regulates/upregulates/downregulates/associated_with/other |
| confidence_score | REAL | NOT NULL | 0.0–1.0 |
| extraction_method | TEXT | NOT NULL | llm/rule/hybrid |
| is_direct_interaction | INTEGER | NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 | 0=association only, 1=direct molecular interaction claimed |
| negation | INTEGER | NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 | 1 = relationship is negated (e.g. "does not inhibit") |
| uncertainty | INTEGER | NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 | 1 = uncertain language (e.g. "may", "suggests") |
| speculation | INTEGER | NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 | 1 = speculative language (e.g. "potential", "hypothesized") |
| experimental_context | TEXT | | in_vitro/in_vivo/animal/cell_line/clinical/unknown |
| source_passage | TEXT | NOT NULL | exact, verifiable verbatim passage from source |
| source_passage_hash | TEXT | NOT NULL | SHA-256 of source_passage for verification |
| created_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |
| FK (investigation_id) | | REFERENCES investigations | |
| FK (source_entity_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES entities | composite |
| FK (target_entity_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES entities | composite |

**evidence** (provenance for each relationship; FR-06)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| evidence_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| relationship_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | isolation |
| paper_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | |
| section_id | INTEGER | nullable | |
| supporting_text | TEXT | NOT NULL | exact supporting passage |
| page_number | INTEGER | | |
| evidence_type | TEXT | | experimental/computational/review/clinical/other |
| extraction_method | TEXT | NOT NULL | |
| confidence_score | REAL | NOT NULL | 0.0–1.0 |
| extracted_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |
| FK (relationship_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES relationships | composite |
| FK (paper_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES papers | composite |
| FK (section_id, paper_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES paper_sections | composite, nullable |

**research_gaps** (deterministic, explainable ranking; clarification 8)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| gap_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL, FK → investigations | isolation |
| gap_description | TEXT | NOT NULL | LLM-generated description only |
| gap_category | TEXT | NOT NULL | low_coverage/conflicting_findings/limited_evidence/missing_validation/underexplored_combination/trend_change |
| ranking_score | REAL | NOT NULL | 0.0–1.0, deterministic, computed in Python — LLM never invents |
| ranking_criteria | TEXT | NOT NULL | JSON documenting deterministic inputs + weights used |
| literature_coverage | TEXT | | summary of papers found |
| limitations | TEXT | NOT NULL | why this is a candidate, not proof |
| supporting_reasoning | TEXT | NOT NULL | LLM-generated reasoning |
| created_at | TEXT | NOT NULL | ISO-8601 UTC |
| FK (investigation_id) | | REFERENCES investigations | |

**gap_supporting_evidence** (junction; cannot cross investigations)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| gap_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | |
| evidence_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL | isolation |
| PRIMARY KEY (gap_id, evidence_id) | | | |
| FK (gap_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES research_gaps | composite |
| FK (evidence_id, investigation_id) | | REFERENCES evidence | composite |

**processing_history** (durable task/checkpoint storage; correction 2)
| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| task_id | INTEGER | PK, AUTOINCREMENT | |
| investigation_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL, FK → investigations | isolation |
| agent_name | TEXT | NOT NULL | |
| task_key | TEXT | NOT NULL | idempotency key, e.g. "agent2:paper:{paper_id}" |
| status | TEXT | NOT NULL | queued/running/completed/failed/skipped |
| inputs | TEXT | | JSON task inputs |
| outputs | TEXT | | JSON task outputs |
| checkpoint_state | TEXT | | JSON resumable checkpoint state |
| started_at | TEXT | | |
| completed_at | TEXT | | |
| execution_time_seconds | REAL | | |
| error_details | TEXT | | JSON error info |
| retry_count | INTEGER | NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 | |
| max_retries | INTEGER | NOT NULL DEFAULT 3 | |
| FK (investigation_id) | | REFERENCES investigations | |

### 3.2 Indexes

```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_investigation ON papers(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_pmid ON papers(pmid, investigation_id) WHERE pmid IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_papers_doi ON papers(doi, investigation_id) WHERE doi IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_sections_paper ON paper_sections(paper_id, investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_chunks_paper ON paper_chunks(paper_id, investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_entities_investigation ON entities(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_entities_type ON entities(entity_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_mentions_paper ON paper_entity_mentions(paper_id, investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_mentions_entity ON paper_entity_mentions(entity_id, investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_mentions_chunk ON paper_entity_mentions(chunk_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_investigation ON relationships(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_entities ON relationships(source_entity_id, target_entity_id, investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_relationships_type ON relationships(relationship_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_evidence_relationship ON evidence(relationship_id, investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_evidence_paper ON evidence(paper_id, investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_gaps_investigation ON research_gaps(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_history_investigation ON processing_history(investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_history_task_key ON processing_history(task_key, investigation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_history_agent ON processing_history(agent_name);
```

### 3.3 Foreign Keys & Transactions
`PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;` on every connection. `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;` for concurrent read safety. Composite FKs reference `(parent_id, investigation_id)` pairs. `ON DELETE CASCADE` only where semantically safe (e.g., paper_entity_mentions → papers; evidence → relationships; investigations → gaps/papers/history/chunks/sections/mentions/entities). Multi-table writes (e.g., relationship + its evidence) executed in a single `BEGIN…COMMIT` transaction.

---

## 4. Migration Strategy
- Versioned SQL in `db/migrations/`: `V001__initial_schema.sql`, `V002__...`, etc.
- `schema_version` table: `CREATE TABLE schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL);`
- Startup applies pending migrations in order within a single transaction.
- No automated rollbacks; destructive migrations require a SQLite backup first.
- Raw SQL (no Alembic) — small, auditable surface.

---

## 5. Data Retention & Portability
- SQLite file + `data/` storage root relocatable; paths relative to configurable `DDS_DATA_DIR`.
- Backups = copy SQLite file + data folder (safe when app stopped).
- No cloud sync; DB never leaves local machine.

---

## 6. Schema Gaps to Confirm
- Authors normalised into separate table? Deferred — JSON array acceptable for v1.
- stable_identifier lookups best-effort given permitted-internet limits; nullable.

# System Architecture — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.1 (planning, revised)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written  
**Planned location:** `/home/user/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`  
**Consistent with:** SRS.md, SRS_ANALYSIS.md, DATABASE_DESIGN.md, AGENT_SPECIFICATION.md, DATA_PIPELINE.md, DEPLOYMENT_PLAN.md

---

## 1. Architectural Goals

- **Local-first:** all inference, NLP, orchestration, storage, reporting run on the user's machine. No cloud LLM APIs.
- **Portable:** identical codebase on Arch Linux (dev) and Windows 11 (target ASUS).
- **Modular:** agents, NLP stages, data sources, exporters independently replaceable.
- **Resource-bounded:** 16 GB RAM, 4 GB VRAM GPU; single model loaded at a time; CPU fallback everywhere.
- **Scientifically sound:** full provenance, confidence scores, contradiction preservation, no unsupported clinical claims.
- **Investigation-isolated:** all data scoped to an investigation_id; isolation enforced at the SQLite schema level (composite foreign keys), not merely by application queries.
- **Durable recovery:** persistent task/checkpoint storage with idempotency keys; interrupted investigations resume without duplicating completed work.
- **Deterministic-first:** prefer deterministic Python over LLM calls where sufficient; avoid unnecessary LLM invocations.
- **Secure document handling:** isolated PDF parsing with subprocess timeouts, resource limits, and safe file handling.

---

## 2. High-Level Architecture (three-tier local)

```
TIER 3 — FRONTEND (React + Tailwind + Plotly)
   Dashboard, investigation creation, result browsing, graph viz, upload, exports
          HTTP / JSON (REST API)
TIER 2 — BACKEND (Python + FastAPI)
   API routers | Coordinator (LangGraph, state-machine fallback) | 5 agents
   NLP service wrappers | SQLite (investigation-isolated, transactions, WAL) | file/storage
          Local file system
   SQLite DB | PDFs/TXTs | reports | Ollama GGUF models
TIER 1 — LOCAL RUNTIMES
   Ollama (local LLM) | Python venv | Node.js (frontend build)
```

### Tier responsibilities
- **Frontend:** UI only; talks to FastAPI backend over HTTP.
- **Backend:** REST API, validation, job queue, agent orchestration via coordinator, NLP wrappers, DB access, file storage, report assembly.
- **Local runtimes:** Ollama serves the LLM on `http://localhost:11434` (configurable). Backend calls Ollama REST — never cloud. Python hosts FastAPI, LangGraph (or fallback state machine), SciSpaCy, Transformers, Sentence-Transformers, FAISS, PyMuPDF, NetworkX.

---

## 3. Component Diagram (logical)

```
User input -> FastAPI API -> Coordinator (LangGraph / state-machine fallback)
   |                 |                         |
   v                 v                         v
 SQLite DB    Agent 2: Bio Extraction      Agent 1: Lit Discovery
                     |                         |
                     v                         v
               Agent 3: Evidence          Agent 4: Gap Analysis
               Agent 5: Report            Agent 1..5 share 1 Ollama LLM
                     |
               File system (PDFs, reports)
```

- Agents read/write SQLite; coordinator owns the state machine and durable task/checkpoint storage.
- LLM calls via Ollama; deterministic NLP (SciSpaCy, PyMuPDF, NetworkX, FAISS) in-process.
- One LLM loaded at a time; reused across agents via different prompts.

---

## 4. Layered Backend Design

| Layer | Responsibility | Technologies |
|---|---|---|
| API layer | REST endpoints, validation, progress streaming | FastAPI, Pydantic |
| Orchestration | Investigation lifecycle, sequencing, retries, checkpoints, durable task storage | LangGraph (or state-machine fallback), SQLite processing_history |
| Agent layer | Five agents with prompts + deterministic tools | Ollama client, SciSpaCy, Transformers |
| NLP services | PDF extraction, chunking, NER, RE, embeddings, vector search | PyMuPDF, SciSpaCy, Sentence-Transformers, FAISS |
| Analytics | Knowledge graph, gap ranking, contradiction detection | NetworkX, Plotly data prep, deterministic Python |
| Data layer | SQLite access, migrations, storage paths, investigation isolation | sqlite3 (stdlib), file storage |
| Report layer | PDF/CSV/JSON assembly with citations | ReportLab (server-side), csv/json |

### Single-model constraint
Only one LLM served by Ollama at a time; reused across agents via different prompts. Embedding/NER models are smaller; not loaded simultaneously with a large LLM if memory constrained.

### Deterministic-first principle
Relationship-type hints, negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental-context flags, section detection, deduplication, coverage counts, conflict detection and gap ranking scores are computed deterministically in Python where possible. The LLM is used only for disambiguation and narrative descriptions — never to invent ranking scores.

### Investigation isolation
Every write is scoped to an `investigation_id`. Composite foreign keys in SQLite prevent relationships, mentions, evidence and gap references from crossing investigations. The same PMID/DOI may appear in different investigations (uniqueness scoped per investigation).

### Durable workflow recovery (correction 2)
- Persistent task/checkpoint storage in `processing_history` (DATABASE_DESIGN §3.1): each task stores `task_key` (idempotency key), `status`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `checkpoint_state` (JSON), `retry_count`, `max_retries`, timestamps.
- A custom SQLite task/checkpoint schema is the source of truth for recovery (LangGraph SQLite checkpointing is not required; LangGraph may be used for orchestration but recovery is driven by the custom schema).
- Resume semantics: on investigation restart, query `processing_history` for the investigation; tasks with `status='completed'` are skipped (idempotent, not re-run); `failed` tasks retried up to `max_retries`; stale `running` tasks (interrupted) reset to `queued`; `queued` tasks run. Completed work is never duplicated.

---

## 5. End-to-End Data Flow (logical)

1. User creates investigation (question + params) → API → coordinator creates investigation record (`queued`, investigation_id).
2. Coordinator enqueues Agent 1 (task_key `agent1:discover:{investigation_id}`).
3. Agent 1 builds queries, calls PubMed/Europe PMC, deduplicates, stores paper metadata scoped to investigation_id.
4. Coordinator enqueues download/processing per paper (FR-02, FR-03), task keys `agent2:process:{paper_id}`.
5. Agent 2: extract text → chunk (persist to `paper_chunks`) → section detection → NER → stable identifiers + synonym normalisation → candidate relationships (negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental context) → every relationship gets an exact, verifiable source passage + hash.
6. Agent 3: verbatim passage verification → compare across papers → contradictions (explicit mapping, clarification 7) → evidence matrix.
7. Agent 4: coverage → deterministic, explainable gap ranking (Python; LLM writes description only) → research gaps.
8. Agent 5: consolidate → report (JSON/CSV/PDF via ReportLab).
9. Frontend polls progress; user browses and exports.

Each stage writes SQLite within a transaction scoped to investigation_id and emits progress events. Failed stages retry/resume from checkpoint (processing_history).

---

## 6. Cross-Cutting Design Decisions

### 6.1 No cloud inference
Ollama local; GGUF model files on local disk; Ollama client at `127.0.0.1:11434` (env-configurable). No OpenAI/Gemini/Claude/OpenRouter keys accepted or stored.

### 6.2 Database as integration point + investigation isolation
Agents communicate via shared SQLite state, not direct calls. Every core table carries `investigation_id`; composite FKs enforce isolation. Transactions wrap multi-statement writes.

### 6.3 Untrusted document handling (PDF security, clarification 10)
- PDFs/TXTs stored outside the web root, validated by magic bytes (`%PDF-`) + size limit before parsing.
- Isolated parsing: PyMuPDF extraction runs in a single subprocess with a hard timeout and resource limits (memory/CPU); subprocess is killed on hang.
- Embedded JavaScript/actions scanned before parsing; files with active content rejected or sanitised.
- No shell execution of downloaded document content.
- Paper contents treated as untrusted input in prompts (system-message isolation; no raw paper text reflected unsanitised to the user).
- Upload validation: file type, size, extension checks.

### 6.4 Memory management
Documents streamed/chunked; full text never loaded at once; FAISS index per-investigation, discardable after completion; per-paper progress events keep UI responsive; single model at a time.

### 6.5 Portability
No machine-specific absolute paths; storage root configurable via `DDS_DATA_DIR` (default `./data`); SQLite file-based and portable; deps pinned in `requirements.txt` / `package.json`; GPU vs CPU is a config flag.

---

## 7. Architectural Revisions
- If LangGraph cannot run offline on Windows 11 → lightweight deterministic Python state machine (same interfaces).
- PDF export library = ReportLab (server-side), pinned.

# Agent Specification — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.1 (planning, revised)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written  
**Planned location:** `/home/user/docs/AGENT_SPECIFICATION.md`  
**Consistent with:** SRS.md §6, SRS_ANALYSIS.md §2.5, ARCHITECTURE.md, DATABASE_DESIGN.md, DATA_PIPELINE.md

---

## 1. Orchestration Model

- **Research Coordinator** (LangGraph primary, lightweight Python state-machine fallback): owns investigation lifecycle, agent sequencing, state, retries, checkpoints, duplicate prevention, history, restart. All state and outputs scoped to `investigation_id` (investigation-level isolation enforced at the SQLite schema level, per DATABASE_DESIGN.md).
- **Agents communicate via shared SQLite**, not direct calls. Each agent reads inputs from DB, writes outputs to DB within a transaction, records `processing_history`.
- **One shared local LLM** (Ollama) across agents, specialised prompts per agent; deterministic Python post-processing where possible.
- **Deterministic-first:** section detection, deduplication, negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental-context flags, coverage counts, conflict detection and gap ranking scores computed in Python where sufficient; LLM used only for disambiguation and narrative descriptions. Avoid unnecessary LLM calls/agents.

---

## 2. Durable Workflow Recovery (correction 2)

### Persistent task and checkpoint storage
Recovery is driven by a **custom SQLite task/checkpoint schema** (`processing_history`, DATABASE_DESIGN §3.1), which is the source of truth. LangGraph may be used for orchestration, but recovery does not depend on LangGraph checkpointing.

Each task row stores:
- `task_key` — idempotency key, e.g. `agent1:discover:{investigation_id}` or `agent2:process:{paper_id}`. Guarantees a logical unit of work is processed at most once per investigation.
- `status` — queued/running/completed/failed/skipped.
- `inputs` — JSON task inputs.
- `outputs` — JSON task outputs.
- `checkpoint_state` — JSON resumable checkpoint state (e.g., papers already processed, next page cursor, last completed chunk).
- `retry_count` / `max_retries` — retry budget.
- `started_at` / `completed_at` / `execution_time_seconds` — timing.
- `error_details` — JSON error info for failed tasks.

### Resume without duplicating completed work
On investigation restart or after an interruption:
1. Query `processing_history` for all tasks of the `investigation_id`.
2. Tasks with `status='completed'` are **skipped** (idempotent; outputs already persisted).
3. Tasks with `status='failed'` and `retry_count < max_retries` are retried.
4. Tasks with `status='failed'` and `retry_count >= max_retries` are marked `skipped` and the investigation continues with remaining work.
5. Stale `status='running'` tasks (interrupted mid-execution) are reset to `queued` and re-run from their checkpoint state.
6. Tasks with `status='queued'` are run in order.

Because every agent writes outputs to SQLite within a transaction scoped to `investigation_id`, resuming never duplicates completed relationships, mentions, evidence, or gaps. Composite foreign keys further guarantee no cross-investigation contamination.

---

## 3. State Schema (coordinator)

`{ investigation_id, status, current_agent, papers[], entities[], relationships[], evidence[], gaps[], errors[], retry_counts, checkpoints, max_papers }` — all keyed by `investigation_id`. Checkpoints persisted to `processing_history.checkpoint_state`.

---

## 4. Agent 1 — Literature Discovery

**Inputs:** investigation research question + search parameters (disease, drug, gene, date range, max_papers ≤ 100 configurable, publication types, full-text preference).
**Responsibilities:** interpret query; generate search keywords (Boolean, MeSH-aware); call PubMed E-utilities + Europe PMC REST; retrieve metadata (PMID, DOI, title, authors, abstract, date); deduplicate by PMID/DOI/normalized title (deduplication scoped per investigation — same PMID may appear in different investigations); store source DB + retrieval date; mark access_status (open_access/abstract_only/paywalled/unavailable).
**Outputs:** paper metadata rows scoped to investigation_id.
**Deterministic:** query construction, deduplication, metadata normalisation. **LLM:** keyword generation from research question (optional; can be rule-based).
**Failure:** API rate limits → backoff/retry; one DB down → use the other; empty result → flag to user.

---

## 5. Agent 2 — Biomedical Extraction

**Inputs:** paper list from Agent 1; full-text paths (open-access downloads + user imports).
**Responsibilities:** extract PDF/TXT text (PyMuPDF, isolated subprocess per ARCHITECTURE §6.3); preserve sections (abstract/intro/methods/results/conclusion); persist chunks to `paper_chunks` (clarification 6) with page/section references; chunk text with page/section refs; NER (SciSpaCy) for drugs, proteins, genes, diseases, pathways; stable biomedical identifiers + synonym normalisation (store original + normalized); identify candidate relationships.
**Relationship extraction (required detection):**
- relationship type: inhibits/activates/binds_to/regulates/upregulates/downregulates/associated_with/other
- negation (e.g., "does not inhibit")
- uncertainty (e.g., "may", "suggests", "could")
- speculation (e.g., "potential", "hypothesized")
- experimental context (in vitro / in vivo / animal / cell line / clinical / unknown)
**Every relationship must carry an exact, verifiable source passage** (verbatim span from source text) + `source_passage_hash` (SHA-256) for verification. Association ≠ direct interaction (`is_direct_interaction` flag).
**Outputs:** entities, entity_synonyms, entity mentions, candidate relationships scoped to investigation_id.
**Deterministic:** PDF extraction, chunking, section detection, SciSpaCy NER, normalisation lookup, context-flag heuristics. **LLM:** relationship-type disambiguation, direct-vs-association, confidence-scoring assistance.
**Security:** paper text treated as untrusted; prompt-injection mitigations; size/time limits on extraction; isolated PDF parsing.
**Failure:** corrupted PDF → extraction_failed flag, continue; abstract-only papers → NER from abstract only, flagged.

---

## 6. Agent 3 — Evidence Analysis

**Inputs:** candidate relationships + source passages from Agent 2.
**Responsibilities:** cross-check candidate evidence against source passages (verbatim span verification via `source_passage_hash`); compare findings across publications; identify contradictory findings using the **explicit contradiction mapping** (clarification 7); categorise evidence types (experimental/computational/review/clinical); preserve uncertainty (low confidence, conflicting).
**Outputs:** evidence matrix scoped to investigation_id (provenance, confidence, type).
**Deterministic:** passage-span verification, contradiction detection (per mapping below), evidence categorisation heuristics. **LLM:** passage-relationship validation, confidence scoring.
**Contradiction handling:** both supporting and contradicting rows stored; no silent selection of one conclusion.

### Explicit contradiction mapping (clarification 7)
Two relationships for the same `(source_entity, target_entity)` pair are classified **contradictory** only when ALL of the following hold:
1. One relationship has a **positive** type (activates / binds_to / upregulates) and the other has a **negative** type (inhibits / downregulates), OR vice versa.
2. Neither relationship has `negation = 1` (a negated relationship is not treated as a contradictory positive claim).
3. Experimental contexts are compatible: both are `in_vitro`, both `clinical`, both `in_vivo`, both `animal`, both `cell_line`, or at least one is `unknown`. If contexts are explicitly different (e.g., `in_vitro` vs `clinical`), the pair is flagged **context-divergent**, not contradictory.

Relationships of different types that are **not** contradictory: e.g., `binds_to` vs `regulates` (different specificity, not opposite); `associated_with` vs `inhibits` (association ≠ direct interaction). Negation and experimental context are accounted for before a contradiction is declared.

---

## 7. Agent 4 — Research Gap

**Inputs:** aggregated relationships + evidence matrix from Agent 3.
**Responsibilities:** analyse literature coverage per drug-target-disease; identify underexplored relationships; detect conflicting results (per contradiction mapping); identify evidence limitations; rank candidate gaps using transparent, deterministic criteria.
**Deterministic research-gap scoring formula (clarification 8):**
The `ranking_score` (0.0–1.0) is computed entirely in Python; the LLM is completely outside score calculation. The LLM writes `gap_description` and `supporting_reasoning` only, and never invents or adjusts `ranking_score`.

```
ranking_score = w_coverage * coverage_score
              + w_conflict * conflict_score
              + w_evidence * evidence_score
              + w_recency  * recency_score
```

Weights (documented, sum to 1.0): `w_coverage = 0.40`, `w_conflict = 0.30`, `w_evidence = 0.20`, `w_recency = 0.10`.

Input normalization (each component scaled to 0.0–1.0):
- `coverage_score = 1.0 - min(paper_count_for_pair, coverage_cap) / coverage_cap`, where `coverage_cap = 20`. Fewer papers on a drug-target-disease pair → higher gap score (0 papers → 1.0).
- `conflict_score = 1.0` if at least one contradictory pair exists for the relationship, else `0.0`.
- `evidence_score = 1.0 - avg_confidence_of_relationships`. Lower average extraction confidence → higher gap score.
- `recency_score = 1.0 - (years_since_most_recent_paper / recency_cap)`, capped at [0,1], `recency_cap = 5`. Stale relationships → higher gap score.

`ranking_criteria` (stored as JSON) documents the exact inputs, weights, and caps used so the score is reproducible and explainable. Each gap also carries `literature_coverage`, `limitations`, and `supporting_reasoning`. Gaps are corpus-relative: absence in collected papers ≠ proof of no global research.

**Outputs:** research gaps scoped to investigation_id, each with gap_category, ranking_score, ranking_criteria (JSON), literature_coverage, limitations, supporting_reasoning, gap_supporting_evidence references.

---

## 8. Agent 5 — Research Report

**Inputs:** all prior agent outputs for an investigation.
**Responsibilities:** consolidate findings; generate structured summaries; prepare report with citations; include limitations + confidence info.
**Outputs:** final report (JSON/CSV/PDF via ReportLab).
**Contents:** research question, search methodology, literature stats, identified drugs, proteins/genes, relationships, supporting evidence, contradictory findings, gaps, limitations, references.
**Deterministic:** stats computation, citation formatting, section assembly. **LLM:** narrative summaries, gap narratives.

---

## 9. Research Coordinator

- Manage agent execution order (1→2→3→4→5; per-paper parallelism inside Agent 2).
- Pass structured data between agents via investigation-isolated SQLite.
- Track execution status per task (`processing_history`) within transactions.
- Handle failures: retry (configurable), mark failed, continue other papers, allow restart from checkpoint.
- Prevent duplicate processing (unique constraints, idempotent `task_key`s).
- Maintain investigation history.
- Support restarting interrupted workflows (resume from last completed stage, §2).
- Expose progress events to frontend (polling).

---

## 10. Communication Contracts (summary)

| From → To | Via | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| Coordinator → Agent 1 | SQLite task queue | investigation_id, search params, max_papers |
| Agent 1 → Coordinator | SQLite (txn) | paper rows, access_status |
| Coordinator → Agent 2 | SQLite task queue | paper_id, full_text_path |
| Agent 2 → Coordinator | SQLite (txn) | entities, synonyms, mentions, candidate relationships (with source passages + hashes) |
| Agent 2 → Agent 3 | SQLite | relationships + source passages |
| Agent 3 → Agent 4 | SQLite | evidence matrix, contradiction pairs |
| Agent 4 → Agent 5 | SQLite | research gaps (deterministic scores) |
| Agent 5 → Coordinator | SQLite (txn) | report artifacts |
| All → Coordinator | processing_history (txn) | status, timestamps, errors, checkpoint_state |

---

## 11. Dashboard Views (clarification 9)
The React dashboard implements 12 views:

| # | View | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Home dashboard | Overview of investigations, recent activity, quick-start entry point |
| 2 | New research investigation | Create an investigation; input research question, disease/drug/gene, date range, max papers, publication types, full-text preference |
| 3 | Literature search results | Browse retrieved paper metadata from discovery (PMID/DOI/title/authors/abstract/date, access status) |
| 4 | Paper library | All papers for an investigation with access_status; mark open_access / abstract_only / paywalled / unavailable |
| 5 | Paper detail and evidence viewer | Full text, sections, persistent chunks, and evidence passages with page/section provenance |
| 6 | Biomedical entity explorer | Entities by type (drug/protein/gene/disease/pathway/concept), stable identifiers, synonyms, original text |
| 7 | Drug-target relationship explorer | Relationships by type, confidence, direct-vs-association, negation/uncertainty/speculation/context flags, source passages |
| 8 | Interactive knowledge graph | NetworkX/Plotly graph (drug/protein/gene/disease nodes, typed edges, evidence references); node/edge inspection |
| 9 | Research gap analysis | Ranked candidate gaps with deterministic scores, reasoning, literature coverage, limitations |
| 10 | Report generation | Assemble and export report (JSON/CSV/PDF via ReportLab) with citations |
| 11 | Investigation history | Status, processing_history, retries, checkpoints; restart interrupted investigations |
| 12 | Application settings | Configuration: model (OLLAMA_MODEL), GPU/CPU mode, data dir (DDS_DATA_DIR), max papers per investigation |

**Version:** 1.1 (planning, revised)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written  
**Planned location:** `/home/user/docs/DATA_PIPELINE.md`

---

## 1. Pipeline Stages (end-to-end)

```
[1] Ingestion & Query
    User creates investigation → coordinator → Agent 1
[2] Literature Discovery
    Agent 1: keywords → PubMed + Europe PMC → metadata → deduplicate (per investigation) → store (Papers, investigation-scoped)
[3] Paper Acquisition
    Download open-access full text (PDF); user PDF/TXT import;
    isolated PDF parsing (ARCHITECTURE §6.3); validate magic bytes + size; mark access_status; store under data/papers/
[4] Document Processing & Chunking
    Agent 2: PyMuPDF text extraction → section detection (abstract/intro/methods/results/conclusion)
    → persist chunks to paper_chunks (clarification 6) with page/section refs → handle errors (corrupt PDF → flag, continue)
[5] Biomedical NER & Normalisation
    SciSpaCy NER → entities (drug/protein/gene/disease/pathway/concept)
    → stable identifiers + synonym normalisation → preserve original text
    → store Entities + Entity Synonyms + Paper Entity Mentions (anchored to paper_chunks)
[6] Relationship Extraction
    Deterministic context flags + LLM → candidate relationships (type, direct-vs-association,
    negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental context, confidence)
    → EVERY relationship carries an exact, verifiable source passage + source_passage_hash
    → store Relationships + Evidence (investigation-scoped)
[7] Evidence Analysis
    Agent 3: verbatim passage verification (source_passage_hash) → compare across papers → contradictions
    (explicit mapping, clarification 7) → evidence matrix
[8] Research Analytics
    Agent 4: coverage → deterministic, explainable gap ranking (clarification 8; Python, LLM outside score)
    → store Research Gaps; NetworkX knowledge graph (nodes/edges/evidence refs)
[9] Reporting
    Agent 5: consolidate → JSON/CSV/PDF (ReportLab) report with citations + limitations
[10] Export & UI
    Frontend browses investigation-scoped data; downloads JSON/CSV/PDF; Plotly graph visualisation
```

---

## 2. Stage Details

### Stage 1–2: Ingestion & Discovery
- Query builder: disease + drug + gene + date range + publication types → Boolean/MeSH queries for PubMed E-utilities + Europe PMC.
- Rate-limit respect (PubMed: 3 req/sec without key; Europe PMC limits).
- Deduplication key: PMID > DOI > normalized title, scoped per investigation (same PMID/DOI allowed across investigations).
- Store: PMID, DOI, title, authors, abstract, publication_date, source, retrieved_at, access_status. Max 100 papers per investigation (configurable).

### Stage 3: Acquisition
- Open-access full-text via Europe PMC `fullTextUrl` / PubMed Central OA; respect `access_status`.
- User imports: validate file (PDF magic `%PDF`, TXT), size cap, scan for embedded JS/scripts; isolated subprocess parsing with timeout and resource limits; store outside web root.
- Paywalled: mark `paywalled`, do NOT bypass; user may upload manually.

### Stage 4: Processing & Chunking (clarification 6)
- PyMuPDF extract text per page (isolated subprocess, timeout, resource limits); detect sections via headings; preserve page numbers.
- Persistent chunks stored in `paper_chunks`: chunk_text, chunk_order, page_start/page_end, token_count, linked to `paper_sections` and `paper_id`.
- Chunk size target ~512–1024 tokens with overlap; each chunk carries paper_id, section_id, page range.
- Errors logged per paper; pipeline continues.

### Stage 5–6: NLP & Relationships
- SciSpaCy models (`en_ner_bc5cdr_md` chemicals/diseases, `en_ner_bionlp13cg_md` genes/proteins — see MODEL_SELECTION.md).
- Stable identifiers + synonym normalisation (best-effort NCBI Gene/UniProt/DrugBank); store original + normalized.
- Relationship extraction: deterministic detection of negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental context; LLM classifies type + direct/interaction flag + confidence + supporting span; deterministic post-validation (span exists verbatim in source text).
- **Verifiable source passage:** every relationship stores `source_passage` (exact text) and `source_passage_hash` (SHA-256) so a reviewer can locate and confirm the passage.

### Stage 7: Evidence Analysis
- For each relationship, verify supporting span verbatim in source passage (hash check).
- Contradiction: same source→target entity pair → explicit mapping (clarification 7); both supporting and contradicting rows kept; context-divergent pairs flagged separately.
- Evidence type heuristic: section keywords (methods/results → experimental; discussion → review; clinical trial terms → clinical).

### Stage 8: Analytics
- NetworkX graph: nodes = entities (typed), edges = relationships (typed, weighted by confidence/frequency).
- Gap ranking_score: deterministic formula documented in `ranking_criteria` (JSON of inputs/weights); LLM writes description only, never invents score.
- Trend: relationship counts bucketed by publication year.

### Stage 9–10: Reporting & Export
- JSON: nested, full provenance.
- CSV: flat relationships + evidence.
- PDF: server-side ReportLab, citations, limitations.

---

## 3. Memory & Performance Bounds
- Stream PDFs; never load full corpus into RAM.
- Per-paper processing; FAISS index per-investigation (optional, discardable).
- Progress per paper → UI responsive.
- Single LLM at a time via Ollama.

---

## 4. Failure & Recovery
- Failed download → retry (exponential backoff), then mark failed, continue.
- Corrupt PDF → extraction_failed flag, continue.
- Interrupted workflow → coordinator resumes from last completed stage (processing_history checkpoints; §2 AGENT_SPECIFICATION).
- Duplicate prevention → unique constraints + idempotent task_keys.
- All multi-stage writes scoped to investigation_id within SQLite transactions.

---

## 5. Outputs per Investigation (investigation-scoped)
- Papers collection + metadata
- Persistent chunks (paper_chunks) linked to sections and mentions
- Entities + synonyms + mentions
- Relationships + evidence (with contradictions; verifiable source passages)
- Knowledge graph (NetworkX → Plotly for frontend)
- Research gaps (ranked, deterministic score, reasoning/coverage/limitations)
- Report (JSON/CSV/PDF)

1. **Unit tests** (Pytest): query builder, deduplication (per investigation), section detection, chunking, gap ranking score (deterministic, clarification 8), contradiction mapping (clarification 7), negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental-context flags, export formatting, SQLite transaction handling, investigation isolation (composite foreign keys), idempotent task_keys, checkpoint/resume logic.
2. **Integration tests** (Pytest): agent ↔ SQLite (transactions, isolation), PubMed/Europe PMC clients (mocked + recorded fixtures), Ollama client, isolated PDF parsing (timeout/resource limits), ReportLab PDF export.
3. **Scientific evaluation** (manual annotated dataset): NER precision/recall/F1; relationship extraction precision/recall/F1; evidence source attribution; supporting-passage accuracy (verbatim span + hash verification); citation correctness; contradiction identification accuracy (per explicit mapping).
4. **System evaluation:** download reliability, PDF processing, agent coordination, failure recovery, memory consumption, CPU/GPU inference, cross-platform (Arch ↔ Windows).
5. **Frontend tests:** component rendering, navigation, graph interaction, export triggers (frontend testing library).
6. **Model benchmark test (gate):** VRAM, load time, tokens/sec on target hardware — measured, not invented; result is a gate before production relationship extraction (MODEL_SELECTION §4).

---

## 2. Scientific Evaluation Dataset
- Manually annotated abstracts/full-texts with gold-standard entities and relationships. Size and source determined by project owner (initially 50–100 papers, SRS_ANALYSIS §4 item 3).
- Source: PubMed open-access papers, annotated by the project owner.
- Used to compute measured NER/RE precision, recall, F1 — **no accuracy claims without these results**. Model benchmarking results also must be measured before production use (MODEL_SELECTION §4).

---

## 3. Acceptance Criteria per Milestone

| Milestone | Acceptance Criteria |
|---|---|
| M0 Architecture | Schema finalised (investigation isolation, composite FKs, chunks); model candidates shortlisted (Qwen2.5-1.5B, Llama-3.2-1B); interfaces defined; risks logged |
| M1 Foundation | Repo builds on Arch + Windows; FastAPI health endpoint; SQLite init + migrations + transactions + isolation run; logging works; React dev server starts |
| M2 Literature Acquisition | PubMed + Europe PMC search returns metadata; deduplication per investigation works; same PMID/DOI allowed across investigations; open-access download succeeds for sample; paywalled identified not bypassed; PDF/TXT import validated; max 100 papers enforced |
| M3 Scientific NLP | PDF extraction (isolated subprocess, timeout, limits) preserves sections/pages; persistent chunks stored; SciSpaCy NER runs on CPU; relationships extracted with negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental-context flags; **every relationship has a verifiable source passage + hash**; deterministic baseline on annotated subset |
| M4 Evidence Analysis | Evidence rows carry full provenance (paper, section, page, method, timestamp); contradictions preserved both sides per explicit mapping; evidence matrix queryable; passage-span verification works |
| M5 Multi-Agent | Coordinator runs 5 agents in order (LangGraph + fallback); durable task/checkpoint storage; failed agent retries; interrupted investigation resumes without duplicating completed work; investigation isolation; processing_history complete within transactions |

- *Depends on:* M3 (candidate models available); *blocks:* M5 production relationship extraction.

- *Depends on:* M2, M3, M4, Model Benchmark Milestone.

# Database Design — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.1 (planning, revised)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written  
**Planned location:** `/home/user/docs/DATABASE_DESIGN.md`  
**Consistent with:** SRS.md §7, SRS_ANALYSIS.md §2.6, ARCHITECTURE.md, AGENT_SPECIFICATION.md, DATA_PIPELINE.md, TEST_RESULTS.md  
**Executable DDL:** `docs/schema.sql` (validated; see TEST_RESULTS.md)

---

## 1. Design Principles

- **SQLite** — single local relational DB, file-based, portable, no server.
- **Investigation-level isolation enforced at the schema level:** every core entity carries `investigation_id` NOT NULL; composite foreign keys guarantee relationships, mentions, evidence, and gap references can never cross investigations. Isolation is a database constraint, not merely an application-query assumption.
- **Same PMID/DOI allowed in different investigations:** uniqueness of PMID/DOI is scoped per investigation (`UNIQUE(pmid, investigation_id)`, `UNIQUE(doi, investigation_id)` via partial indexes). A paper may be retrieved under multiple investigations.
- **Reliable transaction handling:** multi-statement writes wrapped in explicit transactions; `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` and `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` on every connection.
- **Fully normalised** to ≥3NF; junction tables for many-to-many.
- **Provenance-first:** every extracted fact links to paper, section, page/chunk, extraction method, timestamp, confidence.
- **Contradiction-safe:** relationships and evidence are never soft-deleted or overwritten to "pick a winner"; contradictory rows coexist.
- **Cross-platform:** relative, configurable paths; no machine-specific absolute paths.
- **Migratable:** versioned SQL migration files applied at startup within a transaction.

---

## 2. Entity-Relationship Summary

```
investigation 1:N paper
investigation 1:N paper_section (via paper)
investigation 1:N paper_chunk (via paper)
investigation 1:N entity
investigation 1:N entity_synonym (via entity)
investigation 1:N paper_entity_mention (via paper and entity)
investigation 1:N relationship (via source and target entities)
investigation 1:N evidence (via relationship and paper)
investigation 1:N research_gap
investigation 1:N gap_supporting_evidence (via gap and evidence)
investigation 1:N processing_history
```

Composite foreign key rule: every child table references its parent through `(parent_id, investigation_id)`. Because each parent's primary key makes `(id, investigation_id)` unique, SQLite composite foreign keys are valid and enforce isolation at storage time.

# Agent Specification — Drug Discovery Literature Mining System

**Version:** 1.1 (planning, revised)  
**Status:** Planning phase — no application code written  
**Planned location:** `/home/user/docs/AGENT_SPECIFICATION.md`  
**Consistent with:** SRS.md §6, SRS_ANALYSIS.md §2.5, ARCHITECTURE.md, DATABASE_DESIGN.md, DATA_PIPELINE.md, TESTING_STRATEGY.md

---

## 1. Orchestration Model

- **Research Coordinator** (LangGraph primary, lightweight Python state-machine fallback): owns investigation lifecycle, agent sequencing, state, retries, checkpoints, duplicate prevention, history, restart. All state and outputs scoped to `investigation_id` (investigation-level isolation enforced at the SQLite schema level, per DATABASE_DESIGN.md).
- **Agents communicate via shared SQLite**, not direct calls. Each agent reads inputs from DB, writes outputs to DB within a transaction, records `processing_history`.
- **One shared local LLM** (Ollama) across agents, specialised prompts per agent; deterministic Python post-processing where possible.
- **Deterministic-first:** section detection, deduplication, negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental-context flags, coverage counts, conflict detection and gap ranking scores computed in Python where sufficient; LLM used only for disambiguation and narrative descriptions. Avoid unnecessary LLM calls/agents.

---

## 2. Durable Workflow Recovery

### Persistent task and checkpoint storage
Recovery is driven by a **custom SQLite task/checkpoint schema** (`processing_history`, DATABASE_DESIGN §3), which is the source of truth. LangGraph may be used for orchestration, but recovery does not depend on LangGraph checkpointing.

Each task row stores:
- `task_key` — idempotency key, e.g. `agent1:discover:{investigation_id}` or `agent2:process:{paper_id}`. Guarantees a logical unit of work is processed at most once per investigation (unique per investigation via `idx_processing_history_task_key`).
- `status` — queued/running/completed/failed/skipped.
- `inputs` — JSON task inputs.
- `outputs` — JSON task outputs.
- `checkpoint_state` — JSON resumable checkpoint state (e.g., papers already processed, next page cursor, last completed chunk).
- `retry_count` / `max_retries` — retry budget.
- `started_at` / `completed_at` / `execution_time_seconds` — timing.
- `error_details` — JSON error info for failed tasks.

### Resume without duplicating completed work
On investigation restart or after an interruption:
1. Query `processing_history` for all tasks of the `investigation_id`.
2. Tasks with `status='completed'` are **skipped** (idempotent; outputs already persisted).
3. Tasks with `status='failed'` and `retry_count < max_retries` are retried.
4. Tasks with `status='failed'` and `retry_count >= max_retries` are marked `skipped` and the investigation continues with remaining work.
5. Stale `status='running'` tasks (interrupted mid-execution) are reset to `queued` and re-run from their checkpoint state.
6. Tasks with `status='queued'` are run in order.

Because every agent writes outputs to SQLite within a transaction scoped to `investigation_id`, resuming never duplicates completed relationships, mentions, evidence, or gaps. Composite foreign keys further guarantee no cross-investigation contamination.

---

## 3. State Schema (coordinator)

`{ investigation_id, status, current_agent, papers[], entities[], relationships[], evidence[], gaps[], errors[], retry_counts, checkpoints, max_papers }` — all keyed by `investigation_id`. Checkpoints persisted to `processing_history.checkpoint_state`.

---

## 4. Agent 1 — Literature Discovery

**Inputs:** investigation research question + search parameters (disease, drug, gene, date range, max_papers ≤ 100 configurable, publication types, full-text preference).
**Responsibilities:** interpret query; generate search keywords (Boolean, MeSH-aware); call PubMed E-utilities + Europe PMC REST; retrieve metadata (PMID, DOI, title, authors, abstract, date); deduplicate by PMID/DOI/normalized title (deduplication scoped per investigation — same PMID may appear in different investigations); store source DB + retrieval date; mark access_status (open_access/abstract_only/paywalled/unavailable).
**Outputs:** paper metadata rows scoped to investigation_id.
**Deterministic:** query construction, deduplication, metadata normalisation. **LLM:** keyword generation from research question (optional; can be rule-based).
**Failure:** API rate limits → backoff/retry; one DB down → use the other; empty result → flag to user.

---

## 5. Agent 2 — Biomedical Extraction

**Inputs:** paper list from Agent 1; full-text paths (open-access downloads + user imports).
**Responsibilities:** extract PDF/TXT text (PyMuPDF, isolated subprocess per ARCHITECTURE §6.3); preserve sections (abstract/intro/methods/results/conclusion); persist chunks to `paper_chunks` (clarification 6) with page/section references; chunk text with page/section refs; NER (SciSpaCy) for drugs, proteins, genes, diseases, pathways; stable biomedical identifiers + synonym normalisation (store original + normalized); identify candidate relationships.
**Relationship extraction (required detection):**
- relationship type: inhibits/activates/binds_to/regulates/upregulates/downregulates/associated_with/other
- negation (e.g., "does not inhibit")
- uncertainty (e.g., "may", "suggests", "could")
- speculation (e.g., "potential", "hypothesized")
- experimental context (in vitro / in vivo / animal / cell line / clinical / unknown)
**Every relationship must carry an exact, verifiable source passage** (verbatim span from source text) + `source_passage_hash` (SHA-256) for verification. Association ≠ direct interaction (`is_direct_interaction` flag).
**Outputs:** entities, entity_synonyms, entity mentions, candidate relationships scoped to investigation_id.
**Deterministic:** PDF extraction, chunking, section detection, SciSpaCy NER, normalisation lookup, context-flag heuristics. **LLM:** relationship-type disambiguation, direct-vs-association, confidence-scoring assistance.
**Security:** paper text treated as untrusted; prompt-injection mitigations; size/time limits on extraction; isolated PDF parsing.
**Failure:** corrupted PDF → extraction_failed flag, continue; abstract-only papers → NER from abstract only, flagged.

---

## 6. Agent 3 — Evidence Analysis

**Inputs:** candidate relationships + source passages from Agent 2.
**Responsibilities:** cross-check candidate evidence against source passages (verbatim span verification via `source_passage_hash`); compare findings across publications; identify contradictory findings using the **predicate-specific contradiction mapping** (clarification 7); categorise evidence types (experimental/computational/review/clinical); preserve uncertainty (low confidence, conflicting).
**Outputs:** evidence matrix scoped to investigation_id (provenance, confidence, type).
**Deterministic:** passage-span verification, contradiction detection (per mapping below), evidence categorisation heuristics. **LLM:** passage-relationship validation, confidence scoring.
**Contradiction handling:** both supporting and contradicting rows stored; no silent selection of one conclusion.

### Predicate-specific contradiction mapping (clarification 7)

Two relationships for the same `(source_entity, target_entity)` pair are evaluated using **predicate-specific opposites**, not broad positive/negative grouping.

**Opposite predicate pairs** (only these are treated as potential contradictions):
| Predicate A | Opposite Predicate B |
|---|---|
| activates | inhibits |
| upregulates | downregulates |
| binds_to | (no opposite — `binds_to` vs `inhibits` is NOT automatically contradictory) |

**Negation reverses assertion polarity:** a negated relationship (`negation = 1`) flips its predicate to the opposite for contradiction purposes. E.g., "Drug X does not inhibit Protein Y" is treated as an assertion of `activates`/`upregulates` polarity for contradiction comparison.

**Contradiction decision (same source→target pair):**
1. Determine each relationship's **effective polarity** = (predicate mapped to positive/negative/neutral) XOR (negation flag).
   - Positive: activates, upregulates
   - Negative: inhibits, downregulates
   - Neutral/other: binds_to, regulates, associated_with, other
2. The pair is **contradictory** ONLY when one relationship has effective positive polarity and the other has effective negative polarity (per the opposite-predicate table above).
3. `binds_to` vs `inhibits`: **compatible**, not contradictory (binding does not preclude inhibition).
4. Negation: "does not inhibit" → effective positive; "does not activate" → effective negative.
5. Experimental context comparison: if both relationships have explicit, differing contexts (e.g., `in_vitro` vs `clinical`), the pair is **context-divergent** (not contradictory). If contexts match or at least one is `unknown`, the contradiction/context-divergent classification stands on polarity alone.
6. If polarity is not opposite (e.g., both positive, both negative, or either neutral), the pair is **compatible**.

**Classification outcomes:** `contradictory` / `compatible` / `context-divergent`.

### Concrete examples

| # | Relationship A | Relationship B | Classification | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Drug X **inhibits** Protein Y (in_vitro) | Drug X **activates** Protein Y (in_vitro) | **Contradictory** | Opposite predicates (inhibits vs activates), same context |
| 2 | Drug X **binds_to** Protein Y | Drug X **inhibits** Protein Y | **Compatible** | binds_to has no opposite; binding ≠ activation |
| 3 | Drug X **inhibits** Protein Y (in_vitro) | Drug X **inhibits** Protein Y (clinical) | **Context-divergent** | Same polarity, differing explicit contexts |
| 4 | Drug X **does not inhibit** Protein Y | Drug X **activates** Protein Y | **Compatible** | Negation reverses "inhibits" → positive polarity; matches "activates" |
| 5 | Drug X **upregulates** Gene Z | Drug X **downregulates** Gene Z | **Contradictory** | Opposite predicates (upregulates vs downregulates) |
| 6 | Drug X **regulates** Protein Y | Drug X **inhibits** Protein Y | **Compatible** | regulates is neutral; not an opposite pair |

### Unit tests (contradiction detection)

| Test | Relationship A | Relationship B | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| CT-1 | inhibits / not negated / in_vitro | activates / not negated / in_vitro | contradictory |
| CT-2 | inhibits / not negated / in_vitro | activates / not negated / clinical | context-divergent |
| CT-3 | binds_to / not negated / unknown | inhibits / not negated / unknown | compatible |
| CT-4 | inhibits / negated=1 / unknown | activates / not negated / unknown | compatible (negation flips inhibits → positive) |
| CT-5 | upregulates / not negated / unknown | downregulates / not negated / unknown | contradictory |
| CT-6 | regulates / not negated / unknown | inhibits / not negated / unknown | compatible |
| CT-7 | associated_with / not negated / unknown | inhibits / not negated / unknown | compatible |
| CT-8 | inhibits / not negated / in_vivo | inhibits / not negated / in_vivo | compatible |

---

## 7. Agent 4 — Research Gap

**Inputs:** aggregated relationships + evidence matrix from Agent 3.
**Responsibilities:** analyse literature coverage per drug-target-disease; identify underexplored relationships; detect conflicting results (per contradiction mapping); identify evidence limitations; rank candidate gaps using transparent, deterministic criteria.

### Candidate combination generation
Candidate gaps are generated over **(drug, target, disease) triples** derived from extracted relationships:
- A candidate triple exists when at least one relationship in the investigation has a drug-typed source/target, a protein/gene-typed source/target, and a disease-typed entity associated (via co-occurrence in the same paper or via the disease context of the investigation).
- `paper_count` = number of distinct papers reporting at least one relationship for that triple.
- A triple with `paper_count = 0` can still be a candidate if its constituent entities co-occur in collected papers but no relationship between them was extracted; in that case `coverage_score = 1.0` (maximum gap).
- Triples with no entities at all are not candidates.

### Deterministic research-gap scoring formula (clarification 8)

The `ranking_score` (0.0–1.0) is computed **entirely in Python**; the LLM is completely outside score calculation. The LLM writes `gap_description` and `supporting_reasoning` only, and never invents or adjusts `ranking_score`.

```
ranking_score = clamp(0.0, 1.0,
    w_coverage * coverage_score
  + w_conflict * conflict_score
  + w_evidence * evidence_score
  + w_recency  * recency_score
)
```

Weights (documented, sum to 1.0): `w_coverage = 0.40`, `w_conflict = 0.30`, `w_evidence = 0.20`, `w_recency = 0.10`.

**Input normalization (each component scaled to 0.0–1.0):**

1. `coverage_score = 1.0 - min(paper_count, coverage_cap) / coverage_cap`, `coverage_cap = 20`.
   - Fewer papers on a drug-target-disease pair → higher gap score.
   - `paper_count = 0` → `coverage_score = 1.0`. `paper_count >= 20` → `coverage_score = 0.0`.

2. `conflict_score = 1.0` if at least one contradictory pair (per §6 mapping) exists for the relationship, else `0.0`.

3. `evidence_score = 1.0 - avg_confidence`, where `avg_confidence` = mean of `confidence_score` across relationships for the triple.
   - Missing confidence (`NULL`) → treated as `0.5` (neutral), so `evidence_score = 0.5`.
   - No relationships / empty evidence → `avg_confidence = 0.5`, `evidence_score = 0.5`.

4. `recency_score` — **stale literature increases the gap score; recent literature decreases it.**
   - `years_since = current_year - max(publication_date)` across papers for the triple (most recent paper).
   - `recency_score = clamp(0.0, 1.0, years_since / recency_cap)`, `recency_cap = 5`.
   - Recent literature (years_since ≈ 0) → `recency_score ≈ 0.0` → lower gap score (area is actively studied).
   - Stale literature (years_since >= 5) → `recency_score = 1.0` → higher gap score (area may be underexplored recently).
   - Missing publication dates for all papers in a triple → `recency_score = 0.5` (neutral).

`clamp(x, lo, hi) = max(lo, min(hi, x))` guarantees every normalized input and the final `ranking_score` remains in [0.0, 1.0].

`ranking_criteria` (stored as JSON) documents the exact inputs, weights, caps, and clamps used so the score is reproducible and explainable. Each gap also carries `literature_coverage`, `limitations`, and `supporting_reasoning`. Gaps are corpus-relative: absence in collected papers ≠ proof of no global research.

**Outputs:** research gaps scoped to investigation_id, each with gap_category, ranking_score, ranking_criteria (JSON), literature_coverage, limitations, supporting_reasoning, gap_supporting_evidence references.

---

## 8. Agent 5 — Research Report

**Inputs:** all prior agent outputs for an investigation.
**Responsibilities:** consolidate findings; generate structured summaries; prepare report with citations; include limitations + confidence info.
**Outputs:** final report (JSON/CSV/PDF via ReportLab).
**Contents:** research question, search methodology, literature stats, identified drugs, proteins/genes, relationships, supporting evidence, contradictory findings, gaps, limitations, references.
**Deterministic:** stats computation, citation formatting, section assembly. **LLM:** narrative summaries, gap narratives.

---

## 9. Research Coordinator

- Manage agent execution order (1→2→3→4→5; per-paper parallelism inside Agent 2).
- Pass structured data between agents via investigation-isolated SQLite.
- Track execution status per task (`processing_history`) within transactions.
- Handle failures: retry (configurable), mark failed, continue other papers, allow restart from checkpoint.
- Prevent duplicate processing (unique constraints, idempotent `task_key`s).
- Maintain investigation history.
- Support restarting interrupted workflows (resume from last completed stage, §2).
- Expose progress events to frontend (polling).

---

## 10. Communication Contracts (summary)

| From → To | Via | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| Coordinator → Agent 1 | SQLite task queue | investigation_id, search params, max_papers |
| Agent 1 → Coordinator | SQLite (txn) | paper rows, access_status |

| Agent 2 → Coordinator | SQLite (txn) | entities, synonyms, mentions, candidate relationships (with source passages + hashes) |

| Agent 5 → Coordinator | SQLite (txn) | report artifacts |
| All → Coordinator | processing_history (txn) | status, timestamps, errors, checkpoint_state |

---

## 11. Dashboard Views (clarification 9)
The React dashboard implements 12 views:

| # | View | Purpose |

| 1 | Home dashboard | Overview of investigations, recent activity, quick-start entry point |

[10] Export & UI

```

## 2. Stage Details

### Stage 1–2: Ingestion & Discovery
- Query builder: disease + drug + gene + date range + publication types → Boolean/MeSH queries for PubMed E-utilities + Europe PMC.
- Rate-limit respect (PubMed: 3 req/sec without key; Europe PMC limits).
- Deduplication key: PMID > DOI > normalized title, scoped per investigation (same PMID/DOI allowed across investigations).
- Store: PMID, DOI, title, authors, abstract, publication_date, source, retrieved_at, access_status. Max 100 papers per investigation (configurable).

### Stage 3: Acquisition
- Open-access full-text via Europe PMC `fullTextUrl` / PubMed Central OA; respect `access_status`.
- User imports: validate file (PDF magic `%PDF`, TXT), size cap, scan for embedded JS/scripts; isolated subprocess parsing with timeout and resource limits; store outside web root.
- Paywalled: mark `paywalled`, do NOT bypass; user may upload manually.

### Stage 4: Processing & Chunking (clarification 6)
- PyMuPDF extract text per page (isolated subprocess, timeout, resource limits); detect sections via headings; preserve page numbers.
- Persistent chunks stored in `paper_chunks`: chunk_text, chunk_order, page_start/page_end, token_count, linked to `paper_sections` and `paper_id`.
- Chunk size target ~512–1024 tokens with overlap; each chunk carries paper_id, section_id, page range.
- Errors logged per paper; pipeline continues.

### Stage 5–6: NLP & Relationships
- SciSpaCy models (`en_ner_bc5cdr_md` chemicals/diseases, `en_ner_bionlp13cg_md` genes/proteins — see MODEL_SELECTION.md).
- Stable identifiers + synonym normalisation (best-effort NCBI Gene/UniProt/DrugBank); store original + normalized.
- Relationship extraction: deterministic detection of negation/uncertainty/speculation/experimental context; LLM classifies type + direct/interaction flag + confidence + supporting span; deterministic post-validation (span exists verbatim in source text).
- **Verifiable source passage:** every relationship stores `source_passage` (exact text) and `source_passage_hash` (SHA-256) so a reviewer can locate and confirm the passage.

### Stage 7: Evidence Analysis (clarification 7)
- For each relationship, verify supporting span verbatim in source passage (hash check).
- Contradiction: same source→target entity pair → **predicate-specific mapping**:
  - Opposite predicate pairs only: activates↔inhibits, upregulates↔downregulates.
  - `binds_to` has no opposite; `binds_to` vs `inhibits` is compatible, not contradictory.
  - Negation reverses assertion polarity.
  - Differing explicit experimental contexts → context-divergent (not contradictory).
- Both supporting and contradicting rows kept; context-divergent pairs flagged separately.
- Evidence type heuristic: section keywords (methods/results → experimental; discussion → review; clinical trial terms → clinical).

### Stage 8: Analytics
- NetworkX graph: nodes = entities (typed), edges = relationships (typed, weighted by confidence/frequency).
- Gap ranking_score: deterministic formula documented in `ranking_criteria` (JSON of inputs/weights); LLM writes description only, never invents score.
- Trend: relationship counts bucketed by publication year.

### Stage 9–10: Reporting & Export
- JSON: nested, full provenance.
- CSV: flat relationships + evidence.
- PDF: server-side ReportLab, citations, limitations.

---

## 3. Memory & Performance Bounds
- Stream PDFs; never load full corpus into RAM.
- Per-paper processing; FAISS index per-investigation (optional, discardable).
- Progress per paper → UI responsive.
- Single LLM at a time via Ollama.

---

## 4. Failure & Recovery
- Failed download → retry (exponential backoff), then mark failed, continue.
- Corrupt PDF → extraction_failed flag, continue.
- Interrupted workflow → coordinator resumes from last completed stage (processing_history checkpoints; AGENT_SPECIFICATION §2).
- Duplicate prevention → unique constraints + idempotent task_keys.
- All multi-stage writes scoped to investigation_id within SQLite transactions.

---

## 5. Outputs per Investigation (investigation-scoped)
- Papers collection + metadata
- Persistent chunks (paper_chunks) linked to sections and mentions
- Entities + synonyms + mentions
- Relationships + evidence (with contradictions; verifiable source passages)
- Knowledge graph (NetworkX → Plotly for frontend)
- Research gaps (ranked, deterministic score, reasoning/coverage/limitations)
- Report (JSON/CSV/PDF)

|---|---|---|---|
| CT-1 | inhibits / not negated / in_vitro | activates / not negated / in_vitro | contradictory |
| CT-2 | inhibits / not negated / in_vitro | activates / not negated / clinical | context-divergent |
| CT-3 | binds_to / not negated / unknown | inhibits / not negated / unknown | compatible |
| CT-4 | inhibits / negated=1 / unknown | activates / not negated / unknown | compatible |
| CT-5 | upregulates / not negated / unknown | downregulates / not negated / unknown | contradictory |
| CT-6 | regulates / not negated / unknown | inhibits / not negated / unknown | compatible |
| CT-7 | associated_with / not negated / unknown | inhibits / not negated / unknown | compatible |
| CT-8 | inhibits / not negated / in_vivo | inhibits / not negated / in_vivo | compatible |

**Version:** 1.1 (planning, revised)  
**Project Type:** Final-Year B.Tech IT Project  
**Status:** Planning phase — analysis of the Software Requirements Specification (SRS.md, version 1.0)
